After a word in the third case, in the senses of 'done' and so forth, the suffix `ṇika` occurs. What is done by the body is `kāyikaṃ` (bodily); by speech, `vācasikaṃ` (verbal); by mind, `mānasikaṃ` (mental). An illness caused by wind is `vātiko` (wind-related). What is bought for a hundred is `sātikaṃ`; for a thousand, `sāhassikaṃ`. The form `devadatena kītaṃ` does not occur because that meaning is not understood. Bound by a thong is `vārattiko`; also `āyasiko` (bound by iron), `pāsiko` (bound by a snare). Prepared or mixed with ghee is `ghātikaṃ`; also `goḷikaṃ` (with jaggery), `dādhikaṃ` (with curds), `māricikaṃ` (with pepper). One killed by a net, or one who kills with a net, is `jāliko`; also `bālīsiko` (one who kills with a hook). Won by dice is `akkhikaṃ`; also `sālākikaṃ` (won by sticks). One who wins or gambles with dice is `akkhiko`. One who digs with a digging tool is `khāṇittiko`; also `kuddāliko` (one who digs with a spade). The forms `devadatena jitaṃ` (won by Devadatta) and `aṅgulyā khaṇatīti` (digs with a finger) do not occur because that meaning is not understood. One who crosses by a raft is `oḷumpiko`; `uḷumpiko` is with `ika`, as are `gopucchiko` and `nāviko`. One who travels by cart is `sākaṭiko`; `rathiko` and `parappiko` are with `ika`. One who carries on the shoulder is `khandhiko`; also `aṃsiko`. `Sīsiko` is with `ika`. One who lives by wages is `vetaniko`; `bhatiko`, `kayiko`, `vikkayiko`, and `kayavikkayiko` are with `ika`.

30. Tassa saṃvattati.

30. It conduces to that.

Catutthiyantā saṃvattatīti asmiṃ atthe ṇiko hoti, punabbhavāya saṃvattatīti ponobhaviko, itthiyaṃ pono bhavikā, lokāya saṃvattatīti lokiko suṭṭhu aggoti saggo, saggāya saṃvattatīti sovaggiko, sassovaka tadaminādipāṭhā, dhanāya saṃvattatīti dhaññaṃ, yo.

After a word in the fourth case, in the sense of 'it conduces to', the suffix `ṇika` occurs. What conduces to rebirth is `ponobhaviko`; in the feminine, `ponobhavikā`. What conduces to the world is `lokiko`. That which is exceedingly excellent is `saggo` (heaven); what conduces to heaven is `sovaggiko`. There are also variant readings. What conduces to wealth is `dhaññaṃ`; the suffix is `ya`.

31. Tato sambhūtamāgataṃ.

31. Originated from that, or come from that.

Pañcamyantā sambhūtamāgatanti etesvatthesu ṇiko hoti, mātiko sambhūtamāgataṃ vā mattikaṃ, pettikaṃ, ṇyariyaṇa -yāpi dissanti, surabhito sambhūtaṃ sorabhyaṃ, thanato sambhūtaṃ thaññaṃ, pitito sambhūto pettiyo, mātiyo, mattiyo, macco vā.

After a word in the fifth case, in the senses of 'originated from' or 'come from', the suffix `ṇika` occurs. What originated from or has come from the mother is `mattikaṃ`; from the father, `pettikaṃ`. The suffixes `ṇya`, `riya`, and `ṇa` are also seen. What originated from fragrance is `sorabhyaṃ`; from the breast is `thaññaṃ`. One originated from the father is `pettiyo`; from the mother, `mātiyo`, `mattiyo`, or `macco`.

32. Tattha vasati vidito bhatto niyutto.

32. He dwells there, is known there, is supported there, is appointed there.

Sattamyantā tattha vasatītvevamādīsvatthesu ṇiko hoti. Rukkhamūle vasatīti rukkhamūliko, āraññiko, sosāniko. Loke vidito lokiko. Catumahārājesu bhattā cātummahārājikā[M 0.0153]. Dvāre niyutto dovāriko dassoka tadaminādipāṭhā, bhaṇḍāgāriko, iko-navakammiko, kiyojātikiyo, andhakiyo.

After a word in the seventh case, in such senses as 'dwells there', the suffix `ṇika` occurs. One who dwells at the foot of a tree is `rukkhamūliko`; also `āraññiko`, `sosāniko`. One known in the world is `lokiko`. One supported in the realm of the Four Great Kings is `cātummahārājikā`. One appointed at the gate is `dovāriko`. There are also variant readings. Also `bhaṇḍāgāriko`. With the suffix `ika`: `navakammiko`. Also `kiyojātikiyo`, `andhakiyo`.

33. Tassidaṃ.

33. This is his.

Chaṭṭhiyantā idamiccasmiṃ atthe ṇiko hoti, saṅghassa idaṃ saṅghikaṃ, puggalikaṃ, sakyaputtiko, nātiputtiko, jenadattiko, kiye-sakiyo, parakiyo, niye-attaniyaṃ, ke- sako rājakaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ.

After a word in the sixth case, in the sense of 'this is his', the suffix `ṇika` occurs. This of the Saṅgha is `saṅghikaṃ`; also `puggalikaṃ`. Also `sakyaputtiko`, `ñātiputtiko`, `jinadattiko`. With `kiya`: `sakiyo`, `parakiyo`. With `niya`: `attaniyaṃ`. With `ka`: `sako`, `rājakaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ`.

34. Ṇo.

34. The suffix `ṇa`.

Chaṭṭhiyantā idamiccasmiṃ atthe ṇo hoti, kaccāyanassa idaṃ kaccāyanaṃ byākaraṇaṃ, sogataṃ sāsanaṃ, māhisaṃ maṃsādi.

After a word in the sixth case, in the sense of 'this is his', the suffix `ṇa` occurs. This of Kaccāyana is `kaccāyanaṃ byākaraṇaṃ` (Kaccāyana's grammar); `sogataṃ sāsanaṃ` (the Sugata's teaching); `māhisaṃ maṃsādi` (buffalo meat, etc.).

35. Gavādīhi yo.

35. After `go` and so forth, the suffix `ya`.

Gavādīhi chaṭṭhiyantehi idamiccasmiṃ atthe yo hoti, gunnaṃ idaṃ gabyaṃ maṃsādi, kabyaṃ, dabbaṃ.

After `go` and so forth in the sixth case, in the sense of 'this is his', the suffix `ya` occurs. This of cows is `gabyaṃ maṃsādi` (cow's meat, etc.); also `kabyaṃ`, `dabbaṃ`.

36. Pitito bhātari reyyaṇa.

36. From 'father', in the sense of 'brother', the suffix `eyya`.

Pitusaddā tassa bhātari reyyaṇa hoti, pitu bhātā petteyyo.

After the word `pitu`, in the sense of 'his brother', the suffix `eyya` occurs. The father's brother is `petteyyo`.

37. Mātito ca bhaginiyaṃ cho.

37. And from 'mother', in the sense of 'sister', the suffix `cha`.

Mātito pitito ca tesaṃ bhaginiyaṃ cho hoti, mātu bhaginī mātucchā, pitu bhaginī pitucchā, kathaṃ ‘mātulo’ti “mātulāditvānī”ti nipātanā.

From `mātu` and `pitu`, in the sense of their sister, the suffix `cha` occurs. The mother's sister is `mātucchā`; the father's sister is `pitucchā`. How is `mātulo` formed? By irregular formation, according to the rule on `mātula`, etc.

38. Mātāpitūsvāmaho.

38. In the sense of 'mother' and 'father', the suffix `āmaha`.

Mātāpitūhi [M 0.0154] tesaṃ mātāpitūsu āmaho hoti, mātu mātā mātāmahī, mātu pitā mātāmaho, pitu mātā pitāmahī, pitu pitā pitāmaho, na yathāsaṅkhyaṃ, paccekābhi sambandhā.

After `mātā` and `pitu`, in the sense of their mothers and fathers, the suffix `āmaha` occurs. The mother's mother is `mātāmahī`; the mother's father is `mātāmaho`. The father's mother is `pitāmahī`; the father's father is `pitāmaho`. This is not in respective order, due to individual connection.

39. Hite reyyaṇa.

39. In the sense of 'beneficial to', the suffix `eyya`.

Mātāpitūhi hite reyyaṇa hoti, matteyyo, petteyyo.

After `mātā` and `pitu`, in the sense of 'beneficial to', the suffix `eyya` occurs: `matteyyo`, `petteyyo`.

40. Nindāññātappapaṭibhāgarassadayāsaññāsu ko.

40. In the senses of censure, unknown, small, likeness, short, compassion, and designation, the suffix `ka`.

Nindādīsvattheyu nāmasmā ko hoti, nindāyaṃ-muṇḍako, samaṇako. Aññāte-kassāyaṃ assoti assako, payogasāmatthiyā sambandhivisesānavagamovagamyate. Appatthetelakaṃ, ghatakaṃ. Paṭibhāgatthe-hatthī viya hatthiko, assako, balībaddako. Rasse-mānusako, rukkhako, pilakkhako. Dayāyaṃ-puttako, vacchako. Saññāyaṃ-moro viya morako.

In the senses of censure and so forth, the suffix `ka` occurs after a noun. In censure: `muṇḍako`, `samaṇako`. In the sense of 'unknown': 'Whose horse is this?' becomes `assako`. By the force of usage, the non-understanding of a specific relation is understood. In the sense of 'small': `telakaṃ`, `ghatakaṃ`. In the sense of 'likeness': like an elephant, `hatthiko`; also `assako`, `balībaddako`. In the sense of 'short': `mānusako`, `rukkhako`, `pilakkhako`. In compassion: `puttako`, `vacchako`. In designation: like a peacock, `morako`.

41. Tamassaparimāṇaṃ ṇiko ca.

41. And the suffix `ṇika` in the sense of 'that is its measure'.

Paṭhamantā asseti asmiṃ atthe ṇiko hoti ko ca tañce paṭhamantaṃ parimāṇaṃ bhavati, parimīyate neneti parimāṇaṃ, doṇo parimāṇamassa doṇiko vīhi, khārasatiko, khārasahassiko āsītiko vayo, upaḍḍhakāyikaṃ bimbohanaṃ, pañcakaṃ, chakkaṃ.

After a word ending in the first case, in the sense of 'that is its measure', the suffixes 'ṇika' and 'ka' occur, if that word ending in the first case is a measure. A measure is that by which something is measured. A 'doṇa' is its measure, hence 'doṇiko vīhi' (rice measured by a doṇa). Also 'khārasatiko' (a hundred loads), 'khārasahassiko' (a thousand loads), 'āsītiko vayo' (eighty years of age), 'upaḍḍhakāyikaṃ bimbohanaṃ' (a cushion of half a body's length), 'pañcakaṃ' (a group of five), 'chakkaṃ' (a group of six).

42. Yatetehi ttako.

42. After 'ya', 'ta', and 'eta', the suffix 'ttaka' occurs.

Yādīhi [M 0.0155] paṭhamantehī asseti chaṭṭhiyatthe ttako hoti, tañce paṭhamantaṃ parimāṇaṃ bhavati, yaṃ parimāṇamassa yattakaṃ, tattakaṃ, ettakaṃ, āvatake yāvatako, tāvatako (etāvatako).

After words such as 'ya' ending in the first case, in the sense of the sixth case ('that is its measure'), the suffix 'ttaka' occurs, if that word ending in the first case is a measure. 'yaṃ parimāṇamassa' (whatever measure it has) becomes 'yattakaṃ' (as much as); also 'tattakaṃ' (that much), 'ettakaṃ' (this much). In the sense of quantity: 'yāvatako' (as much as), 'tāvatako' (so much), 'etāvatako' (this much).

43. Sabbā cāvantu.

43. And after 'sabba', the suffix 'āvantu' occurs.

Sabbato paṭhamantehi yādīhi ca asseti chaṭṭhiyatthe āvantu hoti, tañce paṭhamantaṃ parimāṇaṃ bhavati. Sabbaṃ parimāṇamassa sabbāvantaṃ, yāvantaṃ, tāvantaṃ, etāvantaṃ.

After 'sabba' and words such as 'ya' ending in the first case, in the sense of the sixth case ('that is its measure'), the suffix 'āvantu' occurs, if that word ending in the first case is a measure. 'sabbaṃ parimāṇamassa' (its measure is all) becomes 'sabbāvantaṃ' (all-encompassing); also 'yāvantaṃ' (as much as), 'tāvantaṃ' (so much), 'etāvantaṃ' (this much).

44. Kimhā ratirīvarīvatakarittakā.

44. After 'kiṃ', the suffixes 'rati', 'rīva', 'rīvataka', and 'rittaka' occur.

Kimhā paṭhamantā asseti chaṭṭhiyatthe ratirīvarīvatakarittakā honti, tañce paṭhamantaṃ parimāṇaṃ bhavati, kiṃ saṅkhyānaṃ parimāṇamesaṃ kati ete, kīva, kīvatakaṃ, kittakaṃ. Rīvanto sabhāvato asaṅkhyo.

After 'kiṃ' ending in the first case, in the sense of the sixth case ('that is its measure'), the suffixes 'rati', 'rīva', 'rīvataka', and 'rittaka' occur, if that word ending in the first case is a measure. 'kiṃ saṅkhyānaṃ parimāṇamesaṃ' (what is the measure of their number?) becomes 'kati ete' (how many are these?); also 'kīva' (how much?), 'kīvatakaṃ' (how much?), 'kittakaṃ' (how much?). The suffix 'rīva' by its nature indicates 'countless'.

45. Sañjātaṃ tārakāditvito.

45. After 'tārakā' and similar words, the suffix 'ita' occurs in the sense of 'arisen'.

Tārakādīhi paṭhamantehi asseti chaṭṭhiyatthe ito hoti, te ce sañjātā honti, tārakā sañjātā assa tārakitaṃ gaganaṃ, pupphito rukkho, pallavitā latā.

After 'tārakā' and similar words ending in the first case, the suffix 'ita' occurs in the sense of the sixth case ('in which it has arisen'), if they have arisen. 'tārakā sañjātā assa' (stars have arisen in it) becomes 'tārakitaṃ gaganaṃ' (a starry sky). Also 'pupphito rukkho' (a blossoming tree), 'pallavitā latā' (a sprouting creeper).

46. Māne matto.

46. The suffix 'matta' occurs in the sense of 'measure'.

Paṭhamantā mānavuttito asseti asmiṃatthe matto hoti, palaṃ ummānamassa palamattaṃ, hattho pamāṇamassa hatthamattaṃ [M 0.0156] sataṃ mānamassa satamattaṃ, doṇo parimāṇamassa doṇamattaṃ, abhedopacārā doṇotipi hoti.

After a word ending in the first case that denotes a measure, the suffix 'matta' occurs in the sense of 'that is its measure'. 'palaṃ ummānamassa' (a 'pala' is its weight) becomes 'palamattaṃ' (a pala's worth). 'hattho pamāṇamassa' (a hand is its length) becomes 'hatthamattaṃ' (a hand's length). 'sataṃ mānamassa' (a hundred is its quantity) becomes 'satamattaṃ' (a hundred's worth). 'doṇo parimāṇamassa' (a 'doṇa' is its capacity) becomes 'doṇamattaṃ' (a doṇa's worth). Through the figurative use of non-distinction, it is also simply 'doṇo'.

47. Taggho cuddhaṃ.

47. And the suffix 'taggha' occurs in the sense of 'up to'.

Uddhamānavuttiho asseti chaṭṭhiyatthe taggho hoti matto ca, jaṇṇutagghaṃ, jaṇṇumattaṃ.

After a word denoting a measure upwards, in the sense of the sixth case ('that is its measure'), the suffixes 'taggha' and 'matta' occur. Thus 'jaṇṇutagghaṃ' (up to the knee), 'jaṇṇumattaṃ' (as much as the knee).

48. Ṇo ca purisā.

48. And after 'purisa', the suffix 'ṇa' occurs.

Purisā paṭhamantā uddhamānavuttito ṇo hoti mattādayo ca, porisaṃ, purisamattaṃ, purisatagghaṃ.

After 'purisa' ending in the first case, in the sense of a measure upwards, the suffix 'ṇa' occurs, as well as 'matta' and others. Thus 'porisaṃ' (a man's height), 'purisamattaṃ' (as much as a man), 'purisatagghaṃ' (up to a man's height).

49. Ayūbhadvitīhaṃse.

49. After 'ubha', 'dvi', and 'ti', in the sense of a part, [the suffix 'aya' occurs].

Ubhadvitīhi avayavavuttīti paṭhamantehi asseti chaṭṭhiyatthe ayo hoti. Ubho aṃsā assa ubhayaṃ, dvayaṃ, tayaṃ.

After 'ubha', 'dvi', and 'ti' denoting a part, from these words ending in the first case, the suffix 'aya' occurs in the sense of the sixth case ('that has'). For example: 'ubho aṃsā assa' (it has two parts) becomes 'ubhayaṃ' (a pair); also 'dvayaṃ' (a dyad), 'tayaṃ' (a triad).

50. Saṅkhyāya saccutīsāsadasantāyādhikāsmiṃ savasahasse ḍo.

50. After a number ending in 'sat', 'uti', 'īsa', 'āsa', or 'dasa', in the sense of 'more than' with respect to a hundred or a thousand, the suffix 'ḍa' occurs.

Satyantāya utyantāya īsantāya āsantāya dasantāya ca saṅkhyāya paṭhamantāya asminti sattamyatthe ḍo hoti, sā ce saṅkhyā adhikā hoti, yadasminti tañce sataṃ sahassaṃ satasahassaṃ vā hoti, vīsati adhikā asmiṃ sateti vīsaṃ sataṃ, ekavīsaṃ sataṃ, sahassaṃ, satasahassaṃ vā, tiṃsaṃ sataṃ, ekatiṃsaṃ sataṃ. Utyantāya-navutaṃ sataṃ sahassaṃ satasahassaṃ vā. Īsantāya cattālīsaṃ sataṃ, sahassaṃ, satasahassaṃ vā. Āsantāya [M 0.0157] paññāsaṃ sataṃ, sahassaṃ, satasahassaṃ vā. Dasantāyaekādasaṃ sataṃ, sahassaṃ, satasahassaṃ vā. Saccutīsāsadasantāyāti kiṃ? Chādhikā asmiṃsate. Adhiketi kiṃ? Pañcadasahīnā asmiṃsate, asminti kiṃ? Vīsatyadhikā etasmā satā, satasahasseti kiṃ? Ekādasa adhikā assaṃ vīsatiyaṃ.

After a number ending in 'sat', 'uti', 'īsa', 'āsa', or 'dasa', from that word ending in the first case, the suffix 'ḍa' occurs in the locative sense of 'asmiṃ' (in this), if that number is 'more', and if that 'in which' is a hundred, a thousand, or a hundred thousand. For example: 'vīsati adhikā asmiṃ sate' (twenty more than this hundred) becomes 'vīsaṃ sataṃ'; also 'ekavīsaṃ sataṃ', 'sahassaṃ', or 'satasahassaṃ'; 'tiṃsaṃ sataṃ', 'ekatiṃsaṃ sataṃ'. For a number ending in 'uti': 'navutaṃ sataṃ', 'sahassaṃ', or 'satasahassaṃ'. For one ending in 'īsa': 'cattālīsaṃ sataṃ', 'sahassaṃ', or 'satasahassaṃ'. For one ending in 'āsa': 'paññāsaṃ sataṃ', 'sahassaṃ', or 'satasahassaṃ'. For one ending in 'dasa': 'ekādasaṃ sataṃ', 'sahassaṃ', or 'satasahassaṃ'. Why [the condition] 'ending in sat, uti, īsa, āsa, or dasa'? To exclude cases like 'chādhikā asmiṃ sate' (six more than this hundred). Why [the condition] 'adhikā' (more)? To exclude cases like 'pañcadasahīnā asmiṃ sate' (fifteen less than this hundred). Why [the condition] 'asmiṃ' (in this)? To exclude cases like 'vīsatyadhikā etasmā satā' (twenty more than that hundred). Why [the condition] 'hundred, thousand, or hundred thousand'? To exclude cases like 'ekādasa adhikā assaṃ vīsatiyaṃ' (eleven more than twenty).

51. Tassa pūraṇekādasādito vā.

51. Optionally, after numbers from eleven onwards, [the suffix 'ḍa' occurs] in the sense of 'its ordinal'.

Chaṭṭhiyanthāyekādasādikāya saṅkhyāya ḍo hoti (tassa) pūraṇatthe vibhāsā, sā saṅkhyā pūrīyate yena taṃ pūraṇaṃ, ekādasannaṃ pūraṇo ekādaso. Ekādasamo, vīso, vīsatimo, tiṃso, tiṃsatimo, cattālīso, paññāso.

After a number from eleven onwards ending in the sixth case, the suffix 'ḍa' is optionally applied in the sense of 'its ordinal'. That by which a number is completed is an ordinal. The ordinal of eleven is 'ekādaso'. Examples include 'ekādasamo', 'vīso', 'vīsatimo', 'tiṃso', 'tiṃsatimo', 'cattālīso', 'paññāso'.

52. Ma pañcādikatihi.

52. The suffix 'ma' is applied after numbers from five onwards and after 'kati'.

Chaṭṭhiyantāya pañcādikāya saṅkhyāya katismā ca mo hoti (tassa) pūraṇatthe, pañcamo, sattamo, aṭṭhamo, katimo, katimī.

After numbers from five onwards ending in the sixth case, and after 'kati', the suffix 'ma' is applied in the sense of 'its ordinal'. Examples: 'pañcamo' (fifth), 'sattamo' (seventh), 'aṭṭhamo' (eighth), 'katimo' (which number, masculine), 'katimī' (which number, feminine).

53. Satādīnamica. Satādikāya saṅkhyāya chaṭṭhiyantāya (tassa) pūraṇatthe mohoti satādīnamicāntādeso, satimo, sahassimo.

53. And for 'sata' and similar words, 'ima' [is the suffix]. After numbers such as 'sata' ending in the sixth case, the suffix 'ma' occurs in the sense of 'its ordinal', and 'i' is substituted for the final vowel of the base. Examples: 'satimo' (hundredth), 'sahassimo' (thousandth).

54. Chā ṭṭhaṭṭhamā.

54. After 'cha', the suffixes 'ṭṭha' and 'ṭṭhama' occur.

Chasaddā ṭṭhaṭṭhamā honti tassa pūraṇatthe, chaṭṭho, chaṭṭhamo, itthiyaṃ chaṭṭhī, chaṭṭhamī, kathaṃ ‘dutiyaṃ catuttha’nti? “Dutiyassa, catuttha tatiyāna”nti nipātanā.

From the word 'cha', the suffixes 'ṭṭha' and 'ṭṭhama' are formed in the sense of its ordinal. Examples: 'chaṭṭho' (sixth, masculine), 'chaṭṭhamo' (sixth, masculine); in the feminine: 'chaṭṭhī', 'chaṭṭhamī'. How then are forms like 'dutiya' and 'catuttha' formed? By irregular formation, as stated in the rule 'dutiya, tatiya, and catuttha are irregular'.

55. Ekā kākyasahāye.

55. After 'eka', [the suffixes 'ka' and 'ākī' occur] in the sense of 'without a companion'.

Ekasmā [M 0.0158] asahāyatthe kaākī honti vā, ekako, ekākī, eko.

After 'eka', in the sense of 'without a companion', the suffixes 'ka' and 'ākī' are optionally applied. Examples: 'ekako' (alone), 'ekākī' (solitary), 'eko' (one).

56. Vacchādīhi tanutte taro.

56. After 'vaccha' and similar words, the suffix 'tara' is applied in the sense of diminution.

Vacchādīnaṃ sabhāvassa tanutte gamyamāne taro hoti, susuttassa tanutte vacchataro, itthiyaṃ vacchatarī, yobbanassa tanutte okkhataro, assabhāvassa tanutte assataro, sāmatthiyassa tanutte usabhataro.

When the diminution of the nature of 'vaccha' and so on is understood, the suffix 'tara' is applied. For example: in the sense of a diminution of calf-ness, 'vacchataro' (a very young calf); in the feminine, 'vacchatarī' (a very young heifer). In the sense of a diminution of youth, 'okkhataro' (a young bull). In the sense of a diminution of the nature of a horse, 'assataro' (a mule). In the sense of a diminution of capability, 'usabhataro' (a young bull).

57. Kimhā niddhāraṇe ratara ratamā. Kiṃsaddā niddhāraṇe ratara ratamā honti, kataro bhavataṃ devadatto, kataro bhavataṃ kaṭho, katamo bhavataṃ devadatto, katamo bhavataṃ kaṭho, bhāradvājānaṃ katamosi brahme.

57. After 'kiṃ', in the sense of determination, the suffixes 'ratara' and 'ratamā' are applied. From the word 'kiṃ', in the sense of determination, the suffixes 'ratara' and 'ratamā' are applied. Examples: 'kataro bhavataṃ devadatto' (Which of you is Devadatta?), 'kataro bhavataṃ kaṭho' (Which of you is Kaṭha?), 'katamo bhavataṃ devadatto' (Which of you is Devadatta?), 'katamo bhavataṃ kaṭho' (Which of you is Kaṭha?), 'bhāradvājānaṃ katamosi brahme' (Among the Bhāradvājas, which one are you, O Brahmin?).

58. Tena datte liyā.

58. In the sense of 'given by that', the suffix 'liya' is applied.

Tatiyantā datte-bhidheyye laiyā honti, devena datto devalo, deviyo, brahmalo, brahmiyo, sivā sīvalo, sīviyo, sissa dīgho.

From words ending in the third case, in the sense of 'given', the suffix 'laiya' is applied. Examples: 'devena datto' (given by a god) becomes 'devalo' or 'deviyo'; from 'brahmunā datto' come 'brahmalo' and 'brahmiyo'; from 'sivena datto' (given by Siva) come 'sīvalo' and 'sīviyo'. The 'i' is lengthened.

59. Tassa bhāvakammesu ttatāttanaṇyaṇeyyaṇiyaṇiyā.

59. In the sense of its state or action, the suffixes 'tta', 'tā', 'ttana', 'ṇya', 'ṇeyya', 'ṇiya', and 'ṇiyā' are applied.

Chaṭṭhiyantā bhāve kamme ca ttādayo honti bahulaṃ, na ca sabbe sabbato honti aññatra ttatāhi, bhavanti etasmā buddhisaddābhi bhāvo saddassa pavattinimittaṃ, nīlassa paṭassa bhāvo nīlattaṃ [M 0.0159] nīlatābhi guṇo bhāvo, nīlassa guṇassa bhāvo nīlattaṃ nīlatābhi nīlaguṇajāti, gottaṃ gotāti gojāti, pācakattaṃ, daṇḍittaṃ, visāṇittaṃ, rājapurisattanti kriyādisambandhittaṃ, devadattattaṃ, candattaṃ, sūriyattanti tadavatthāvisesasāmaññaṃ, ākāsattaṃ, abhāvattanti upacaritabhedasāmaññaṃ. Ttana-puthujjanattanaṃ, vedanattanaṃ, jāyattanaṃ, jārattanaṃ. Ṇya-ālasyaṃ, brahmaññaṃ, cāpalyaṃ, nepuññaṃ, pesuññaṃ, rajjaṃ, ādhipaccaṃ, dāyajjaṃ, vesammaṃ ‘vesama’nti, keci, sakhyaṃ, vāṇijjaṃ. Ṇeyya-soceyyaṃ, ādhipateyyaṃ. Ṇagāravaṃ, pāṭavaṃ, ajjavaṃ, maddavaṃ. Iya-adhipatiyaṃ, paṇḍitiyaṃ, bahussutiyaṃ, naggiyaṃ, sūriyaṃ. Ṇiya-ālasiyaṃ, kāḷusiyaṃ, mandiyaṃdakkhiyaṃ, porohitiyaṃ, veyyattiyaṃ. Kathaṃ ‘rāmaṇīyaka’nti? Sakatthe kantā ṇena siddhaṃ. Kammaṃ kiriyā, tattha alasassa kammaṃ alasattaṃ’ alasatā, alasattanaṃ, ālasyaṃ, ālasiyaṃ vā, “sakatthe’ (4.122) ti sakatthepi, yathābhuccaṃ, kāruññaṃ, pattakallaṃ, ākāsānañcaṃ, kāyapāguññatā.

From words ending in the sixth case, in the sense of state and action, the suffixes 'tta' and so on are frequently applied, but not all are applied everywhere, except for 'tta' and 'tā'. From this, the state (bhāva) is the cause for the application of a word, as in 'buddhi' (intellect) and 'sadda' (sound). The state of a blue cloth ('nīlassa paṭassa bhāvo') is blueness ('nīlattaṃ', 'nīlatā'); the state is a quality. The state of the blue quality ('nīlassa guṇassa bhāvo') is blueness ('nīlattaṃ', 'nīlatā'), which is the class of the blue quality. The state of a cow ('go') is 'gottaṃ' (lineage), which is the species of cow ('gojāti'). The state of being a cook ('pācakattaṃ'), the state of having a staff ('daṇḍittaṃ'), the state of having horns ('visāṇittaṃ'), the state of being a king's man ('rājapurisattaṃ')—these are states connected with action, etc. The state of being Devadatta ('devadattattaṃ'), the state of being the moon ('candattaṃ'), the state of being the sun ('sūriyattaṃ')—these are the generalities of their specific conditions. The state of being space ('ākāsattaṃ'), the state of non-existence ('abhāvattaṃ')—these are generalities of metaphorical distinctions. With -ttana: 'puthujjanattanaṃ' (the state of being an ordinary person), 'vedanattanaṃ' (the state of feeling), 'jāyattanaṃ' (the state of being a wife), 'jārattanaṃ' (the state of being a paramour). With -ṇya: 'ālasyaṃ' (laziness), 'brahmaññaṃ' (Brahminhood), 'cāpalyaṃ' (fickleness), 'nepuññaṃ' (cleverness), 'pesuññaṃ' (slander), 'rajjaṃ' (kingship), 'ādhipaccaṃ' (lordship), 'dāyajjaṃ' (inheritance), 'vesammaṃ' (inequality)—some say 'vesama'—'sakhyaṃ' (friendship), 'vāṇijjaṃ' (trade). With -ṇeyya: 'soceyyaṃ' (purity), 'ādhipateyyaṃ' (sovereignty). With -ṇa: 'gāravaṃ' (respect), 'pāṭavaṃ' (skill), 'ajjavaṃ' (honesty), 'maddavaṃ' (gentleness). With -iya: 'adhipatiyaṃ' (lordship), 'paṇḍitiyaṃ' (wisdom), 'bahussutiyaṃ' (great learning), 'naggiyaṃ' (nakedness), 'sūriyaṃ' (heroism). With -ṇiya: 'ālasiyaṃ' (laziness), 'kāḷusiyaṃ' (blackness), 'mandiyaṃ' (slowness), 'dakkhiyaṃ' (skill), 'porohitiyaṃ' (the office of a family priest), 'veyyattiyaṃ' (eloquence). How is 'rāmaṇīyaka' (loveliness) formed? It is accomplished from 'kanta' with the suffix 'ṇa' in its own meaning. Action ('kammaṃ') is activity ('kiriyā'). In that sense, the action of a lazy person ('alasassa kammaṃ') is 'alasattaṃ', 'alasatā', 'alasattanaṃ', 'ālasyaṃ', or 'ālasiyaṃ'. According to the rule 'sakatthe' (4.122), suffixes are also applied in the word's own meaning, as is evident in: 'yathābhuccaṃ' (truthfulness), 'kāruññaṃ' (compassion), 'pattakallaṃ' (readiness), 'ākāsānañcaṃ' (infinity of space), 'kāyapāguññatā' (bodily agility).

60. Bya vaddhadāsā vā.

60. Optionally, the suffix 'bya' is applied to 'vaddha' and 'dāsa'.

Chaṭṭhiyantā vaddhā dāsā ca byo vā hoti bhāvakammesu, vaddhabyaṃ vaddhatā, dāsabyaṃ dāsatā, kathaṃ ‘vaddhava’nti? Ṇe vāgamo.

From 'vaddha' and 'dāsa' ending in the sixth case, the suffix 'bya' is optionally applied in the sense of state and action. Examples: 'vaddhabyaṃ' or 'vaddhatā' (old age); 'dāsabyaṃ' or 'dāsatā' (slavery). How is 'vaddhava' formed? There is an insertion of 'va' before the suffix 'ṇa'.

61. Naṇa yuvā bo ca vassa.

61. After 'yuvan', the suffix 'ṇaṇa' is applied, and 'bo' replaces 'va'.

Chaṭṭhiyantā yuvasaddā bhāvakammesu naṇa vā hoti tassa bo ca, yobbanaṃ, vātveva? Yuvattaṃ, yuvatā.

From the word 'yuvan' ending in the sixth case, in the sense of state and action, the suffix 'ṇaṇa' is optionally applied, and 'bo' replaces its 'va'. Example: 'yobbanaṃ' (youth). Is this optional? Yes: 'yuvattaṃ' (youth), 'yuvatā' (youth).

62. Aṇvāditvimo.

62. After 'aṇu' and so on, the suffix 'imo' is applied.

Aṇuādīhi [M 0.0160] chaṭṭhiyantehi bhāve vā imo hoti, aṇimā, laghimā, mahimā, (garimā), kasimā, vātveva? Aṇuttaṃ aṇutā.

From 'aṇu' and so on, ending in the sixth case, the suffix 'imo' is optionally applied in the sense of state. Examples: 'aṇimā' (minuteness), 'laghimā' (lightness), 'mahimā' (greatness), ('garimā' (heaviness)), 'kasimā' (thinness). Is this optional? Yes: 'aṇuttaṃ' (minuteness), 'aṇutā' (minuteness).

63. Bhāvā tena nibbatte.

63. From a state, in the sense of 'produced by that'.

Bhāvavācakā saddā tena nibbatte-bhidheyye imo hoti, pākena nibbatta pāṇimaṃ, sekimaṃ.

From words denoting a state, in the sense of 'produced by that', the suffix 'imo' is applied. Examples: 'pākena nibbatta' (produced by ripening) becomes 'pāṇimaṃ'; 'sekimaṃ' (moistness).

64. Taratamissikiyiṭṭhātisaye.

64. In the sense of excellence, the suffixes 'tara', 'tama', 'issika', 'iya', and 'iṭṭha' are applied.

Atisaye vattamānato hontete paccayā, atisayena pāpo pāpataro, pāpatamo, pāpissiko, pāpiyo, pāpiṭṭho, itthiyaṃ pāpatarā. Atisayantāpi atisayappaccayo, atisayena pāpiṭṭho pāpiṭṭhataro.

These suffixes are applied when a word expresses excellence. For example: 'atisayena pāpo' (exceedingly evil) becomes 'pāpataro' (more evil), 'pāpatamo' (most evil), 'pāpissiko' (very evil), 'pāpiyo' (worse), 'pāpiṭṭho' (worst); in the feminine, 'pāpatarā'. A suffix of excellence may also be applied to a word already expressing excellence: 'atisayena pāpiṭṭho' (exceedingly worst) becomes 'pāpiṭṭhataro' (even more the worst).

65. Tannissite llo.

65. In the sense of 'dependent on that', the suffix 'lla' is applied.

Dutiyantā llappaccayo hoti nissitatthe, vedaṃ nissitaṃ vedallaṃ, duṭṭhu nissitaṃ duṭṭhullaṃ. Ille-saṅkhārillaṃ.

From words ending in the second case, the suffix 'lla' is applied in the sense of 'dependent on'. Examples: 'vedaṃ nissitaṃ' (dependent on the Veda) becomes 'vedallaṃ'; 'duṭṭhu nissitaṃ' (dependent on evil) becomes 'duṭṭhullaṃ'. With 'illa': 'saṅkhārillaṃ' (dependent on formations).

66. Tassa vikārāvayavesu ṇa ṇika ṇeyyamayā.

66. In the sense of its modification or part, the suffixes 'ṇa', 'ṇika', 'ṇeyya', and 'maya' are applied.

Pakatiyā uttaramavatthantaraṃ vikāro, chaṭṭhiyantā nāmasmā vikāre-vayave ca ṇādayo honti bahulaṃ, ṇa-āyasaṃ bandhanaṃ, odumbaraṃ, paṇṇaṃ, odumbaraṃ bhasmaṃ, kāpotaṃ maṃsaṃ, kāpotaṃ satthi. Ṇika-kappāsikaṃ vatthaṃ. Ṇeyya-eṇeyyaṃ maṃsaṃ, eṇeyyaṃ satthi[M 0.0161]. Koseyyaṃ vatthaṃ. Maya-tiṇamayaṃ, dārumayaṃ, naḷamayaṃ, mattikāmayaṃ. “Aññasmi”nti (4.121) gunnaṃ karīsepi mayo, gomayaṃ.

A modification is a subsequent different state from the natural state. From nouns ending in the sixth case, in the sense of a modification or a part, the suffixes 'ṇa' and so on are frequently applied. With 'ṇa': 'āyasaṃ bandhanaṃ' (an iron bond), 'odumbaraṃ' (of fig wood), 'paṇṇaṃ' (of leaf), 'odumbaraṃ bhasmaṃ' (fig ash), 'kāpotaṃ maṃsaṃ' (pigeon meat), 'kāpotaṃ satthi' (pigeon thigh). With 'ṇika': 'kappāsikaṃ vatthaṃ' (cotton cloth). With 'ṇeyya': 'eṇeyyaṃ maṃsaṃ' (deer meat), 'eṇeyyaṃ satthi' (deer thigh); 'koseyyaṃ vatthaṃ' (silk cloth). With 'maya': 'tiṇamayaṃ' (made of grass), 'dārumayaṃ' (made of wood), 'naḷamayaṃ' (made of reed), 'mattikāmayaṃ' (made of clay). According to the rule 'Aññasmi' (4.121), 'maya' is also applied in the case of cow dung: 'gomayaṃ' (cow dung).

67. Jatuto saṇa vā.

67. From 'jatu' (lac), the suffix 'saṇa' is optionally applied.

Chaṭṭhiyantā nāmasmā jatuto vikārāvayavesu saṇa vā hoti. Jatuno vikāro jātusaṃ jatumayaṃ. “Lopo”ti (4.123) bahulaṃ paccayalopopi phalapupphamūlesu vikārāvayavesu, piyālassa phalāni piyālāni, mallikāya pupphāni mallikā, usirassa mūlaṃ usīraṃ, taṃ saddena vā tadabhidhānaṃ.

From the noun 'jatu' ending in the sixth case, the suffix 'saṇa' is optionally applied in the sense of modification or part. For example, a modification of lac ('jatuno vikāro') is 'jātusaṃ' or 'jatumayaṃ'. According to the rule 'Lopo' (4.123), elision of the suffix also frequently occurs for fruits, flowers, and roots in the sense of modification or part. Examples: 'piyālassa phalāni' (fruits of the piyal tree) becomes 'piyālāni'; 'mallikāya pupphāni' (flowers of the jasmine) becomes 'mallikā'; 'usirassa mūlaṃ' (root of the usira grass) becomes 'usīraṃ'. Or, that is designated by the word itself.

68. Samūhe kaṇa ṇa ṇikā.

68. In the sense of a collection, the suffixes 'kaṇa', 'ṇa', and 'ṇikā' are applied.

Chaṭṭhiyantā samūhe kaṇa ṇa ṇikā honti gottappaccayantā. Kaṇa-rājaññakaṃ, mānussakaṃ, ukkhādīhi-okkhakaṃ, oṭṭhakaṃ, orabbhakaṃ, rājakaṃ, rājaputtakaṃ, hatthikaṃ, dhenukaṃ. Ṇa-kākaṃ, bhikkhaṃ. Acittā ṇika-āpūpikaṃ, saṃkulikaṃ.

From words ending in the sixth case, the suffixes 'kaṇa', 'ṇa', and 'ṇikā' are applied in the sense of a collection, from those ending in a 'gotta' suffix. With 'kaṇa': 'rājaññakaṃ' (a group of warriors), 'mānussakaṃ' (a group of humans); from 'ukkhā' and so on: 'okkhakaṃ', 'oṭṭhakaṃ' (a herd of camels), 'orabbhakaṃ' (a flock of rams), 'rājakaṃ' (a group of kings), 'rājaputtakaṃ' (a group of princes), 'hatthikaṃ' (a herd of elephants), 'dhenukaṃ' (a herd of cows). With 'ṇa': 'kākaṃ' (a flock of crows), 'bhikkhaṃ' (a community of monks). From inanimate things, 'ṇika': 'āpūpikaṃ' (a collection of cakes), 'saṃkulikaṃ' (a collection of pastries).

69. Janādīhi tā.

69. From 'jana' and so on, the suffix 'tā' is applied.

Janādīhi chaṭṭhiyantehi samūhe tā hoti. Janatā, gajatā, bandhutā, gāmatā, sahāyatā, nāgaratā. Tāntā sabhāvato itthiliṅgā, ‘madanīya’nti karaṇe-dhikaraṇe vā anīyena siddhaṃ. ‘Dhūmāyitatta’nti ktāntā nāmadhātuto ktena siddhaṃ.

From 'jana' and so on, ending in the sixth case, the suffix 'tā' is applied in the sense of a collection. Examples: 'janatā' (a group of people), 'gajatā' (a herd of elephants), 'bandhutā' (a group of relatives), 'gāmatā' (a collection of villages), 'sahāyatā' (a group of friends), 'nāgaratā' (a body of citizens). Words ending in 'tā' are by nature feminine in gender. The word 'madanīya' is formed with the suffix 'anīya' in the sense of instrument or location. The word 'dhūmāyitatta' is formed from a denominative verb; its base, which ends in 'kta', is formed with the suffix 'kta'.

70. Iyo hite.

70. In the sense of 'beneficial', the suffix 'iya' is applied.

Chaṭṭhiyantā hite iyo hoti. Upādāniyaṃ, aññatrāpi samānodare sayito sodariyo.

From a word ending in the sixth case, the suffix 'iyo' is applied in the sense of 'beneficial'. Example: 'upādāniyaṃ' (related to clinging). Elsewhere also: 'sodariyo' (a brother), one who lies ('sayita') in the same womb ('samānodare').

71. Cakkhvādito sso.

71. From 'cakkhu' and so on, the suffix 'sso' is applied.

Chaṭṭhiyantehi [M 0.0162] cakkhuādīhi hite sso hoti, cakkhussaṃ, āyussaṃ.

From 'cakkhu' and so on, ending in the sixth case, the suffix 'sso' is applied in the sense of 'beneficial'. Examples: 'cakkhussaṃ' (beneficial for the eye), 'āyussaṃ' (beneficial for life).

72. Ṇyo tattha sādhu.

72. In the sense of 'suitable for that', the suffix 'ṇya' is applied.

Sattamyantā tattha sādhūti asmiṃ atthe ṇyo hoti. Sabbho, pārisajjo. Sādhūti kusalo yoggo hito vā. Aññatrāpi rathaṃ vahatīti racchā.

The suffix 'ṇyo' occurs after a word ending in the seventh case (locative) in the sense of 'apt for that'. (E.g.,) Sabbho (apt for an assembly), pārisajjo (apt for a council). 'Sādhu' means skilled, suitable, or beneficial. Even elsewhere, 'it carries a chariot' (rathaṃ vahatīti) becomes 'racchā' (road).

73. Kammā niya ññā.

73. The suffixes 'niya' and 'ññā' occur after 'kamma'.

Sattamyantā kammasaddā tattha sādhūbhi asmiṃ atthe niya ññā honti. Kamme sādhu kammaniyaṃ, kammaññaṃ.

The suffixes 'niya' and 'ññā' occur after the word 'kamma' ending in the seventh case (locative) in the sense of 'apt for that'. (E.g.,) Kammaniyaṃ (apt for action), kammaññaṃ (skilled in action).

74. Kathāditviko.

74. The suffix 'iko' occurs after 'kathā' (talk) and so on.

Kathādīhi sattamyantehi tattha sādhūti asmiṃ atthe iko hoti. Kathiko, dhammakathiko, saṅgāmiko pavāsiko, upavāsiko.

The suffix 'iko' occurs after words like 'kathā' (talk) ending in the seventh case (locative) in the sense of 'apt for that'. (E.g.,) Kathiko (storyteller), dhammakathiko (expounder of the Dhamma), saṅgāmiko (warrior), pavāsiko (traveler), upavāsiko (observer of the fast).

75. Pathādīhi ṇeyyo.

75. The suffix 'ṇeyya' occurs after 'patha' (path) and so on.

Pathādīhi sattamyantehi tattha sādhūti asmiṃ atthe ṇe-yyo hoti, pātheyyaṃ sāpateyyaṃ (ātitheyyaṃ).

The suffix 'ṇeyya' occurs after words like 'patha' (path) ending in the seventh case (locative) in the sense of 'apt for that'. (E.g.,) Pātheyyaṃ (provision for a journey), sāpateyyaṃ (property), (ātitheyyaṃ (hospitality)).

76. Dakkhiṇāyārahe.

76. After 'dakkhiṇā' (offering), in the sense of 'worthy'.

Dakkhiṇāsaddato arahatthe ṇeyyo hoti, dakkhiṇaṃ arahatīti dakkhiṇeyyo.

The suffix 'ṇeyya' occurs after the word 'dakkhiṇā' (offering) in the sense of 'worthy'. (Thus,) 'one who is worthy of an offering' (dakkhiṇaṃ arahatīti) is 'dakkhiṇeyyo'.

77. Rāyo tumantā.

77. The suffix 'rāya' occurs after words ending in 'tuma'.

Tumantato [M 0.0163] arahatthe rāyo hoti. Ghātetāyaṃ vā ghātetuṃ, jāpetāyaṃ vā jāpetuṃ, pabbājetāyaṃ vā pabbājetuṃ.

The suffix 'rāya' occurs after words ending in 'tuma' (infinitive) in the sense of 'worthy'. (E.g.,) Ghātetāyaṃ or ghātetuṃ (worthy to kill), jāpetāyaṃ or jāpetuṃ (worthy to cause to burn), pabbājetāyaṃ or pabbājetuṃ (worthy to banish).

78. Tametthassatthīti mantu.

78. The suffix 'mantu' occurs in the sense of 'he has that here'.

Paṭhamantā ettha assa atthīti etesvatthesu mantu hoti. Gāvo ettha dese, assa vā purisassa santīti gomā. Atthīti vattamānakālopādānato bhūtāhi bhavissantīhi vā gohi na gomā. Kathaṃ ‘gomā āsi, gomā bhavissatī’ti? Tadāpi vattamānāhiyeva gohi gomā, āsi bhavissatīti padantarā kālantaraṃ, itikaraṇato visayaniyamo –

The suffix 'mantu' occurs after words in the first case (nominative) in the sense of 'he has that here'. (E.g.,) 'Cows exist in this region, or a man possesses them,' thus 'gomā' (possessing cows). Because 'atthi' (is) refers to the present tense, 'gomā' does not apply to past or future cows. How then (can one say) 'he was gomā' or 'he will be gomā'? Even then, 'gomā' refers to cows existing presently; 'was' or 'will be' indicates a different time due to other words. Thus, the scope is determined by the usage.

Pahūte ca pasaṃsāyaṃ, nindāyañcātisāyane;

Niccayoge ca saṃsagge, hontime mantuādayo.

And in abundance, in praise, and in blame, and in excess, and in constant connection, and in association – these suffixes like 'mantu' occur.

Go assoti jātisaddānaṃ dabbābhidhānasāmatthiyā mantvādayo na honti, tathā guṇasaddānaṃ ‘seto paṭo’ti, yesantu guṇasaddānaṃ dabbābhidhānasāmatthiyaṃ natthi, tehi honteva ‘buddhimā, rūpavā, rasavā, gandhavā, phassavā, saddavā, rasī, rasiko, rūpī, rūpiko, gandhī, gandhiko’ti.

The suffixes like 'mantu' do not occur with class terms like 'go' (cow) and 'assa' (horse) because of their capacity to denote substances. Likewise with quality terms like 'seto paṭo' (white cloth). However, with those quality terms which do not have the capacity to denote substances, they do occur, (e.g.,) buddhimā (wise), rūpavā (beautiful), rasavā (flavorful), gandhavā (fragrant), phassavā (tangible), saddavā (melodious), rasī (tasteful), rasiko (connoisseur), rūpī (colorful), rūpiko (appreciator of color), gandhī (fragrant), gandhiko (appreciator of fragrance).

79. Vantvāvaṇṇā.

79. The suffix 'vantu' occurs after words that are not terms of censure.

Paṭhamantato avaṇṇantā mantvātthe vantu hoti. Sīlavā, paññavā, avaṇṇāti kiṃ? Satimā bandhumā.

The suffix 'vantu' occurs after words in the first case (nominative) that are not terms of censure, in the sense of 'possessing'. (E.g.,) Sīlavā (virtuous), paññavā (wise). Why the specification 'not a term of censure'? (Consider the forms) Satimā (mindful), bandhumā (having relatives).

80. Daṇḍāditvikaī vā.

80. The suffixes 'ika' and 'ī' optionally occur after 'daṇḍa' (stick) and so on.

Daṇḍādīhi [M 0.0164] ika ī honti vā mantvātthe. Bahulaṃ vidhānā kutoci dve honti, kutocekamekaṃva daṇḍiko daṇḍī daṇḍavā, gandhiko gandhī gandhavā, rūpiko rūpī rūpavā. (28) “Uttamīṇeva dhanā iko”, dhaniko, dhanī dhanavā añño. (29) “Asannihite atthā”, atthiko atthī, aññatra atthavā. (30) “Tadantā ca”, puññatthiko, puññatthī, (31) “vaṇṇantā īyeva” brahmavaṇṇī, devavaṇṇī, (32) “hatthadantehi jātiyaṃ”, hatthī, dantī, aññatra hatthavā dantavā. (33) “Vaṇṇato brahmacārimhi”, vaṇṇī brahmacārī, vaṇṇavā añño. (34) “Pokkharādito dese”, pokkharaṇī, uppalinī, kumudinī, bhisinī, muḷālinī, sālukinī, kvacādesepi padumipi paduminī paṇṇaṃ. Aññatra pokkharavā hatthī, (35) “nāvāyiko”, nāviko. (36) “Sukhadukkhā ī”, sukhī, dukkhī. (37) “Sikhādīhi vā”, sikhī, sikhāvā, mālī, mālāvā, sīlī, sīlavā, balī, balavā. (38) “Balā bāhūrupubbā ca”, bāhubalī, ūrubalī.

The suffixes 'ika' and 'ī' optionally occur after 'daṇḍa' (stick) and so on in the sense of 'possessing'. Due to the manifold application, sometimes two forms occur, sometimes only one: daṇḍiko, daṇḍī, daṇḍavā (one with a stick); gandhiko, gandhī, gandhavā (fragrant); rūpiko, rūpī, rūpavā (beautiful). (28) After 'dhana' (wealth), 'iko' occurs, especially in the sense of 'creditor': dhaniko (creditor); dhanī and dhanavā are other forms for 'wealthy'. (29) After 'attha' (purpose), 'ika' and 'ī' occur in the sense of 'being in need of': atthiko, atthī; elsewhere, atthavā. (30) And after words ending in that (-attha): puññatthiko, puññatthī. (31) After words ending in 'vaṇṇa' (color/appearance), only 'ī' occurs: brahmavaṇṇī, devavaṇṇī. (32) After 'hattha' (hand/trunk) and 'danta' (tooth/tusk) in the sense of species: hatthī (elephant), dantī (tusked elephant); elsewhere, hatthavā, dantavā. (33) After 'vaṇṇa' (color/appearance) when referring to a brahmacārī: vaṇṇī (a brahmacārī of a certain standing); vaṇṇavā is another (person). (34) After 'pokkhara' (lotus) and so on, in the sense of a place: pokkharaṇī (lotus pond), uppalinī (lily pond), kumudinī (water-lily pond), bhisinī (lotus-root pond), muḷālinī (lotus-stalk pond), sālukinī (lotus-root pond); sometimes, not in the sense of a place, padumī or paduminī means a lotus leaf. Elsewhere, pokkharavā (an elephant with lotus-like marks). (35) From 'nāvā' (boat), 'iko': nāviko (boatman). (36) After 'sukha' (happiness) and 'dukkha' (suffering), 'ī': sukhī (happy), dukkhī (suffering). (37) Optionally after words like 'sikhā' (crest): sikhī, sikhāvā; mālī, mālāvā; sīlī, sīlavā; balī, balavā. (38) And after 'bala' (strength) when preceded by 'bāhu' (arm) and 'ūru' (thigh): bāhubalī, ūrubalī.

81. Tapādīhi ssī. Tapādito mantvatthe vā ssī hoti. Tapassī, yasassī, tejassī, manassī, payassī. Vātveva? Yasavā.

81. The suffix 'ssī' occurs after 'tapa' (austerity) and so on. The suffix 'ssī' optionally occurs after 'tapa' and so on in the sense of 'possessing'. (E.g.,) Tapassī (one who has austerity), yasassī (one who has fame), tejassī (one who has splendor), manassī (one who has mind), payassī (one who has milk). The optionality is established by (forms such as) Yasavā.

82. Mukhādito ro. Mukhādīhi mantvatthero hoti. Mukharo, susiro, ūsaro, madhuro, kharo, kuñjaro, nagaraṃ, (39) “dantassu ca unnabhadante”, danturo.

82. The suffix 'ra' occurs after 'mukha' (mouth) and so on. The suffix 'ra' occurs after 'mukha' and so on in the sense of 'possessing'. (E.g.,) Mukharo (garrulous), susiro (hollow), ūsaro (barren), madhuro (sweet), kharo (harsh), kuñjaro (elephant), nagaraṃ (city). (39) And after 'danta' (tooth) when prominent, 'ura' (is added): danturo (toothy).

83. Tundyādīhi bho.

83. The suffix 'bha' occurs after 'tuṇḍi' and so on.

Tundiādīhi [M 0.0165] mantvatthe bho vā hoti. Tundibho, vaṭibho, valibho. Vātveva? Tundimā.

The suffix 'bha' optionally occurs after 'tuṇḍi' and so on in the sense of 'possessing'. (E.g.,) Tuṇḍibho (having a belly), vaṭibho (having a knot), valibho (having wrinkles). The optionality is established by (forms such as) Tuṇḍimā.

84. Saddhāditvā.

84. The suffix 'a' occurs after 'saddhā' (faith) and so on.

Saddhādīhi mantvatthea hoti vā. Saddho, pañño, itthiyaṃ saddhā. Vātveva? Paññavā.

The suffix 'a' optionally occurs after 'saddhā' (faith) and so on in the sense of 'possessing'. (E.g.,) Saddho (faithful), pañño (wise). In the feminine, saddhā (faithful woman). The optionality is established by (forms such as) Paññavā.

85. Ṇo tapā.

85. The suffix 'ṇa' occurs after 'tapas' (austerity).

Tapā ṇo hoti mantvatthe. Tāpaso, itthiyaṃ tāpasī.

The suffix 'ṇa' occurs after 'tapas' (austerity) in the sense of 'possessing'. (E.g.,) Tāpaso (an ascetic). In the feminine, tāpasī (a female ascetic).

86. Ālvabhijjhādīhi.

86. The suffix 'ālu' occurs after 'abhijjhā' (covetousness) and so on.

Abhijjhādīhi ālu hoti mantvatthe, abhijjhālu, sītālu, dhajālu, dayālu. Vātveva? Dayāvā.

The suffix 'ālu' occurs after 'abhijjhā' (covetousness) and so on in the sense of 'possessing'. (E.g.,) Abhijjhālu (covetous), sītālu (sensitive to cold), dhajālu (fond of flags), dayālu (compassionate). The optionality is established by (forms such as) Dayāvā.

87. Picchāditvilo.

87. The suffix 'ila' occurs after 'piccha' (slime) and so on.

Picchādīhi ilo hoti vā mantvatthe. Picchilo picchavā, phenilo phenavā, jaṭilo jaṭāvā. Kathaṃ ‘vācālo’ti? Nindāyamilassādilope “paro kvacī”ti (1-27).

The suffix `ila` optionally occurs after `piccha` and so on in the sense of 'possessing'. For example: `picchilo` or `picchavā` (slimy), `phenilo` or `phenavā` (frothy), `jaṭilo` or `jaṭāvā` (having matted hair). How is `vācālo` (talkative) formed? In the sense of censure, with the elision of the initial vowel of `ila`, according to the rule `paro kvaci` (1-27).

88. Sīlādito vo.

88. The suffix `va` occurs after `sīla` and so on.

Sīlādīhi vo hoti vā mantvatthe. Sīlavo sīlavā, kesavo kesavā, (40) “aṇṇā niccaṃ” aṇṇavo. (41) Gāṇḍī rājīhi saññāyaṃ” gāṇḍīvaṃ dhanu, rājīvaṃ paṅkajaṃ.

The suffix `va` optionally occurs after `sīla` and so on in the sense of 'possessing'. For example: `sīlavo` or `sīlavā` (virtuous), `kesavo` or `kesavā` (hairy). (40) After `aṇṇa` (water), it is always used: `aṇṇavo` (ocean). (41) After `gāṇḍī` and `rājī`, in the sense of a name: `gāṇḍīvaṃ` (a bow), `rājīvaṃ` (a lotus).

89. Māyā medhāhi vī.

89. The suffix `vī` occurs after `māyā` and `medhā`.

Etehi [M 0.0166] dvīhi vī hoti mantvatthe. Māyāvī, medhāvī.

The suffix `vī` occurs after these two words in the sense of 'possessing'. For example: `māyāvī` (deceptive), `medhāvī` (wise).

90. Sissare āmyuvāmī. Sasaddā āmyuvāmī honti issare-bhidhāyye mantvatthe. Samassatthīti sāmī, suvāmī.

90. After `sa`, in the sense of 'master', the suffixes `āmī` and `uvāmī` occur. After the word `sa`, the suffixes `āmī` and `uvāmī` occur in the sense of 'possessing' when denoting a master. For example: `sāmī` (master) is from `saṃ assa atthīti` (he has property); also `suvāmī`.

91. Lakkhyā ṇo a ca. Lakkhīsaddā ṇo hoti mantvatthe a cāntassa. Ṇakārovayavo, lakkhaṇo.

91. After `lakkhī`, the suffix `ṇa` occurs, and `a` replaces the final vowel. After the word `lakkhī`, the suffix `ṇa` occurs in the sense of 'possessing', and `a` replaces the final vowel of the base. The letter `ṇ` is a component of the suffix. For example: `lakkhaṇo`.

92. Aṅgā no kalyāṇe.

92. After `aṅga`, the suffix `na` occurs in the sense of 'beautiful'.

Kalyāṇe gamyamāne aṅgasmā no hoti mantvatthe. Aṅganā.

When 'beautiful' is understood, the suffix `na` occurs after `aṅga` in the sense of 'possessing'. For example: `aṅganā` (a beautiful woman).

93. So lomā.

93. After `loma`, the suffix `sa`.

Lomā so hoti mantvatthe. Lomaso, itthiyaṃ, lomasā.

The suffix `sa` occurs after `loma` in the sense of 'possessing'. For example: `lomaso`; in the feminine, `lomasā`.

94. Imiyā.

94. The suffixes `ima` and `iya`.

Mantvatthe ima iyā honti bahulaṃ. Puttimo, kittimo, puttiyo, kappiyo, jaṭiyo, hānabhāgiyo, seniyo.

In the sense of 'possessing', the suffixes `ima` and `iya` frequently occur. For example: `puttimo` (possessing a son), `kittimo` (possessing fame; artificial), `puttiyo` (possessing a son), `kappiyo` (suitable), `jaṭiyo` (possessing matted hair), `hānabhāgiyo` (liable to decrease), `seniyo` (belonging to an army).

95. To pañcamyā. Pañcamyantā bahulaṃ to hoti vā. Gāmato āgacchati gāmasmā āgacchati, corato bhāyati corehi bhāyati, satthato parihīno satthā parihīno.

95. The suffix `to` occurs after a word with a fifth case ending. After a word with a fifth case ending, the suffix `to` frequently occurs optionally. For example: `gāmato āgacchati` is equivalent to `gāmasmā āgacchati` (he comes from the village); `corato bhāyati` is equivalent to `corehi bhāyati` (he fears thieves); `satthato parihīno` is equivalent to `satthā parihīno` (deprived of a teacher).

96. Ito-tetto kuto.

96. The forms `ito`, `tetto`, and `kuto`.

Tomhi [M 0.0167] imassa ṭi nipaccate, etassa ṭa eta, kiṃsaddassa kuttañca. Ito imasmā, ato etto etasmā, kuto kasmā.

When the suffix `to` follows, for `ima`, `i` is irregularly substituted; for `eta`, `a` and `eta` are substituted; and for the word `kiṃ`, `ku` is substituted. Thus: `ito` from `imasmā`; `ato` and `etto` from `etasmā`; `kuto` from `kasmā`.

97. Abhyādīhi. Abhiādīhi to hoti. Abhito, parito, pacchato heṭṭhato.

97. After `abhi` and so on. The suffix `to` occurs after `abhi` and so on. For example: `abhito` (in front), `parito` (all around), `pacchato` (behind), `heṭṭhato` (below).

98. Ādyādīhi. Ādippabhutīhi to vā hoti, ādo ādito, majjhato antato, piṭṭhito, passato, mukhato, yatodakaṃ tadādittaṃ, yaṃ udakaṃ tadevādittanti attho.

98. After `ādi` and so on. The suffix `to` occurs optionally after `ādi` and so on. For example: `ādo` or `ādito` (from the start), `majjhato` (from the middle), `antato` (from the end), `piṭṭhito` (from behind), `passato` (from the side), `mukhato` (from the front). As in the sentence: `yatodakaṃ tadādittaṃ`, the meaning of which is, 'whatever water there is, that itself is ignited'.

99. Sabbādito sattamyā trattā. Sabbādīhi sattamyantehi tratthā vā honti. Sabbatra sabba. Sabbasmiṃ, yatra yattha yasmiṃ. Bahulādhikārā na tumhāmhehi.

99. After `sabba` and so on, in the seventh case, the suffixes `tra` and `ttha` occur. After `sabba` and similar words with a seventh case ending, the suffixes `tra` and `ttha` occur optionally. For example: `sabbatra` or `sabbattha` is equivalent to `sabbasmiṃ` (everywhere); `yatra` or `yattha` is equivalent to `yasmiṃ` (wherever). Due to the governing `bahulaṃ` rule, this does not apply to `tumha` and `amha`.

100. Katthettha kutrātra kvehidha.

100. `kattha`, `ettha`, `kutra`, `atra`, `kva`, `iha`, `idha`.

Etesaddā nipaccante. Kasmiṃ kattha, kutra, kva, etasmiṃ, ettha, atra, asmiṃ iha, idha.

These words are irregularly formed. Thus: from `kasmiṃ` are formed `kattha`, `kutra`, and `kva`; from `etasmiṃ` are formed `ettha` and `atra`; from `asmiṃ` are formed `iha` and `idha`.

101. Dhi sabbā vā. Sattamyantato sabbasmā dhi vā hoti. Sabbadhi, sabbattha.

101. After `sabba`, the suffix `dhi` occurs optionally. After `sabba` with a seventh case ending, the suffix `dhi` occurs optionally. For example: `sabbadhi`, which is equivalent to `sabbattha` (everywhere).

102. Yā hiṃ. Sattamyantato yato hiṃ vā hoti. Yahiṃ yatra.

102. After `ya`, the suffix `hiṃ` occurs. After `ya` with a seventh case ending, the suffix `hiṃ` occurs optionally. For example: `yahiṃ`, which is equivalent to `yatra` (where).

103. Tā haṃ ca.

103. After `ta`, `haṃ` also occurs.

Sattamyantato [M 0.0168] tato vā haṃ hoti hiṃ ca. Tahaṃ, tahiṃ, tatra.

After `ta` with a seventh case ending, `haṃ` occurs optionally, and `hiṃ` also. For example: `tahaṃ`, `tahiṃ`, or `tatra` (there).

104. Kuhiṃ kahaṃ.

104. The forms `kuhiṃ` and `kahaṃ`.

Kiṃsaddā sattamyantā hiṃ haṃ nipaccante kissa kukā ca. Kuhiṃ, kahaṃ. Kathaṃ ‘kuhiñcana’nti? ‘Canaṃ’ iti nipātantaraṃ ‘kuhiñcī’ti ettha cisaddo viya.

After the word `kiṃ` with a seventh case ending, the suffixes `hiṃ` and `haṃ` are irregularly added, and `ku` and `ka` are substituted for the base `kiṃ`. For example: `kuhiṃ` (where), `kahaṃ` (where). How is `kuhiñcana` formed? `cana` is another particle, just like the particle `ci` in `kuhiñci`.

105. Sabbekaññayatehi kāle dā. Etehi sattamyantehi kāle dā hoti. Sabbasmiṃ kāle sabbadā, ekadā, aññadā, yadā, tadā. Kāleti kiṃ? Sabbattha dese.

105. After `sabba`, `eka`, `añña`, `ya`, and `ta`, the suffix `dā` occurs in the sense of time. After these words with a seventh case ending, the suffix `dā` occurs in the sense of time. For example: from `sabbasmiṃ kāle` (at all times) comes `sabbadā` (always); also `ekadā` (once), `aññadā` (at another time), `yadā` (when), `tadā` (then). Why specify 'in the sense of time'? To exclude its use in the sense of place, as in `sabbattha dese` (everywhere, in a place).

106. Kadā kudā sadā dhunedāni.

106. The forms `kadā`, `kudā`, `sadā`, `adhunā`, and `idāni`.

Ete saddā nipaccante. Kasmiṃ kāle kadā, kudā, sabbasmiṃ kāle sadā, imasmiṃ kāle adhunā, idāni.

These words are irregularly formed. Thus: from `kasmiṃ kāle` (at what time) are formed `kadā` and `kudā` (when); from `sabbasmiṃ kāle` (at all times) is formed `sadā` (always); from `imasmiṃ kāle` (at this time) are formed `adhunā` and `idāni` (now).

107. Ajja sajjvaparajjvetarahi karahā.

107. Ajja, sajju, aparajju, etarahi, karahā.

Etesaddā nipaccante. Pakatippaccayo ādeso kālavisesoti sabbametaṃ nipātanā labbhati, imassa ṭo jjo jāhani nipaccate, asmiṃ ahani ajja. Samānassa sabhāvo jju cāhani, samāne ahani sajju. Aparasmā jju, aparasmiṃ ahani aparajju. Imasseto kāle rahi ca, imasmiṃ kāle etarahi. Kiṃsaddassa ko raha cānajjatane, kasmiṃ kāle karaha.

These words are irregularly formed. Base, suffix, substitution, and specific time—all this is obtained by irregular formation. For `ima`, `ṭo` becomes `jja` in the sense of 'day' by irregular formation; thus, `asmiṃ ahani` becomes `ajja`. For `samāna`, `sa` is the substitute and `jju` is the suffix, also in the sense of 'day'; thus, `samāne ahani` becomes `sajju`. From `apara`, `jju` is the suffix; thus, `aparasmiṃ ahani` becomes `aparajju`. For `ima` and `eta`, `rahi` is also the suffix in the sense of time; thus, `imasmiṃ kāle` becomes `etarahi`. For the word `kiṃ`, `ka` is the substitute and `raha` is the suffix in the sense of 'not today'; thus, `kasmiṃ kāle` becomes `karaha`.

108. Sabbādīhi payāre thā.

108. The suffix `thā` occurs after `sabba` and similar words in the sense of manner.

Sāmaññassa [M 0.0169] bhedako viseso pakāro, tattha vattamānehi sabbādīhi thā hoti. Sabbena pakārena sabbathā, yathā, tathā.

A manner is a specific distinction of generality; when occurring in that sense, `thā` occurs after `sabba` and similar words. For example: `sabbena pakārena` (in every manner) becomes `sabbathā` (in every way); `yathā` (as); `tathā` (thus).

109. Kathamitthaṃ.

109. Kathaṃ, itthaṃ.

Ete saddā nipaccante pakāre. Kimimehi thaṃ paccayo, kaita ca tesaṃ yathākkamaṃ, kathaṃ, itthaṃ.

These words are irregularly formed in the sense of manner. After `kiṃ` and `ima`, the suffix `thaṃ` occurs, and `ka` and `ita` are the respective substitutes for them; thus, `kathaṃ` and `itthaṃ`.

110. Dhā saṅkhyāhi.

110. The suffix `dhā` occurs after numerals.

Saṅkhyāvācīhi pakāre dhā parā hoti. Dvīhi pakārehi, dve vā pakāre karoti dvidhā karoti, bahudhā karoti, ekaṃ rāsiṃ pañcappakāraṃ karoti pañcadhā karoti, pañcappakāramekappakāraṃ karoti ekadhā karoti.

After words expressing numerals, `dhā` occurs in the sense of manner. For example: `dvīhi pakārehi` (in two ways), or `dve vā pakāre karoti` (he makes two ways) becomes `dvidhā karoti` (he makes twofold); `bahudhā karoti` (he makes manifold); `ekaṃ rāsiṃ pañcappakāraṃ karoti` (he makes one heap into five kinds) becomes `pañcadhā karoti` (he makes fivefold); `pañcappakāram ekappakāraṃ karoti` (he makes five kinds into one kind) becomes `ekadhā karoti` (he makes onefold).

111. Vekā jjhaṃ.

111. After `eka`, `jjhaṃ` occurs optionally.

Ekasmā pakare jjhaṃ vā hoti. Ekajjhaṃ karoti, ekadhā, karoti.

After `eka`, in the sense of manner, `jjhaṃ` occurs optionally. For example: `ekajjhaṃ karoti` (he makes onefold), or `ekadhā karoti` (he makes onefold).

112. Dvitīhedhā.

112. After `dvi` and `ti`, `edhā` occurs.

Dvitīhi pakāre edhā vā hoti. Dvedhā, tedhā, dvidhā, tidhā.

After `dvi` and `ti`, in the sense of manner, `edhā` occurs optionally. For example: `dvedhā` (twofold), `tedhā` (threefold), `dvidhā` (twofold), `tidhā` (threefold).

113. Tabbati jātiyo.

113. After a word denoting a quality, `jātiyo` occurs.

Pakāravati taṃsāmaññavācakā saddā jātiyo hoti, paṭujātiyo, mudujātiyo.

After words denoting a type or a general quality, the suffix `jātiyo` occurs. For example: `paṭujātiyo` (of a sharp kind), `mudujātiyo` (of a soft kind).

114. Vārasaṅkhyāya kkhattuṃ.

114. After a numeral of times, `kkhattuṃ` occurs.

Vārasambandhiniyā [M 0.0170] saṅkhyāya kkhattuṃ hoti. Dve vāre bhuñjati dvikkhattuṃ divasassa bhuñjati. Vāraggahaṇaṃ kiṃ? Pañca bhuñjati. Saṅkhyāyāti kiṃ? Pahūte vāre bhuñjati.

After a number related to turns, `kkhattuṃ` occurs. For example: `dve vāre bhuñjati` (he eats two times) becomes `dvikkhattuṃ divasassa bhuñjati` (he eats twice a day). Why the inclusion of 'turn'? [To exclude:] `pañca bhuñjati` (he eats five). Why 'number'? [To exclude:] `pahūte vāre bhuñjati` (he eats many times).

115. Katimhā.

115. After `kati`.

Vārasambandhiniyā katisaṅkhyāya kkhattuṃ hoti, kati vāre, bhuñjathi, katikkhattuṃ bhuñjati.

After the numeral `kati`, when related to turns, the suffix `kkhattuṃ` occurs. For example: `kati vāre bhuñjati` (how many times does one eat?) becomes `katikkhattuṃ bhuñjati` (how many times does one eat?).

116. Bahumhā dhā ca paccāsattiyaṃ.

116. After `bahu`, `dhā` also occurs, in the sense of proximity.

Vārasambandhiniyā bahusaṅkhyāya dhā hoti kkhatthuṃ ca, vārānañce paccāsatti hoti, bahudhā divasassa bhuñjati bahukkhattuṃ bhuñjati. Paccāsattiyanti kiṃ? Bahuvāre māsassa bhuñjati.

After the numeral `bahu`, when related to turns, `dhā` occurs, and also `kkhattuṃ`, if there is proximity of the turns. For example: `bahudhā divasassa bhuñjati` (he eats manifoldly during the day), `bahukkhattuṃ bhuñjati` (he eats many times). Why the condition 'in proximity'? [To exclude cases like:] `bahuvāre māsassa bhuñjati` (he eats many times in a month).

117. Sakiṃ vā.

117. `Sakiṃ` is also an optional form.

Ekaṃ vāramiccasmiṃ atthe sakinti vā nipaccate. Ekavāraṃ bhuñjati sakiṃ bhuñjati, vāti kiṃ? Ekakkhattuṃ bhuñjati.

In the sense of 'one time', the word `sakiṃ` is optionally formed by irregular derivation. For example: `ekavāraṃ bhuñjati` (he eats one time) or `sakiṃ bhuñjati` (he eats once). Why 'optionally'? [Because there is also the form:] `ekakkhattuṃ bhuñjati` (he eats one time).

118. So vīcchappakāresu.

118. The suffix `so` occurs in the senses of repetition and manner.

Vīcchāyaṃ pakāre ca so hoti bahulaṃ. Vīcchāyaṃ-khaṇḍaso, bilaso. Pakāre-puthuso, sabbaso.

In the sense of repetition and manner, the suffix `so` occurs frequently. In repetition: `khaṇḍaso` (piecemeal), `bilaso` (in portions). In manner: `puthuso` (variously), `sabbaso` (in every way).

119. Abhūtatabbhāve karāsabhūyoge vikārā cī.

119. After a word denoting a transformation, the suffix `cī` occurs in the sense of 'becoming what it was not before', when in connection with the verbs `karoti`, `atthi`, and `bhavati`.

Avatthāvato-vatthantarenābhūtassa tāyāvatthāya bhāvekarāsabhūhi sambandhe sati vikāravācakā cī hoti, adhavalaṃ dhavalaṃ [M 0.0171] karoti dhavalī karoti, adhavalo dhavalo siyā dhavalī siyā, adhavalo dhavalo bhavati dhavalī bhavati. Abhūta tabbhāveti kiṃ? Ghaṭaṃ karoti, dadhi atthi, ghaṭo bhavati. Karāsabhūyogeti kiṃ? Adhavalodhavalo jāyate. Vikārāti kiṃ? Pakatiyā māhotu, suvaṇṇaṃ kuṇḍalaṃ karoti.

When there is a connection with the verbs `karoti`, `atthi`, and `bhavati`, the suffix `cī` occurs after a word denoting a transformation, in the sense of a thing which was not in a previous state becoming that state. For example: `adhavalaṃ dhavalaṃ karoti` (he makes what is not white, white) becomes `dhavalī karoti` (he whitens); `adhavalo dhavalo siyā` (what is not white may become white) becomes `dhavalī siyā` (it may whiten); `adhavalo dhavalo bhavati` (what is not white becomes white) becomes `dhavalī bhavati` (it whitens). Why the condition 'becoming what it was not'? [To exclude:] `ghaṭaṃ karoti` (he makes a pot); `dadhi atthi` (there is yogurt); `ghaṭo bhavati` (a pot comes into being). Why the condition 'in connection with `karoti`, `atthi`, and `bhavati`'? [To exclude:] `adhavalo dhavalo jāyate` (what is not white is born white). Why the condition 'from a word denoting transformation'? [To exclude:] `suvaṇṇaṃ kuṇḍalaṃ karoti` (he makes gold into an earring).

120. Dissantaññepi paccayā.

120. Other suffixes are also seen.

Vuttato-ññepi paccayā dissanti vuttāvuttatthesu. Vividhā mātaro vimātaro, tāsaṃ puttā vemātikā-rikaṇa. Pathaṃ gacchatīti pathāvino-āvī. Issā assa atthīti issukī-ukī. Dhuraṃ vahatīti dhorayho- yhaṇa.

Suffixes other than those mentioned are also seen, in meanings both mentioned and not mentioned. For example: from `vividhā mātaro, tāsaṃ puttā` (sons of different mothers), comes `vemātika` (a step-brother), with the suffix `ikaṇa`. From `pathaṃ gacchati` (one who goes on the path), comes `pathāvī` (a traveler), with the suffix `āvī`. From `issā assa atthi` (one who has envy), comes `issukī` (envious), with the suffix `ukī`. From `dhuraṃ vahati` (one who bears a yoke), comes `dhorayha` (a beast of burden), with the suffix `yhaṇa`.

121. Aññasmiṃ.

121. In another meaning.

Vuttato-ññasmimpi atthe vuttappaccayā dissanti. Magadhānaṃ issaro māgadho-dhaṇā. Kāsīti sahassaṃ, tamagghatīti kāsiyo iyo.

The suffixes already mentioned are also seen in meanings other than those for which they were prescribed. For example: from `Magadhānaṃ issaro` (the lord of the Magadhans) comes `Māgadho`, with the suffix `aṇa`. A `kāsi` is a thousand; from `tam agghati` (it is worth that) comes `kāsiyo`, with the suffix `iya`.

122. Sakatthe.

122. In its own meaning.

Sakatthepi paccayā dissanti. Hīnako, potako, kiccayaṃ.

Even in its own meaning, suffixes are seen. For example: 'Hīnako' (inferior), 'potako' (young animal), 'kiccayaṃ' (what is to be done).

123. Lopo.

123. Elision.

Paccayānaṃ lopopi dissati. Buddhe ratanaṃ paṇītaṃ, cakkhuṃ suññaṃ attena vā attariyena vāti bhāvappaccayalopo.

The elision of suffixes is also seen. For example: 'In the Buddha is the exquisite jewel'; 'the eye is empty of self or of what belongs to self'—this is the elision of the suffix expressing state (bhāva).

124. Sarānamādissāyuvaṇṇassāeo ṇānubandhe.

124. For the initial short vowels a, i, and u, the substitutions are ā, e, and o respectively, when a suffix with an indicatory 'ṇa' follows.

Sarānamādibhūtā [M 0.0172] ye akārivaṇṇuvaṇṇā, tesaṃ āeo honti yathākkamaṃṇānubandhe. Rāghavo, venateyyo, meniko, oḷumpiko, dobhaggaṃ. Ṇānubandheti kiṃ? Purātano.

For the initial vowels, namely 'a', 'i', and 'u', the substitutions are 'ā', 'e', and 'o' respectively when a suffix with an indicatory 'ṇa' follows. Examples: Rāghavo, Venateyyo, Meniko, Oḷumpiko, Dobhaggaṃ. Why specify 'when a suffix with an indicatory ṇa follows'? For example: Purātano.

125. Saṃyoge kvaci.

125. Sometimes, in a consonant cluster.

Sarānamādibhūtā ye ayuvaṇṇā, tesaṃ āeo honti kvacideva saṃyogavisaye ṇānubandhe. Decco, koṇḍañño. Kvacīti kiṃ? Kattikeyyo.

For the initial short vowels a, i, and u, the substitutions 'ā', 'e', and 'o' occur only sometimes in the case of a consonant cluster when a suffix with an indicatory 'ṇa' follows. Examples: Decco, Koṇḍañño. Why 'sometimes'? For example: Kattikeyyo.

126. Majjhe.

126. In the middle.

Majjhe vattamānānampi ayuvaṇṇānaṃ ā e o honti kvaci. Aḍḍhateyyo, vāseṭṭho.

Even for the short vowels a, i, and u occurring in the middle, the substitutions 'ā', 'e', and 'o' sometimes occur. Examples: Aḍḍhateyyo, Vāseṭṭho.

127. Kosajjājjava pārisajja sohajja maddavārissāsabhājaññatheyya bāhusaccā.

127. Kosajja (laziness), ajjava (uprightness), pārisajja (suitability for an assembly), sohajja (good-heartedness), maddava (gentleness), ārissa (sagehood), āsabha (excellence), ājañña (nobility), theyya (thievery), and bāhusacca (great learning).

Etesaddā nipaccanteṇānubandhe. Kusī tassa bhāvokosajjaṃ, ujuno bhāvo ajjavaṃ, parisāsu sādhu pārisajjo, suhadayova suhajjo, tassa pana bhāvo sohajjaṃ, muduno bhāvo maddavaṃ, isino idaṃ bhāvo vā ārissaṃ, usabhassa idaṃ bhāvo [M 0.0173] vā āsabhaṃ, ājānīyassa bhāvo so eva vā ājaññaṃ, thenassa bhāvo kammaṃ vā theyyaṃ, bahussatassa bhāvo bāhusaccaṃ, etesu yamalakkhaṇikaṃ, taṃ nipātanā.

These words are irregularly formed with a suffix having an indicatory 'ṇa'. 'Kosajjaṃ' is the state of a lazy person; 'ajjavaṃ' is the state of an upright one; 'pārisajjo' is one who is good in assemblies. A good-hearted one is a 'suhajjo', and his state is 'sohajjaṃ'. 'Maddavaṃ' is the state of a gentle one. 'Ārissaṃ' is that which belongs to a sage, or his state. 'Āsabhaṃ' is that which belongs to a bull, or his state. 'Ājaññaṃ' is the state of a thoroughbred, or that very thing. 'Theyyaṃ' is the state of a thief, or his action. 'Bāhusaccaṃ' is the state of a much-learned one. Among these, whatever is characterized by consonant doubling is due to irregular formation.

128. Manādīnaṃ saka.

128. For 'mana' and others, 'sa' with 'ka'.

Manādīnaṃ saka hoti ṇānubandhe. Manasi bhavaṃ mānasaṃ, dummanaso bhāvo domanassaṃ, somanassaṃ.

For 'mana' and others, 'sa' with 'ka' occurs when a suffix with an indicatory 'ṇa' follows. For example: 'Mānasaṃ' is what arises in the mind. 'Domanassaṃ' is the state of a depressed mind. 'Somanassaṃ' is the state of a joyful mind.

129. Uvaṇṇassāvaṅa sare.

129. For the vowel 'u', 'ava' is substituted when a vowel follows.

Sarādo ṇānubandhe uvaṇṇassāvaṅa hoti. Rāghavo, jambavaṃ.

When a vowel-initial suffix with an indicatory 'ṇa' follows, 'ava' is substituted for the vowel 'u'. Examples: Rāghavo, Jambavaṃ.

130. Yamhi gossa ca.

130. And for 'go', when a suffix beginning with 'ya' follows.

Yakārādo paccaye gossuvaṇṇassa ca avaṅa hoti. Gabyaṃ, bhātabyo.

When a suffix beginning with 'ya' follows, 'ava' is substituted for 'go' and for the vowel 'u'. Examples: Gabyaṃ, Bhātabyo.

131. Lopo-vaṇṇivaṇṇānaṃ.

131. Elision of the vowels 'a' and 'i'.

Yakārādo paccaye avaṇṇivaṇṇānaṃ lopo hoti. Dāyajjaṃ, kāruññaṃ, ādhipaccaṃ, deppaṃ. Bahulaṃvidhānā kvaci na hoti kiccayaṃ.

When a suffix beginning with 'ya' follows, there is elision of the vowels 'a' and 'i'. Examples: 'Dāyajjaṃ' (inheritance), 'Kāruññaṃ' (compassion), 'Ādhipaccaṃ' (sovereignty), 'Deppaṃ' (brilliance). Because the application is extensive, it sometimes does not occur, for example: 'kiccayaṃ'.

132. Rānubandhe-nta sarādissa.

132. When a suffix with an indicatory 'ra' follows, elision of the final vowel of the initial part occurs.

Anto saro ādimhi yassāvayavassa, tassa lopo hoti rānubandhe. Kittakaṃ, petteyyaṃ.

The final vowel of the initial component is elided when a suffix with an indicatory 'ra' follows. Examples: Kittakaṃ (how much), Petteyyaṃ (belonging to a father).

133. Kisamahatamime kasa mahā.

133. For 'kisa' and 'mahant', 'kasa' and 'mahā' are substituted before 'ima'.

Kisassa mahato ime kasamahā honti yathākkamaṃ, kasimā, mahimā.

For 'kisa' and 'mahant', 'kasa' and 'mahā' are substituted respectively. Examples: 'Kasimā' (thinness), 'Mahimā' (greatness).

134. Āyussāyasa mantumhi.

134. For 'āyu', 'āyas' is substituted when the suffix 'mantu' follows.

Āyussa [M 0.0174] āyasādeso hoti mantumhi. Āyasmā.

For 'āyu', the substitution 'āyas' occurs when the suffix 'mantu' follows. Example: 'Āyasmā' (Venerable).

135. Jo vuddhassiyiṭṭhesu.

135. For 'vuddha', 'ja' is substituted before the suffixes 'iya' and 'iṭṭha'.

Vuddhassa jo hoti iyaiṭṭhesu, jeyyo, jeṭṭho.

For 'vuddha', 'ja' is substituted before the suffixes 'iya' and 'iṭṭha'. Examples: jeyyo, jeṭṭho.

136. Bāḷhantikapasatthānaṃ sādha neda sā.

136. For 'bāḷha', 'antika', and 'pasattha'; 'sādha', 'neda', and 'sā' are the respective substitutes.

Iyaiṭṭhesu bāḷhantikapasatthānaṃ sādha neda sā honti yathākkamaṃ. Sādhiyo, sādhiṭṭho, nediyo, nediṭṭho, seyyo, seṭṭho.

Before the suffixes 'iya' and 'iṭṭha', for 'bāḷha', 'antika', and 'pasattha', the respective substitutes are 'sādha', 'neda', and 'sā'. Examples: sādhiyo, sādhiṭṭho; nediyo, nediṭṭho; seyyo, seṭṭho.

137. Kaṇakanāppayuvānaṃ.

137. Regarding kaṇa and kanā for appa and yuva.

Iyaiṭṭhesu appayuvānaṃ kaṇa kanā honti yathākkamaṃ. Kaṇiyo kaṇiṭṭho, kaniyo kaniṭṭho.

When the suffixes -iya and -iṭṭha follow, kaṇa and kanā are substituted for appa and yuva respectively. For example: kaṇiyo, kaṇiṭṭho; kaniyo, kaniṭṭho.

138. Lopo vī mantu vantūnaṃ.

138. Elision of -vī, -mantu, and -vantu.

Vī mantu vantūnaṃ lopo hoti iyaiṭṭhesu. Atisayena medhāvī medhiyo, medhiṭṭho, atisayena satimā satiyo, satiṭṭho, atisayena guṇavā guṇiyo, guṇiṭṭho.

Elision of the suffixes -vī, -mantu, and -vantu occurs when -iya and -iṭṭha follow. For example: from atisayena medhāvī (exceedingly intelligent) are formed medhiyo, medhiṭṭho; from atisayena satimā (exceedingly mindful) are formed satiyo, satiṭṭho; from atisayena guṇavā (exceedingly virtuous) are formed guṇiyo, guṇiṭṭho.

139. Ḍe satissa tissa.

139. Of the ti of sati when ḍa follows.

Ḍepare satyantassa tikārassa lopo hoti, vīsaṃ sataṃ, tiṃsaṃ sataṃ.

When ḍa follows, the letter ti of a word ending in sati is elided. For example: vīsaṃ sataṃ, tiṃsaṃ sataṃ.

140. Etasseṭa ttake.

140. For etassa, eṭa is substituted when ttaka follows.

Ttake pare etassa eṭa hoti. Ettakaṃ.

When ttaka follows, eṭa is substituted for etassa. For example: ettakaṃ.

141. Ṇikassiyo vā.

141. For the suffix -ṇika, -iyo is optionally substituted.

Ṇikassa [M 0.0175] vā iyo hoti, sakyaputtiyo, sakyaputtiko.

For the suffix -ṇika, -iyo is optionally substituted. For example: sakyaputtiyo, sakyaputtiko.

142. Adhātussa kā-syādito ghe-ssi.

142. For the `a` before `ka` of a non-root, not following `syādi`, there is `i` when `ghe` follows.

Ghe pare adhātussa yo kakāro, tato pubbassa akārassa bahulaṃ i hoti sace gho na syādito paro hoti. Bālikā, kārikā, adhātussāti kiṃ? Sakā, keti kiṃ? Nandanā, asyāditoti kiṃ? Bahuparibbājakā mathurā, bahucammikāti kakārena syādino byavahitattā siddhaṃ, gheti kiṃ? Bālako, assāti kiṃ? Bahukattukā sālā.

When `ghe` follows, the `a` preceding the letter `ka` of a non-root stem frequently becomes `i`, provided that the `ka` does not follow a `syādi` suffix. For example: bālikā, kārikā. Why the specification 'of a non-root'? For example, sakā. Why 'of ka'? For example, nandanā. Why 'not following a syādi suffix'? For example, bahuparibbājakā mathurā. In bahucammikā, the form is established because of the separation from the syādi suffix by the letter ka. Why 'when ghe follows'? For example, bālako. Why 'of the a'? For example, bahukattukā sālā.

Iti moggallāne byākaraṇe vuttiyaṃ

Thus in the commentary on the Moggallāna Grammar.

Ṇādikaṇḍo catuttho.

Here ends the fourth chapter, the Ṇādikaṇḍa.

5. Pañcamo kaṇḍo (khādi)

5. The Fifth Chapter (Khādi)

1. Tija mānehi kha sā khamā vīmaṃsāsu.

1. From the roots tij and mān, the suffixes kha and sa are used respectively in the senses of khamā (forbearance) and vīmaṃsā (investigation).

Khantiyaṃ tijā vīmaṃsāyaṃ mānā ca khasappaccayā honti yathākkamaṃ, titikkhā, vīmaṃsā, titikkhati, vīmaṃsati. Khamāvīmaṃsā, sūti kiṃ? Tejanaṃ, tejo, tejayati, mānanaṃ, mānomāneti.

In the sense of patience (khanti), from the root tij, and in the sense of investigation (vīmaṃsā), from the root mān, the suffixes kha and sa occur respectively. For example: titikkhā, vīmaṃsā; titikkhati, vīmaṃsati. Why the specification khamāvīmaṃsāsu? To exclude cases such as: tejanaṃ, tejo, tejayati; mānanaṃ, mānomāneti.

2. Kitā tikicchāsaṃsayesu cho.

2. From the root kit, the suffix cha is used in the senses of tikicchā (medical treatment) and saṃsaya (doubt).

Tikicchāyaṃ saṃsaye ca vattamānā kitā cho hoti. Tikicchā, vicikicchā, tikicchati, vicikicchati. Aññatra niketo, saṃketo, ketanaṃ, keto, ketayati.

From the root kit, when used in the sense of tikicchā (treatment) and saṃsaya (doubt), the suffix cha occurs. For example: tikicchā, vicikicchā; tikicchati, vicikicchati. In other senses: niketo, saṃketo, ketanaṃ, keto, ketayati.

3. Nindāyaṃ gupa badhā bassa bho ca.

3. From gup and badh in the sense of censure; and bassa bho.

Nindāyaṃ [M 0.0176] vattamānehi gupa badhehi cho hoti bassa bho ca. Jigucchā, bībhacchā, jigucchati, bībhacchati, aññatra gopanaṃ, gopo, gopeti, badhako.

From gup and badh, when used in the sense of censure, the suffix cha occurs, and also bassa bho. For example: jigucchā, bībhacchā; jigucchati, bībhacchati. In other senses: gopanaṃ, gopo, gopeti; badhako.

4. Tuṃsmā lopo cicchāyaṃ te.

4. From the suffix -tuṃ, elision occurs, and the suffix -te is used in the sense of desire.

Tumantato icchāyamatthe te khasachā honti bahulaṃ, lopo ca tuṃpaccayassa hoti sutattā, bubhukkhā, jigīsāṃ, jighacchā, bubhukkhati, jigīsati jighacchati. Idha kasmā na hoti ‘bhottumicchatī’ti? Padantarenābhidhānā. Tuṃsmāti kiṃ? Bhojanamicchati. Icchāyanti kiṃ? Bhuñjituṃ gacchati. Kathaṃ ‘kūlaṃ vipati satī’ti? Yathā kūlaṃ patitu micchatīti vākyaṃ hoti, evaṃ vuttipi hossati. Vākyameva carahi kathaṃ hoti? Lokassa tathā vacanicchāya.

From a word ending in the suffix -tuṃ, in the sense of desire, the suffixes -te, -kha, -sa, and -cha frequently occur, and there is elision of the -tuṃ suffix, as is established by usage. For example: bubhukkhā, jigīsā, jighacchā; bubhukkhati, jigīsati, jighacchati. Why does this not apply in the case of bhottum icchati? Because it is expressed by a separate word. Why the specification 'from -tuṃ'? To exclude bhojanam icchati. Why 'in the sense of desire'? To exclude bhuñjituṃ gacchati. How then is kūlaṃ vipatisati explained? Just as there is the sentence kūlaṃ patituṃ icchati, so too will this derived form exist. Then how does the sentence itself come to be? From the people's desire to speak in such a way.

5. Īyo kammā.

5. The suffix -īya is added to a word that is the object.

Icchākammato icchāyamatthe īyappaccayo hoti. Puttamicchati putthīyati. Kammāti kiṃ? Asinecchati. Idha kasmā na hoti ‘raññoputtamicchatī’ti? Sāpekkhattā, na hi aññamapekkhamāno aññena sahekatthibhāvamanubhavituṃ sakkoti. Idhāpi carahi na siyā ‘attano putta micchatī’ti? Nevettha bhavitabbaṃ, na hi bhavati ‘attano puttīyatī’ti, kathaṃ carahi puttassa attaniyatā-vagamyate[M 0.0177]? Aññassāsutattā icchāya ca tabbisayattā.

From the object of the verb 'to desire', the suffix -īya occurs in the sense of desire. For example, from puttam icchati (he desires a son) is formed puttīyati. Why the specification 'from the object'? To exclude asinā icchati (he desires with a sword). Why does this not apply in the case of rañño puttam icchati (he desires the king's son)? Because of its dependence; for a word that is dependent on another cannot experience a state of being one with yet another. Then should it also not apply in the case of attano puttaṃ icchati (he desires his own son)? It should not apply here, for attano puttīyati is not a valid form. How then is the son's belonging to oneself understood? Because another owner is not mentioned, and because the desire is directed towards that object.

6. Upamānācāre.

6. From a standard of comparison, in the sense of behavior.

Kammato upamānā ācāratthe īyo hoti. Puttami-vā-carati puttīyati māṇavakaṃ, upamānāti kiṃ? Puttamācarati.

From a word that is an object and a standard of comparison, the suffix -īya occurs in the sense of 'to behave like'. For example: from puttam iva ācarati māṇavakaṃ (he treats the young man like a son) is formed puttīyati māṇavakaṃ. Why the specification 'from a standard of comparison'? To exclude puttam ācarati (he approaches his son).

7. Ādhārā.

7. From a locative.

Ādhāratū-pamānā ācāratthe īyo yoti. Kuṭiyamivā-carati kuṭīyatī pāsāde, pāsādīyati kuṭiyaṃ bhikkhu.

From a word that is a locative and a standard of comparison, the suffix -īya occurs in the sense of 'to behave as if in'. For example: from kuṭiyaṃ iva ācarati pāsāde (he behaves in the palace as if in a hut) is formed kuṭīyati pāsāde; and pāsādīyati kuṭiyaṃ bhikkhu (the monk behaves in the hut as if in a palace).

8. Kattutāyo.

8. From an agent, the suffix -āya.

Kattutū-pamānā ācāratthe āyo hoti. Pabbato ivācarati pabbatāyati.

From a noun denoting an agent, when used as a comparison, the suffix 'āyo' occurs in the sense of behavior. For example: 'pabbato ivācarati' (he behaves like a mountain) becomes 'pabbatāyati'.

9. Ycatthe.

9. Regarding the meaning of the suffix 'y'.

Kattuto abhūtatabbhāve āyo hoti bahulaṃ. Bhusāyati, paṭapaṭāyati, lohitāyati, kattutotveva? (Abhusaṃ) bhusaṃ karotīhi, iha kasmā na hoti ‘bhusī bhavatī’ti? Vuttatthatāya.

From a noun denoting an agent, the suffix 'āyo' frequently occurs in the sense of becoming what one was not. For example: bhusāyati, paṭapaṭāyati, lohitāyati. Is it only from an agent? [This is derived from the sense,] 'one makes what is not abundant, abundant.' Why does the form 'bhusī bhavati' not occur here? Because the meaning is already expressed.

10. Saddādīni karoti.

10. One makes sounds and so forth.

Saddādīhi dutiyantehi karotīti asmiṃ atthe āyo hoti. Saddāyati, verāyati, kalahāyati, dhūpāyati.

From nouns such as 'sadda', when ending in the accusative case, the suffix 'āyo' occurs in the sense of 'karoti' (he makes). For example: saddāyati, verāyati, kalahāyati, dhūpāyati.

11. Numotva-sso.

11. From 'namo', the suffix 'assa'.

Namoiccasmā [M 0.0178] karotīti asmiṃ atthe asso hoti. Namassati tathāgtaṃ.

From the indeclinable 'namo', the suffix 'assa' occurs in the sense of 'karoti' (to do). For example: Namassati tathāgataṃ (He pays homage to the Tathāgata).

12. Dhātvatthe nāmasmi.

12. From a noun, in the sense of a verbal root.

Nāmasmā dhātvatthe bahulamihoti. Hatthinā atikkamati atihatthayati, vīṇāya upagāyati upavīṇayati, daḷhaṃ karoti vinayaṃ daḷhayati, visuddhā hoti ratti visuddhayati, kusalaṃ pucchati kusalayati.

From a noun, a denominative verb is frequently formed in the sense of a verbal root. For example: from 'hatthinā atikkamati' (he surpasses by means of an elephant), 'atihatthayati' is formed; from 'vīṇāya upagāyati' (he sings along with a lute), 'upavīṇayati' is formed; from 'daḷhaṃ karoti vinayaṃ' (he makes the discipline firm), 'vinayaṃ daḷhayati' is formed; from 'visuddhā hoti ratti' (the night becomes pure), 'ratti visuddhayati' is formed; from 'kusalaṃ pucchati' (he asks about what is skillful), 'kusalayati' is formed.

13. Saccādīhāpi.

13. Also from 'sacca' and so forth.

Saccādīhi dhātvatthe āpi hoti. Saccāpeti, atthāpeti, vedāpeti, sukkhāpeti, sukhāpeti, dukkhāpeti.

From nouns such as 'sacca', the suffix 'āpi' occurs in the sense of a verbal root. For example: saccāpeti (causes to realize the truth), atthāpeti (causes to be established), vedāpeti (causes to know), sukkhāpeti (causes to dry), sukhāpeti (causes to be happy), dukkhāpeti (causes to suffer).

14. Kriyatthā.

14. From that which has the meaning of action.

Ayamadhikāro āsatthaparisamattiyā. Kriyā attho yassa so kriyattho dhātu.

This governing rule extends until the end of the chapter. That which has action as its meaning is a 'kriyattha', that is, a verbal root.

15. Curādito ṇi.

15. From the 'curādi' group of roots, the suffix 'ṇi'.

Curādīhi kriyatthehi sakatthe ṇi paro hoti bahulaṃ. Ṇakāro vuddhyattho, evamaññatrāpi, corayati, lāḷayati, kathaṃ ‘rajjaṃ kāretī’ti? Yogavibhāgato.

From the 'curādi' group of roots, which have the meaning of action, the suffix 'ṇi' frequently follows in their own meaning. The letter 'ṇ' serves to cause 'vuddhi' substitution, and so also elsewhere. For example: corayati (he steals), lāḷayati (he fondles). How is 'rajjaṃ kāreti' (he causes the kingdom to be ruled) formed? By means of 'yogavibhāga' (splitting the rule).

16. Payojakabyāpāre ṇāpi ca.

16. And also the suffix 'ṇāpi', in the sense of the activity of an instigator.

Kattāraṃ yo payojayati, tassa byāpāre kriyatthā ṇiṇāpī honti bahulaṃ, kāreti, kārāpeti. Nanu ca kattāpi karaṇādīnaṃ [M 0.0179] payojakoti taṃbyāpārepi ṇiṇāpī pāpuṇanti? Payojakaggahaṇasāmatthiyā na bhavissanti curādīhi visuṃ vacanasāmatthiyā ca. Ato bhiyyo ṇāpiyeva, ṇiyevuvaṇṇato, dvayamevaññehi.

He who instigates an agent to act, in the activity of that instigator, the suffixes 'ṇi' and 'ṇāpi' are frequently added to verbal roots. For example: kāreti (causes to do), kārāpeti (causes to have done). Now, is not the agent also an instigator of the instruments and so forth? Therefore, should not 'ṇi' and 'ṇāpi' also apply to its activity? They do not, by the force of the specific mention of 'instigator', and by the force of the separate rule for the 'curādi' group. Furthermore, 'ṇāpi' is more common; 'ṇi' is used after roots ending in the vowel 'u'; and both are used after other roots.

17. Kyo bhāvakammesva-parokkhesu māna nta tyādīsu. Bhāvakammavihitesu parokkhāvajjitesu mānantatyādīsu paresu kyo hoti kriyatthā. Ntaggahaṇamuttaratthaṃ, kakāro avuddhyattho evamuttaratrāpi. Ṭhīyamānaṃ, ṭhīyate, sūyamānaṃ, sūyate, aparokkhesu mānantatyādīsūti kiṃ? Babhūva devadattena, bibhida kusulo. Bhijjate kusulo sayamevāti ‘bhijjate’ti savanā kammatā-vagamyate, ‘sayamevā’ti savanato kattutā, kattutāvacanicchāyantu ‘bhindati kusulo attāna’nti bhavati, evamaññampi yathāgamamanugantabbaṃ. ‘Aparokkhesu mānantatyādīsū’ti ayamadhikāro ā ‘tanāditvo’ti 5.26. Apica ete kyādayo tyādīsu parabhūtesu kattukammabhāva vihitesu kyalādīnaṃ vidhānato tesveva viññāyantīti akammakehi dhātūhi kattubhāvesu, sakammakehi kattukammesu, kammāvacanicchāyaṃ bhāve ca bhavantīti veditabbā. Yassa pana dhātussa kiriyā kammamapekkhate, so sakammako, yassa tu kiriyā kattumattamapekkhate, svākammakoti ñātabbaṃ.

17. The suffix 'kyo' is used in the impersonal (bhāva) and passive (kamma) senses, when the suffixes 'māna', 'nta', 'ti', etc., follow, except in the perfect tense (parokkha). [Commentary:] After a verbal root, the suffix 'kyo' occurs when the suffixes 'māna', 'nta', 'ti', etc., which are prescribed in the impersonal and passive senses, follow, excluding the perfect tense. The inclusion of 'nta' is for a subsequent rule; the letter 'k' serves to prevent 'vuddhi' substitution, and so also elsewhere. For example: ṭhīyamānaṃ (being stood), ṭhīyate (it is stood); sūyamānaṃ (being heard), sūyate (it is heard). Why the specification 'excluding the perfect tense...'? Consider: 'babhūva devadattena' (it was become by Devadatta), 'bibhida kusulo' (the reed split).
