When one hears 'bhijjate kusulo sayameva' (the reed splits by itself), from 'bhijjate' the passive sense is understood, and from 'sayameva' the agentive sense is understood. However, when there is a desire to express the agentive sense explicitly, it becomes 'bhindati kusulo attānaṃ' (the reed splits itself). Other cases should be understood similarly, according to tradition. This governing rule, 'excluding the perfect tense...', extends up to the rule 'tanāditvo' (5.26). Moreover, these suffixes 'kyo', etc., when 'ti', etc., follow, are understood only in those senses—agent, object, or impersonal—for which 'kyo', etc., are prescribed. Thus, it should be known that they occur with intransitive roots in the agentive and impersonal senses; with transitive roots in the agentive and passive senses; and also in the impersonal sense when there is a desire to not express the object. Furthermore, a root whose action requires an object is known as transitive (sakammaka), whereas a root whose action requires only an agent is known as intransitive (akammaka).

18. Kattari lo.

18. In the agentive sense, the suffix 'lo'.

Kriyatthato aparokkhesu kattuvihitamāna ntatyādīsu lo hoti. Lakāro, “ñilasse”ti 5-163 visesanattho. Pacamāno, pacanto, pacati.

From a verbal root, the suffix 'lo' occurs when the suffixes 'māna', 'nta', 'ti', etc., prescribed in the agentive sense, follow, excluding the perfect tense. The letter 'la' serves for specification in the rule 'ñilassa' (5-163). For example: pacamāno (cooking), pacanto (cooking), pacati (he cooks).

19. Maṃ ca rudhādīnaṃ.

19. And the infix 'ṃ' for the 'rudhādi' group.

Rudhādito [M 0.0180] kattuvihitamānanta tyādīsu lo hoti maṃ ca antasarā paro. Makāro-nubandho, akāro uccāraṇattho. Rundhamāno, rundhanto, rundhati.

From the 'rudhādi' group of roots, the suffix 'lo' occurs when 'māna', 'nta', 'ti', etc., prescribed in the agentive sense, follow, and the infix 'ṃ' is inserted after the root vowel. The letter 'a' [in 'maṃ'] is for pronunciation, while 'ṃ' is the actual infix. For example: rundhamāno (obstructing), rundhanto (obstructing), rundhati (he obstructs).

20. Ṇiṇāpyāpīhi vā.

20. Optionally after 'ṇi', 'ṇāpi', and 'āpi'.

Ṇiṇāpyāpīhi kattuvihitamānanta tyādīsu lo hoti vibhāsā, orayanto, corento, kārayanto, kārento, kārāpayanto, kārāpento, saccāpayanto, saccāpento, corayati, coreti, kārayati, kāreti, kārāpayati, kārāpeti, saccāpayati, saccāpeti. Vavatthitavibhāsattho-yaṃ vāsaddo, tena māne niccaṃ, corayamāno, kārayamāno, kārāpayamāno, saccāpayamāno.

After the suffixes 'ṇi', 'ṇāpi', and 'āpi', the suffix 'lo' occurs optionally when 'māna', 'nta', 'ti', etc., prescribed in the agentive sense, follow. For example: corayanto/corento, kārayanto/kārento, kārāpayanto/kārāpento, saccāpayanto/saccāpento; corayati/coreti, kārayati/kāreti, kārāpayati/kārāpeti, saccāpayati/saccāpeti. This word 'vā' (or) indicates a restricted option; therefore, with the suffix 'māna', the rule is obligatory: corayamāno, kārayamāno, kārāpayamāno, saccāpayamāno.

21. Divādīhi yaka.

21. From the 'divādi' group of roots, the suffix 'yaka'.

Divādīhi lavisaye yaka hoti. Dibbanto, dibbati.

From the 'divādi' group of roots, the suffix 'yaka' occurs in the domain of 'la'. For example: dibbanto (playing), dibbati (he plays).

22. Tudādīhi ko.

22. From the 'tudādi' group of roots, the suffix 'ko'.

Tudādīhi lavisaye ko hoti. Tudamāno, tudanto, tudati.

From the 'tudādi' group of roots, the suffix 'ko' occurs in the domain of 'la'. For example: tudamāno (striking), tudanto (striking), tudati (he strikes).

23. Jyādīhi knā.

23. From the 'ji' group of roots, the suffix 'knā'.

Jiādīhi lavisaye knā hoti. Jinanto, jināti. Kathaṃ ‘jayanto’ jayatī, ti? Bhūvādipāṭhā.

From the 'ji' group of roots, the suffix 'knā' occurs in the domain of 'la'. For example: jinanto (conquering), jināti (he conquers). How then are 'jayanto' and 'jayati' formed? From the root's inclusion in the 'bhūvādi' group.

24. Kyādīhi kṇā.

24. From the ki group of roots, the suffix kṇā.

Kīādīhi [M 0.0181] lavisaye kṇā hoti. Kiṇanto, kiṇāti.

From the ki group of roots, in the domain of the la-kāras, the suffix kṇā occurs. For example: kiṇanto (buying), kiṇāti (he buys).

25. Svādīhi kṇo.

25. From the su group of roots, the suffix kṇo.

Suādīhi lavisaye kṇo hoti. Suṇamāno, suṇanto, suṇoti. Kathaṃ suṇātīti? Kyādipāṭhā.

From the su group of roots, in the domain of the la-kāras, the suffix kṇo occurs. For example: suṇamāno (hearing), suṇanto (hearing), suṇoti (he hears). How is suṇāti formed? By its inclusion in the list of the ki group.

26. Tanāditvo.

26. From the tan group of roots, the suffix o.

Tanādito lavisaye o hoti. Tanoti.

From the tan group of roots, in the domain of the la-kāras, the suffix o occurs. For example: tanoti (he stretches).

27. Bhāvakammesu tabbā-nīyā.

27. In the impersonal (bhāva) and passive (kamma) senses, the suffixes tabba and anīya.

Tabbaanīyā kriyatthā pare bhāvakammesu bahulaṃ bhavanti. Kattabbaṃ, karaṇīyaṃ, kattabbo kaṭo, karaṇīyo. Bahulādhikārā karaṇādīsupi bhavanti, sinānīyaṃ cuṇṇaṃ, dānīyo brāhmaṇo, sammāvattanīyo guru, pavacanīyo upajjhāyo, upaṭṭhānīyo sisso.

The suffixes tabba and anīya frequently occur after verbs in the impersonal and passive senses. For example: kattabbaṃ (to be done), karaṇīyaṃ (to be done); kattabbo kaṭo (the mat is to be made), karaṇīyo (to be done). By the governing rule of 'variously', they also occur in the sense of instrument and so forth: sinānīyaṃ cuṇṇaṃ (powder for bathing), dānīyo brāhmaṇo (a brahmin worthy of gifts), sammāvattanīyo guru (a teacher to be properly served), pavacanīyo upajjhāyo (a preceptor to be addressed), upaṭṭhānīyo sisso (a pupil to be attended to).

28. Ghyaṇa.

28. The suffix ghyaṇa.

Bhāvakammesu kriyatthā paro ghyaṇa hoti bahulaṃ. Vākyaṃ, kāriyaṃ, ceyyaṃ, jeyyaṃ.

In the impersonal and passive senses, the suffix ghyaṇa frequently occurs after verbs. For example: vākyaṃ (that which is to be said), kāriyaṃ (that which is to be done), ceyyaṃ (that which is to be gathered), jeyyaṃ (that which is to be conquered).

29. Āsse ca.

29. And for ā.

Ātoghyaṇa hoti bhāvakammesu, āssa e ca. Deyyaṃ.

From a root ending in ā, the suffix ghyaṇa occurs in the impersonal and passive senses, and e is substituted for the ā. For example: deyyaṃ (that which is to be given).

30. Vadādīhi yo.

30. From the vad group of roots, the suffix ya.

Vadādīhi [M 0.0182] kriyatthehi yo hoti bahulaṃ bhāvakammesu. Vajjaṃ, majjaṃ, gammaṃ. (42) “Bhujānne”, bhojjo odano, bhojjā yāgu, bhoggamaññaṃ.

From the roots of the vad group, the suffix ya frequently occurs in the impersonal and passive senses. For example: vajjaṃ (that which is to be said), majjaṃ (that which is to be cleansed), gammaṃ (that which is to be gone to). From the root bhuj in the sense of 'food': bhojjo odano (rice to be eaten), bhojjā yāgu (gruel to be eaten), bhoggamaññaṃ (another thing to be enjoyed).

31. Kicca ghacca bhacca bhabba leyyā.

31. Kicca, ghacca, bhacca, bhabba, and leyya.

Ete saddā yappaccayantā nipaccante.

These words, ending with the suffix ya, are irregularly formed.

32. Guhādīhi yaka.

32. From the guh group of roots, the suffix yaka.

Gutādīhi kriyattehi bhāvakammesu yaka hoti. Guyhaṃ, duyhaṃ, sisso. Siddhā evete tabbādayo pesātisaggapattakālesupi gamyamānesu sāmaññenavidhānato, tvayā khalu kaṭo kattabbo, karaṇīyo, kāriyo, kicco, evaṃ tvayā kaṭo kattabbo, bhotā kaṭo kattabbo, bhoto hi patto kālo kaṭakaraṇe. Evaṃ uddhamohuttikepi vattamānato pesādīsu siddhā eva. Tathā arahe kattari sattivisiṭṭhe ca patīyamāne āvassakādhamīṇatāvisiṭṭhe ca bhāvādo siddhā, uddhaṃmuhuttato-bhotā kaṭo kattabbo, bhotā rajjaṃ kattabbaṃ. Bhavaṃ araho, bhotā sāro vahitabbo, bhavaṃ sakko, bhotā avassaṃ kaṭo kattabbo, bhotā nikkho dātabbo.

From the guh group of roots, the suffix yaka occurs in the impersonal and passive senses. For example: guyhaṃ (to be hidden), duyhaṃ (to be milked), sisso (a pupil). These suffixes, tabba and so forth, are indeed established even when command, permission, or opportune time are understood, due to their general prescription. For instance: 'Indeed, the mat is to be made by you,' 'it is to be done,' 'it is to be performed,' 'it is a duty.' Thus: 'the mat is to be made by you'; 'the mat is to be made by you, sir'; 'for you, sir, the time has come for making the mat.' In this way, they are established in the sense of command and so forth, even when referring to the immediate future. Likewise, they are established in the impersonal sense and so forth when a worthy agent distinguished by power is understood, and also when one distinguished by necessity or obligation is understood. From the next moment onwards: 'the mat is to be made by you, sir'; 'the kingdom is to be ruled by you, sir.' 'You, sir, are worthy; the essence is to be borne by you, sir.' 'You, sir, are able; the mat must necessarily be made by you, sir.' 'A gold coin is to be given by you, sir.'

33. Kattari ltuṇakā.

33. In the agentive sense, the suffixes ltu, ṇa, and ka.

Kattari kārake kriyatthā ltuṇakā honti bahulaṃ. Paṭhitā, pāṭhako. Bahulamitveva? Pādehi harīyatīti pādahā-rako[M 0.0183], gale cuppateti galecopako. Siddhova ltu, arahe sīlasādhudhammesu ca sāmaññavihitattā, bhavaṃ khalu kaññāya pariggahitā, bhavametaṃ arahati. Sīlādīsu-khalvapi upādātā kumārake, gantā khelaṃ, muṇḍayitāro sāviṭṭhāyanā vadhuṃ katapariggahaṃ.

In the agentive case, the suffixes ltu, ṇa, and ka frequently occur after roots. For example: paṭhitā (a reciter), pāṭhako (a reciter). Why 'frequently'? For example: 'one who carries with the feet' is pādahāraka; 'one who kisses on the neck' is galecopaka. The suffix ltu is indeed established in the sense of 'worthy' and in cases of habit, nature, and skill, due to its general prescription. For example: 'Indeed, sir, you are to be accepted by the maiden; you, sir, are worthy of this.' Also in the sense of habit and so forth: 'one who takes up the boy' (upādātā kumārake); 'one who goes to play' (gantā khelaṃ); 'the Sāviṭṭhāyanas are those who shave a bride whose marriage has been performed' (muṇḍayitāro sāviṭṭhāyanā vadhuṃ katapariggahaṃ).

34. Āvī.

34. The suffix āvī.

Kriyatthā āvī hoti bahulaṃ kattari. Bhayadassāvī. Appavisayataññāpanatthaṃ bhinnayogakaraṇaṃ, sāmaññavihitattā sīlā dīsu ca hoteva.

The suffix āvī frequently occurs after a root in the agentive sense. For example: bhayadassāvī (one who sees danger). The splitting of the rule is for the purpose of indicating its limited scope. Due to its general prescription, it also occurs in the sense of habit and so forth.

35. Āsiṃsāyamako.

35. In the sense of blessing, the suffix ako.

Āsiṃsāyaṃ gamyamānāyaṃ kriyatthā ako hoti kattari. Jīvatūti jīvako, nandatūti nandako, bhavatūti bhavako.

When a blessing is understood, the suffix ako occurs after a root in the agentive sense. For example: from 'may he live' (jīvatu) comes jīvako; from 'may he rejoice' (nandatu) comes nandako; from 'may he be' (bhavatu) comes bhavako.

36. Karā ṇano.

36. From the root kar, the suffix ṇa.

Karato kattari ṇano hoti. Karotīti kāraṇaṃ, kattarīti kiṃ? Karaṇaṃ.

From the root kar, the suffix ṇa occurs in the agentive sense. For example: 'one who does' is kāraṇaṃ. Why is 'in the agentive sense' specified? To distinguish it from karaṇaṃ (instrument).

37. Hāto vīhikālesu.

37. From the root hā, in the sense of rice and time.

Hāto vīhismiṃ kāle ca ṇano hoti kattari. Hāyanā nāma vihayo, hāyano saṃvaccharo, vīhikālesūti kiṃ? Hātā.

From the root hā, the suffix ṇa occurs in the agentive sense when meaning rice and time. Hāyanā is a name for a type of rice; hāyano is a year. Why is 'in the sense of rice and time' specified? To form hātā (one who abandons).

38. Vidā kū.

38. From the root vid, the suffix kū.

Vidasmā kū hoti kattari. Vidū, lokavidū.

From the root vid, the suffix kū occurs in the agentive sense. For example: vidū (a wise one), lokavidū (a knower of the world).

39. Vito ñāto.

39. From `ñā` preceded by `vi`.

Vipubbā [M 0.0184] ñāiccasmā kū hoti kattari. Viññū. Vitoti kiṃ? Paññā.

From the root `ñā` preceded by `vi`, the suffix `kū` occurs in the agentive sense. For example, `viññū` (the discerning one). Why 'preceded by `vi`'? For `paññā` (wisdom).

40. Kammā.

40. From `kamma`.

Kammato parā ñāiccasmā kū hoti kattari. Sabbaññū, kālaññū.

From the root `ñā` following a `kamma` (object), the suffix `kū` occurs in the agentive sense. For example, `sabbaññū` (the All-Knowing One), `kālaññū` (the Knower of Time).

41. Kvacaṇa.

41. The suffix `aṇa`, sometimes.

Kammato parā kriyatthā kvaci aṇa hoti kattari. Kumbhakāro, saralāvo, mantajjhāyo, bahulādhikārā idha na hoti ādiccaṃ passati, himavantaṃ suṇoti, gāmaṃ gacchati. Kvacīti kiṃ? Kammakaro.

From a root denoting action, following a `kamma` (object), the suffix `aṇa` sometimes occurs in the agentive sense. For example, `kumbhakāro` (potter), `saralāvo` (arrow-maker), `mantajjhāyo` (mantra reciter). By the governing rule, it does not occur here: `ādiccaṃ passati` (he sees the sun), `himavantaṃ suṇoti` (he hears of the Himālaya), `gāmaṃ gacchati` (he goes to the village). Why 'sometimes'? For `kammakaro` (a worker).

42. Gamā rū.

42. The suffix `rū` from the root `gam`.

Kammato parā gamā rū hoti kattari. Vedagū pāragū.

From the root `gam` following a `kamma` (object), the suffix `rū` occurs in the agentive sense. For example, `vedagū` (knower of the Vedas), `pāragū` (one who has gone beyond).

43. Samānañña bhavanta yāditū-pamānā disā kamme rīrikkhakā.

43. From the root `dis` following the words of comparison `samāna`, `añña`, `bhavanta`, `yādi`, etc., the suffixes `rī`, `rikkha`, and `ka` occur in the objective sense.

Samānādīhi yādīhi copamānehi parā disā kammakārake rīrikkhakā honti. Samāno viya dissatīti sadī sadikkho sadiso. Aññādī aññādikkho aññādiso. Bhavādī bhavādikkho bhavādiso. Yādī yādikkho yādiso. Tyādī tyādikkho tyādiso. Samānādīhīti kiṃ? Rukkho viya dissati. Upamānāti kiṃ? So dissati. Kammeti kiṃ? So [M 0.0185] viya passati. Rakārā antasarādilopatthā, kakāro ekārābhāvattho.

Following the words of comparison `samāna`, etc., and `yādi`, etc., the suffixes `rī`, `rikkha`, and `ka` are applied to the root `dis` in the objective case. For example, `samāno viya dissatīti sadī, sadikkho, sadiso` (one who appears like the same). `Aññādī, aññādikkho, aññādiso` (one who appears like another). `Bhavādī, bhavādikkho, bhavādiso` (one who appears like you, sir). `Yādī, yādikkho, yādiso` (one who appears of which kind). `Tyādī, tyādikkho, tyādiso` (one who appears of that kind). Why 'from `samāna`, etc.'? For `Rukkho viya dissati` (He appears like a tree). Why 'words of comparison'? For `So dissati` (He is seen). Why 'in the objective case'? For `So viya passati` (He sees as if). The letter `r` is for the purpose of eliding the final vowel, etc.; the letter `k` is for the purpose of preventing the vowel `e`.

44. Bhāvakārakesva-ghaṇa ghakā.

44. The suffixes `a`, `ghaṇa`, `gha`, and `ka` in the sense of `bhāva` and `kāraka`.

Bhāve kārake ca kriyatthā a ghaṇa gha kā honti bahulaṃ. A-paggaho, niggaho, karo, garo, cayo, jayo, ravo, bhavo, paco, vaco, annado, purindado, īsakkaro, dukkaro, sukaro. Ghaṇa-bhāve pāko, cāgo, bhāvo, kārakepi saññāyaṃ tāva pajjatenenāti pādo, rujatīti rogo, visatīti veso, sarati kālantaranti sāro thiraṃso, darīyante etehīti dārā, jīrayati etenāti jāro, asaññāyampi dāyo datto, lābho laddho, gha-vako, nipako, ka-piyo, khipo, bhujo, āyudhaṃ.

In the sense of `bhāva` (state) and `kāraka` (case-relation), from a root denoting action, the suffixes `a`, `ghaṇa`, `gha`, and `ka` occur frequently. With `a`: `paggaho` (grasping), `niggaho` (restraint), `karo` (doer), `garo` (poison), `cayo` (accumulation), `jayo` (victory), `ravo` (sound), `bhavo` (existence), `paco` (cooking), `vaco` (speech), `annado` (giver of food), `purindado` (giver of cities), `īsakkaro` (easy to do), `dukkaro` (difficult to do), `sukaro` (easy to do). With `ghaṇa` in the sense of `bhāva`: `pāko` (cooking), `cāgo` (relinquishing), `bhāvo` (being). Also in the sense of `kāraka`, as specific terms: `pajjatenenāti pādo` (that by which one goes is a foot), `rujatīti rogo` (that which afflicts is a disease), `visatīti veso` (that which one enters is a house), `sarati kālantaranti sāro` (that which endures for another time is the essence), `thiraṃso` (a firm part), `darīyante etehīti dārā` (those by whom one is torn are wives), `jīrayati etenāti jāro` (he by whom one is worn out is a paramour). Also when not a specific term: `dāyo` (a gift), `datto` (given), `lābho` (gain), `laddho` (obtained). With `gha`: `vako` (wolf), `nipako` (prudent). With `ka`: `piyo` (dear), `khipo` (throwing), `bhujo` (arm), `āyudhaṃ` (weapon).

45. Dādhātvi.

45. The suffix `i` from the roots `dā` and `dhā`.

Dādhāhi bahulami hoti bhāvakārakesu. Ādi, nidhi, vālami.

From the roots `dā` and `dhā`, the suffix `i` frequently occurs in the sense of `bhāva` and `kāraka`. For example, `ādi` (beginning), `nidhi` (treasure), `vāladhi` (tail).

46. Vamādīyyathu.

46. The suffix `athu` from `vam` and other roots.

Vamādīhi bhāvakārakesvathu hoti. Vamathu, vepathu, (avathu, sayathu).

From `vam` and other roots, the suffix `athu` occurs in the sense of `bhāva` and `kāraka`. For example, `vamathu` (vomiting), `vepathu` (trembling), (`avathu`, `sayathu`).

47. Kvi.

47. The suffix `kvi`.

Kriyatthā [M 0.0186] kvi hoti bahulaṃ bhāvakārakesu. Kakāro kānubandhakāriyattho, abhibhū, sayambhū, bhattaggaṃ, (dānaggaṃ) salākaggaṃ, sabhā, pabhā.

From a root denoting action, the suffix `kvi` frequently occurs in the sense of `bhāva` and `kāraka`. The letter `k` is for the purpose of the function of the `ka` anubandha. For example, `abhibhū` (overpowering), `sayambhū` (self-existent), `bhattaggaṃ` (the best meal), `(dānaggaṃ)` (the best gift), `salākaggaṃ` (the best ticket-food), `sabhā` (assembly), `pabhā` (radiance).

48. Ano.

48. The suffix `ana`.

Kriyattā bhāvakārakesvano hoti. Gamanaṃ, dānaṃ, sampadānaṃ, apādānaṃ, adhikaraṇaṃ, calano, jalano, kodhano, kopano, maṇḍano, bhūsano.

From a root denoting action, the suffix `ana` occurs in the sense of `bhāva` and `kāraka`. For example, `gamanaṃ` (going), `dānaṃ` (giving), `sampadānaṃ` (dative case), `apādānaṃ` (ablative case), `adhikaraṇaṃ` (locative case), `calano` (moving), `jalano` (burning), `kodhano` (an angry person), `kopano` (an irritable person), `maṇḍano` (adornment), `bhūsano` (ornament).

49. Itthiyamaṇa tti ka yaka yā ca.

49. In the feminine: the suffixes `a`, `ṇa`, `tti`, `ka`, `yaka`, and `yā`.

Itthiliṅge bhāve kārake ca kriyatthā aādayo honti ano ca bahulaṃ. A titikkhā, vīmaṃsā, jigucchā, pipāsā, puttiyā īhā bhikkhā, āpadā, medhā, godhā, ṇakārā, hārā, tārā, dhārā, ārā, kti-iṭṭhi, siṭṭhi, bhitti, bhatti, tanti bhūti, ka-guhā, rujā, mudā, yaka-vijjā, ijjā, ya-seyyā, samajjā, pabbajjā, paricariyā, jāgariyā, anakāraṇā, hāraṇā, vedanā, vandanā, upāsanā.

In the feminine gender, in the sense of `bhāva` and `kāraka`, from a root denoting action, the suffixes `a`, etc., and `ana` frequently occur. With `a`: `titikkhā` (patience), `vīmaṃsā` (investigation), `jigucchā` (revulsion), `pipāsā` (thirst), `puttiyā` (desire for a son), `īhā` (effort), `bhikkhā` (alms), `āpadā` (misfortune), `medhā` (wisdom), `godhā` (iguana). With `ṇa`: `kārā` (action), `hārā` (carrying), `tārā` (crossing over), `dhārā` (stream), `ārā` (sharp point). With `kti`: `iṭṭhi` (wish), `siṭṭhi` (creation), `bhitti` (wall), `bhatti` (devotion), `tanti` (lineage, tradition), `bhūti` (prosperity). With `ka`: `guhā` (cave), `rujā` (pain), `mudā` (joy). With `yaka`: `vijjā` (knowledge), `ijjā` (sacrifice). With `ya`: `seyyā` (bed), `samajjā` (assembly), `pabbajjā` (going forth), `paricariyā` (service), `jāgariyā` (vigil). With `ana`: `kāraṇā` (cause), `hāraṇā` (carrying), `vedanā` (feeling), `vandanā` (veneration), `upāsanā` (attendance).

50. Jāhāhi ni.

50. The suffix `ni` from the roots `jā` and `hā`.

Jāhāiccetehi ni hotitthiyaṃ. Jāni, hāni.

From these roots `jā` and `hā`, the suffix `ni` occurs in the feminine gender. For example, `jāni` (loss, decay), `hāni` (loss, decrease).

51. Karā ririyo.

51. The suffixes `ri` and `riya` from the root `kar`.

Karato ririyo hotitthiyaṃ. Karaṇaṃ kiriyā. Kathaṃ ‘kriyā’ti? “Kriyāyaṃ”ti nipātanā.

From the root `kar`, the suffixes `ri` and `riya` occur in the feminine gender. The act of doing is `kiriyā`. How is it `kriyā`? It is by special ruling in the case of `kriyā`.

52. Ikitī sarūpe.

52. The suffixes `iki` and `tī` when denoting a word's own form.

Kriyatthassa [M 0.0187] sarūpe-bhidheyye kriyatthā pare ikitī honti, vaci, yudhi, pacati, ‘akāro kakāro’ti ādīsu kārasaddena samāso, yathā evakāroti.

When the own form of a word denoting action is to be expressed, the suffixes `iki` and `tī` occur after that word. For example: `vaci`, `yudhi`, `pacati`. In examples such as `akāro` and `kakāro`, there is a compound with the word `kāra`, as in `evakāro`.

53. Sīlābhikkhaññā-vassakesu ṇī.

53. The suffix `ṇī` in the sense of habit, repetition, and necessity.

Kriyatthā ṇī hoti sīlādīsu patīyamānesu, uṇhabhojī, khīrapāyī, avassakārī, satandāyī.

From a root denoting action, the suffix `ṇī` occurs when habit and so forth are understood. For example: `uṇhabhojī` (one who is in the habit of eating warm food), `khīrapāyī` (one who is in the habit of drinking milk), `avassakārī` (one who necessarily acts), `satandāyī` (one who constantly gives).

54. Thāvarittara bhaṅgura bhidura bhāsura bhassarā.

54. Firm, fleeting, fragile, radiant, gleaming.

Ete saddā nipaccante sīle gamyamāne.

These words are irregularly formed in the sense of habit.

55. Kattari bhūte ktavantu ktāvī.

55. The affixes -tavant and -tāvin are used in the agentive sense in the past tense.

Bhūte-tthe vattamānato kriyatthā ktavantuttāvī honti kattari. Vijitavā, vijitāvī, bhūteti adhikāro yāva “āhāratthā”ti (5-60).

In the past sense, from the verbal stem, the affixes -tavant and -tāvin occur in the agentive sense. Examples: 'vijitavā' (one who has conquered), 'vijitāvī' (one who has conquered). The governing rule 'bhūte' (in the past tense) extends up to 'āhāratthā' (5-60).

56. Ktobhāvakammesu.

56. The affix -ta is used in the sense of state and object.

Bhāve kamme ca bhūte kto hoti. Āsitaṃ bhavatā. Kato kaṭo bhavatā.

The affix -ta occurs in the sense of state and object in the past tense. Examples: 'Āsitaṃ bhavatā' (It was sat by you). 'Kato kaṭo bhavatā' (The mat was made by you).

57. Kattari cārambhe.

57. And in the agentive sense at the commencement of an action.

Kriyārambhe kattari kto hoti yathāpattañca. Pakato bhavaṃ kaṭaṃ, pakato kaṭo bhavatā, pasutto bhavaṃ, pasuttaṃ bhavatā.

At the commencement of an action, the affix -ta occurs in the agentive sense, and also as appropriate. Examples: 'Pakato bhavaṃ kaṭaṃ' (You began to make the mat), 'pakato kaṭo bhavatā' (The mat was begun to be made by you), 'pasutto bhavaṃ' (You began to sleep), 'pasuttaṃ bhavatā' (Sleeping was begun by you).

58. Ṭhā-sa vasa silisa sī ruha jara janīhi.

58. From the roots ṭhā (to stand), āsa (to sit), vasa (to dwell), silisa (to cling), sī (to lie down), ruha (to grow), jara (to age), and janī (to be born).

Ṭhādīhi [M 0.0188] kattari kto hoti yathāpattañca. Upaṭṭhito guruṃ bhavaṃ, upaṭṭhito guru bhotā, upāsito guruṃ bhavaṃ, upāsito guru bhotā, anuvusito guruṃ bhavaṃ, anuvusito guru bhotā, āsiliṭṭho guruṃ bhavaṃ, āsiliṭṭho guru bhotā, adhissito khaṭopikaṃ bhavaṃ, adhissitā khaṭopikā bhotā, āraḷho rukkhaṃ bhavaṃ, āruḷho rukkho bhotā, anujiṇṇo vasaliṃ devadatto, anujiṇṇā vasalī devadattena, anujāto māṇavako māṇavikaṃ, anujātā māṇavikā māṇavakena.

From the roots beginning with ṭhā, the affix -ta occurs in the agentive sense, and also as appropriate. Examples: 'Upaṭṭhito guruṃ bhavaṃ' (You attended upon the teacher), 'upaṭṭhito guru bhotā' (The teacher was attended upon by you). 'Upāsito guruṃ bhavaṃ' (You served the teacher), 'upāsito guru bhotā' (The teacher was served by you). 'Anuvusito guruṃ bhavaṃ' (You dwelt near the teacher), 'anuvusito guru bhotā' (The teacher was dwelt near by you). 'Āsiliṭṭho guruṃ bhavaṃ' (You clung to the teacher), 'āsiliṭṭho guru bhotā' (The teacher was clung to by you). 'Adhissito khaṭopikaṃ bhavaṃ' (You lay upon the small couch), 'adhissitā khaṭopikā bhotā' (The small couch was lain upon by you). 'Āruḷho rukkhaṃ bhavaṃ' (You climbed the tree), 'āruḷho rukkho bhotā' (The tree was climbed by you). 'Anujiṇṇo vasaliṃ devadatto' (Devadatta followed the outcaste woman in aging), 'anujiṇṇā vasalī devadattena' (The outcaste woman was followed in aging by Devadatta). 'Anujāto māṇavako māṇavikaṃ' (The young man was born after the maiden), 'anujātā māṇavikā māṇavakena' (The maiden was followed in birth by the young man).

59. Gamanatthākammakādhāre ca.

59. And also in the sense of location for verbs of motion and intransitive verbs.

Gamanatthato akammakato ca kriyatthā ādhāre kto hoti kattari ca yathāpattañca, idamesaṃ yātaṃ, iha te yātā, iha tehi yātaṃ, ayaṃ tehi yāto patho, idamesamāsitaṃ, iha te āsitā, ihatehi āsitaṃ, ‘devo ce vuṭṭho sampannā sālayo’ti kāraṇasāmaggīsampatti etthābhimatā.

From verbs of motion and intransitive verbs, the affix -ta occurs in the sense of location and in the agentive sense, and also as appropriate. Examples: 'idamesaṃ yātaṃ' (this is their place of going), 'iha te yātā' (here they have gone), 'iha tehi yātaṃ' (here it was gone by them), 'ayaṃ tehi yāto patho' (this is the path gone by them). 'Idamesamāsitaṃ' (this is their place of sitting), 'iha te āsitā' (here they have sat), 'ihatehi āsitaṃ' (here it was sat by them). The statement 'devo ce vuṭṭho sampannā sālayo' (If the god has rained, the rice crops are abundant) implies the attainment of a combination of causes.

60. Āhāratthā.

60. From roots having the sense of consuming.

Ajjhohāratthā ādhāre kto hoti yathāpattañca, idamesaṃ bhuttaṃ, idamesaṃ pītaṃ, iha tehi bhuttaṃ, iha tehi pītaṃ, odano tehi bhutto pītamudakaṃ, akattattho yogavibhāgo, kathaṃ ‘pītā gāvo’ti? Pītamesaṃ vijjatīti pītā, bāhulakā vā, ‘passinno’ti yā ettha bhūtakālatā, tatra tto, evaṃ raññaṃ mato raññaṃ iṭṭho, raññaṃ buddho, raññaṃ pūjito, evaṃ [M 0.0189] sīlito, rakkhito, khanto, ākuṭṭho, ruṭṭho, rusito, abhibyāhaṭo, dayiyo, haṭṭho, kantā, saṃyato, amato, ‘kaṭṭha’nti bhūtatāyameva hetuno, phalaṃ tvatra bhāvi.

From roots with the sense of consuming, the affix -ta occurs in the sense of location, and also as appropriate. Examples: 'idamesaṃ bhuttaṃ' (this is their place of eating), 'idamesaṃ pītaṃ' (this is their place of drinking), 'iha tehi bhuttaṃ' (here it was eaten by them), 'iha tehi pītaṃ' (here it was drunk by them). 'Odano tehi bhutto' (rice was eaten by them), 'pītamudakaṃ' (water was drunk). The separation of the rule is for the non-agentive sense. How is 'pītā gāvo' (cows that have drunk) explained? 'Pītā' means that drinking exists for them, or it is by frequent usage. In 'passinno' (sweated), the past tense here is from the affix -ta. Similarly, 'raññaṃ mato' (considered by the king), 'raññaṃ iṭṭho' (dear to the king), 'raññaṃ buddho' (known to the king), 'raññaṃ pūjito' (honored by the king). Likewise, 'sīlito' (observed), 'rakkhito' (protected), 'khanto' (forgiven), 'ākuṭṭho' (reviled), 'ruṭṭho' (angered), 'rusito' (angered), 'abhibyāhaṭo' (spoken against), 'dayiyo' (to be pitied), 'haṭṭho' (delighted), 'kantā' (a desired woman), 'saṃyato' (restrained), 'amato' (deathless). The word 'kaṭṭhaṃ' (misery) is used in the sense of pastness as a cause, but the result here is future.

61. Tuṃ tāye tave bhāve bhavissati kriyāyaṃ tadatthāya.

61. The affixes -tuṃ, -tāye, and -tave are used in the sense of state, in the future tense, for an action, for that purpose.

Bhavissati atthe vattamānato kriyatthā bhāve tuṃ tāye tave honti kriyāyaṃ tadatthāyaṃ patīyamānāyaṃ. Kātuṃ gacchati, kattāye gacchati, kātave gacchati, icchati bhottuṃ kāmeti bhottunti imīnāva siddhaṃ, punabbidhāne tvihāpi siyā ‘icchanto karotī’ti, evaṃ sakkoti bhottuṃ, jānāti bhottuṃ, gilāyati bhottuṃ, ghaṭate bhottuṃ, ārabhate bhottuṃ, labhate bhottuṃ, pakkamati bhottuṃ, ussahati bhottuṃ, arahati bhottuṃ, atthi bhottuṃ, vijjati bhottuṃ, vaṭṭa tibhottuṃ, kappati bhottunti. Tathā pārayati bhottuṃ, pahu bhottuṃ, samattho bhottuṃ, pariyatto bhottuṃ, alaṃ bhottunti bhavatissa sabbattha sambhavā. Tathā kālo bhottuṃ. Samayo bhotuṃ, velā bhotunti, yathā bhottuṃmano, sottuṃ soto, daṭṭhuṃ cakkhu, yujjhituṃ dhanu, vattuṃ jaḷo, gantumano, kattumalasoti, uccāraṇantu vattāyattaṃ. Bhāveti kiṃ? Karissāmīti gacchati, kriyāyanti kiṃ? Bhikkhissaṃ iccassa jaṭā, tadatthāyanti kiṃ? Gacchissato te bhavissati bhattaṃ bhojanāya.

In the future sense, from the verbal stem, the affixes -tuṃ, -tāye, and -tave occur in the sense of state for an action, when that purpose is understood. Examples: 'Kātuṃ gacchati' (He goes to do), 'kattāye gacchati' (He goes for doing), 'kātave gacchati' (He goes to do). It is already established by this rule for verbs like 'icchati bhottuṃ' (he desires to eat) and 'kāmeti bhottuṃ' (he wishes to eat); however, by stating the rule again, it might also apply here in cases like 'icchanto karotī' (desiring, he does). Similarly, 'sakkoti bhottuṃ' (he is able to eat), 'jānāti bhottuṃ' (he knows how to eat), 'gilāyati bhottuṃ' (he is weary of eating), 'ghaṭate bhottuṃ' (he strives to eat), 'ārabhate bhottuṃ' (he begins to eat), 'labhate bhottuṃ' (he obtains to eat), 'pakkamati bhottuṃ' (he departs to eat), 'ussahati bhottuṃ' (he endeavors to eat), 'arahati bhottuṃ' (he deserves to eat), 'atthi bhottuṃ' (there is to eat), 'vijjati bhottuṃ' (it is found to eat), 'vaṭṭati bhottuṃ' (it is proper to eat), 'kappati bhottuṃ' (it is fit to eat). Likewise, 'pārayati bhottuṃ' (he is capable of eating), 'pahu bhottuṃ' (he is able to eat), 'samattho bhottuṃ' (he is capable of eating), 'pariyatto bhottuṃ' (he is sufficient to eat), 'alaṃ bhottuṃ' (he is able to eat)—since 'bhavati' (it is) is possible everywhere. Similarly, 'kālo bhottuṃ' (it is time to eat), 'samayo bhottuṃ' (it is the occasion to eat), 'velā bhottuṃ' (it is the moment to eat). As in 'bhottuṃmano' (a mind to eat), 'sottuṃ soto' (an ear to hear), 'daṭṭhuṃ cakkhu' (an eye to see), 'yujjhituṃ dhanu' (a bow to fight), 'vattuṃ jaḷo' (a dull person to speak), 'gantumano' (a mind to go), 'kattum alaso' (lazy to do). The pronunciation, however, depends on the speaker. Why 'in the sense of state'? [To prevent it from applying in] 'He goes, thinking, "I will do"'. Why 'for an action'? [To prevent it from applying in] 'His matted hair is for the purpose of thinking, "I will beg"'. Why 'for that purpose'? [To prevent it from applying in] 'For you who will go, there will be food for eating'.

62. Paṭisedhe-laṃkhalūnaṃ tuna tvāna tvā vā.

62. When 'alaṃ' and 'khalu' are used in prohibition, the affixes -tuna, -tvāna, and -tvā are used optionally.

Alaṃ [M 0.0190] khalusaddānaṃ paṭisedhatthānaṃ payoge tunādayo vā honti bhāve. Alaṃ sotuna, khalu sotuna, alaṃ sutvāna, dhalu sutvāna, alaṃ sutvā, khalu sutvā, alaṃ sutena, khalu sotena, alaṃ khalūnanti kiṃ? Mā hotu, paṭisedheti kiṃ? Alaṅkāro.

When the words 'alaṃ' and 'khalu' are used in the sense of prohibition, the affixes beginning with -tuna are optionally used in the sense of state. Examples: 'Alaṃ sotuna' (Enough of hearing), 'khalu sotuna' (Indeed, enough of hearing), 'alaṃ sutvāna' (Enough having heard), 'khalu sutvāna' (Indeed, enough having heard), 'alaṃ sutvā' (Enough having heard), 'khalu sutvā' (Indeed, enough having heard), 'alaṃ sutena' (Enough with hearing), 'khalu sotena' (Indeed, enough with hearing). Why 'alaṃ' and 'khalu'? [To prevent it from applying in] 'Mā hotu' (Let it not be). Why 'in prohibition'? [To prevent it from applying in] 'Alaṅkāro' (An ornament).

63. Pubbekakatthukānaṃ.

63. Of actions with a single agent, the prior one.

Eko kattā yesaṃ byāpārānaṃ, tesu yo pubbo, tadatthato kriyatthā tunādayo honti bhāve, sotuna yāti, sutvāna, sutvā vā, ekakattukānantikiṃ? Bhuttasmiṃ devadatte yaññadatto vajati, pubbāti kiṃ? Bhuñjabhi ca pacati ca. ‘Appatvā nadiṃ pabbato atikkamma pabbataṃ nadī’ti bhūdhātussa sabbattha sambhavā ekakattukatā pubbakālatā ca gamyate. ‘Bhutvā bhutvā gacchatīti’ imināva siddhaṃ ābhikkhaññantu dvibbacanāvagamyate. Kathaṃ ‘jīvaggāhaṃ agāhayi, kāyappacālakaṃ gacchantī’ti ādi? Ghaṇantena kriyāvisesanena siddhaṃ yathā ‘odanapākaṃ sayatī’ti.

When there is a single agent for several actions, the affixes beginning with -tuna occur in the sense of state after the root denoting the prior action. Examples: 'sotuna yāti' (He goes having heard), 'sutvāna' (having heard), or 'sutvā' (having heard). Why 'with a single agent'? [To prevent it from applying in] 'Bhuttasmiṃ devadatte yaññadatto vajati' (When Devadatta has eaten, Yaññadatta goes). Why 'prior'? [To prevent it from applying in] 'Bhuñjati ca pacati ca' (He eats and he cooks). In 'Appatvā nadiṃ pabbato atikkamma pabbataṃ nadī' (Not having reached the river, the mountain; having crossed the mountain, the river), the single-agent nature and prior action are understood due to the possibility of the root 'bhū' (to be) everywhere. The frequentative sense in 'Bhutvā bhutvā gacchati' (He goes having eaten repeatedly) is established by this same rule, and the repetition is understood by the reduplication. How are examples like 'jīvaggāhaṃ agāhayi' (He seized him alive) and 'kāyappacālakaṃ gacchantī' (going with a shaking body) explained? It is established by the adverb of action ending in -aṃ, as in 'odanapākaṃ sayati' (He sleeps while the rice is cooking).

64. Nto katthari vattamāne.

64. The affix -nta is used in the agentive sense in the present tense.

Vattamānatthe vattamānato kriyattā nto ho ti kattari, tiṭṭhanto.

In the present sense, from the verbal stem, the affix -nta occurs in the agentive sense. Example: 'tiṭṭhanto' (standing).

65. Māno.

65. The affix -māna.

Vattamānatthe vattamānato kriyatthā māno hoti, kattari. Tiṭṭhamāno.

In the present sense, from the verbal stem, the affix -māna occurs in the agentive sense. Example: 'tiṭṭhamāno' (standing).

66. Bhāvakammesu.

66. In the sense of state and object.

Vattamānatthe [M 0.0191] vattamānato kriṃyatthā bhāve kammeca māno hoti. Ṭhīyamānaṃ, paccamāno odano.

In the present sense, from the verbal stem, the affix -māna occurs in the sense of state and object. Examples: 'Ṭhīyamānaṃ' (being stood), 'paccamāno odano' (rice being cooked).

67. Te ssapubbānāgate.

67. Those two affixes, preceded by -ssa-, are used in the future tense.

Anāgatatthe vattamānato kriyatthā tentamānā ssapubbā honti. Ṭhassanto, ṭhassamāno, ṭhīyissamānaṃ, paccissamāno odano.

In the future sense, from the verbal stem, the affixes -nta and -māna, preceded by -ssa-, occur. Examples: 'Ṭhassanto' (one who will stand), 'ṭhassamāno' (one who will stand), 'ṭhīyissamānaṃ' (that which will be stood), 'paccissamāno odano' (rice that will be cooked).

68. Ṇvādayo.

68. The affixes beginning with ṇvu.

Kriyatthā pare bahulaṃ ṇvādayo honti. Cāru, dāru.

After a verbal root, the affixes beginning with ṇvu frequently occur. Examples: 'Cāru' (beautiful), 'dāru' (wood).

69. Khachasāna mekassarodi dve.

69. Of [roots ending in] kha, cha, and sa, the first vowel is doubled.

Khachasappaccayantānaṃ kriyatthānaṃ paṭhamekassaraṃ saddarūpaṃ dve bhavati. Titikkhā, jigucchā, vīmaṃsā.

Of verbal roots ending in the suffixes kha, cha, and sa, the first single-voweled word-form is doubled. Examples: Titikkhā (endurance), jigucchā (disgust), vīmaṃsā (investigation).

70. Parokkhāyañca.

70. And in the perfect tense.

Parokkhāyaṃ paṭhamekassaraṃ saddarūpaṃ dve bhavati. Jagāma, cakāro anuttasamuccayattho, tenaññatrāpi yathāgamaṃ, jahāti, jahitabbaṃ, jahituṃ, daddallati, caṅkamati. ‘Lolupo, momūhoti ottaṃ tadaminādipāṭhā.

In the perfect tense, the first single-voweled word-form is doubled. Example: Jagāma (he went). The particle 'ca' has the meaning of an unstated conjunction; therefore, elsewhere also, according to tradition, [this occurs], as in: jahāti (he abandons), jahitabbaṃ (to be abandoned), jahituṃ (to abandon), daddallati (it shines brightly), caṅkamati (he walks to and fro). The words lolupo (greedy) and momūho (greatly deluded) are from the reading beginning with 'amina'.

71. Ādismā sarā.

71. Of the initial vowels.

Ādibhūtā sarā paramekassaraṃ dve hoti, asisisati, ādismāti kiṃ? Jajagāra, sarāti kiṃ? Papāca.

The initial single-voweled part is doubled. Example: asisisati (he desires to eat). Why [the word] 'ādismā' (from the beginning)? [Consider] Jajagāra (he was awake). Why [the word] 'sarā' (vowels)? [Consider] Papāca (he cooked).

72. Na puna.

72. Not again.

Yaṃ [M 0.0192] dvibhūtaṃ, na taṃ puna dvittamāpajjate, titikkhisati, jigucchisati.

That which has been doubled does not become doubled again; for example, titikkhisati (he desires to endure), jigucchisati (he desires to despise).

73. Yathiṭṭhaṃ syādino.

73. For denominatives, as desired.

Syādyantassa yathiṭṭhamekassaramādibhūtamaññaṃ vā yathāgamaṃ dvittapajjate, puputtīyisati, putittīyisati, puttīyiyisati.

For that which ends in a denominative suffix, the initial single syllable, or another, is doubled as desired and according to tradition. Examples: puputtīyisati, putittīyisati, puttīyiyisati.

74. Rasso pubbassa.

74. The preceding [vowel] is shortened.

Dvitte pubbassa saro rasso hoti. Dadāti.

When doubled, the vowel of the preceding [syllable] becomes short. Example: Dadāti.

75. Lopo-nādibyañjanassa.

75. Elision of the non-initial consonant.

Dvitte pubbassādito-ññassa byañjanassa lopo hoti. Asisisati.

When doubled, the consonant of the preceding [syllable] other than the initial one is elided. Example: Asisisati.

76. Khachasesvassi.

76. Of 'a', there is 'i' in the presence of kha, cha, and sa.

Dvitte pubbassa assa i hoti khachasesu. Pipāsati, jighaṃsati, khachasesūti kiṃ? Jahāti, assāti kiṃ? Bubhukkhati.

When doubled, the 'a' of the preceding [syllable] becomes 'i' in the presence of kha, cha, or sa. Examples: Pipāsati, jighaṃsati. Why [the condition] 'khachasesu'? [Consider] Jahāti. Why [the word] 'assa'? [Consider] Bubhukkhati.

77. Gupissussa.

77. Of the 'u' of 'gup'.

Dvitte pubbassa gupissa ussa i hoti khachasesu, jigucchati.

When doubled, the 'u' of the preceding 'gup' becomes 'i' in the presence of kha, cha, or sa. Example: jigucchati.

78. Catutthadutiyānaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā.

78. For the fourth and second [consonants], the third and first [respectively].

Dvitte pubesaṃ catutthadutiyānaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā honti. Bubhukkhati, ciccheda.

When doubled, for the preceding fourth and second [consonants], the third and first occur respectively. Examples: Bubhukkhati, ciccheda.

79. Kavaggahānaṃ cavaggajā.

79. For the consonants of the k-class and for 'h', the consonants of the c-class and 'j' [are the substitutes].

Dvitte [M 0.0193] pubbesaṃ kavaggahānaṃ cavaggajā honti yathākkamaṃ. Cukopa, jahāti.

When doubled, for the preceding consonants of the k-class and for 'h', the consonants of the c-class and 'j' occur respectively. Examples: Cukopa, jahāti.

80. Mānassa vī parassa ca maṃ.

80. For 'māna', 'vī'; and for the following, 'maṃ'.

Dvitte pubbassa mānassa vī hoti parassa ca maṃ, vīmaṃsati.

When doubled, 'vī' is the substitute for the preceding 'māna', and 'maṃ' for the following [part of the root]. Example: vīmaṃsati.

81. Kitassāsaṃsaye ti vā.

81. For 'kita', 'ti' is the substitute optionally, in the sense of certainty (not-doubting).

Saṃsayaso-ññasmiṃ vattamānassa dvitte pubbassa kitassa vā ti hoti. Tikicchati, cikicchati, asaṃsayeti kiṃ? Vicikicchati.

When occurring in the sense of certainty (non-doubting), for the preceding 'kit' in doubling, 'ti' is the optional substitute. Examples: Tikicchati, Cikicchati. Why [the condition] 'asaṃsaye' (in certainty)? [Consider] Vicikicchati.

82. Yuvaṇṇānameo paccaye.

82. For the vowels i and u, 'e' and 'o' are the substitutes respectively when a suffix follows.

Ivaṇṇuvaṇṇantānaṃ kriyatthānaṃ eohonti yathākkamaṃ paccaye. Cetabbaṃ, netabbaṃ, sotabbaṃ, bhavitabbaṃ.

For verbal roots ending in the vowels i and u, 'e' and 'o' occur respectively when a suffix follows. Examples: Cetabbaṃ, netabbaṃ, sotabbaṃ, bhavitabbaṃ.

83. Lahussupantassa.

83. Of a light penultimate [vowel].

Lahubhūtassa upantassa yuvaṇṇassa eo honti yathākkamaṃ. Esitabbaṃ, kositabbaṃ, lahussāti kiṃ? Dhūpitā, upantassāti kiṃ? Rundhati.

For a light penultimate i- or u-vowel, 'e' and 'o' occur respectively. Examples: Esitabbaṃ, kositabbaṃ. Why [the condition] 'lahussa' (light)? [Consider] Dhūpitā. Why [the condition] 'upantassa' (penultimate)? [Consider] Rundhati.

84. Assā ṇānubandhe.

84. For 'a', 'ā' [is substituted] when a ṇ-anubandha [suffix] follows.

Ṇakārānubandhe paccaye pare upantassa akārassa ā hoti. Kārako.

When a suffix with 'ṇ' as an anubandha follows, the penultimate 'a' becomes 'ā'. (Example:) kārako.

85. Na te kānubandhanāgamesu.

85. Those [changes] do not occur in the case of k-anubandha [suffixes] and nāgama [augments].

Te [M 0.0194] eoā kānubandhe nāgame ca na honti. Cito, suto, diṭṭho, puṭṭho, nāgame ‘vanā’dinā (1.45) cinitabbaṃ, cinituṃ, suṇitabbaṃ, suṇituṃ pāpuṇitabbaṃ, pāpuṇituṃ, dhunitabbaṃ, dhunituṃ, dhunanaṃ, dhunayitabbaṃ, dhunāpetabbaṃ, dhunayituṃ dhunāpetuṃ, dhunayanaṃ, dhunāpanaṃ, dhunayati, dhunāpeti, pīnetabbaṃ, pīnayituṃ, pīnanaṃ, pīnituṃ, pīnayati, sunoti, sinoti, dunoti, hinoti, pahiṇithabbaṃ, pahiṇituṃ, pahiṇanaṃ.

Those changes, 'e', 'o', and 'ā', do not occur when a k-anubandha [suffix] or a nāgama [augment] follows. (Examples:) cito, suto, diṭṭho, puṭṭho. In the case of a nāgama [augment], as in 'vanādi' (1.45): cinitabbaṃ, cinituṃ, suṇitabbaṃ, suṇituṃ, pāpuṇitabbaṃ, pāpuṇituṃ, dhunitabbaṃ, dhunituṃ, dhunanaṃ, dhunayitabbaṃ, dhunāpetabbaṃ, dhunayituṃ, dhunāpetuṃ, dhunayanaṃ, dhunāpanaṃ, dhunayati, dhunāpeti, pīnetabbaṃ, pīnayituṃ, pīnanaṃ, pīnituṃ, pīnayati, sunoti, sinoti, dunoti, hinoti, pahiṇithabbaṃ, pahiṇituṃ, pahiṇanaṃ.

86. Vā kvaci.

86. Optionally, sometimes.

Te kvaci vā na honti kānubandhanāgamesu. Mudito, ruditaṃ, roditaṃ.

Those [changes] sometimes optionally do not occur in the case of k-anubandha [suffixes] and nāgama [augments]. (Examples:) mudito, ruditaṃ, roditaṃ.

87. Aññatrāpi.

87. Elsewhere also.

Kānubandhanāgamato-ññasmimpi te kvaci, nu honti. Khipako, panūdanaṃ, vadhako.

Even elsewhere than in the case of a k-anubandha [suffix] or a nāgama [augment], those [changes] sometimes do not occur. (Examples:) khipako, panūdanaṃ, vadhako.

88. Pye sissā.

88. For `sissa`, `ā` [is substituted] when `pya` follows.

Sissa ā hoti pyādese, nissāya.

The `a` of `sissa` becomes `ā` when `pya` is the substitute. (Example:) nissāya.

89. Eonamayavā sare.

89. For `e` and `o`, `ay` and `av` [are substituted] when a vowel follows.

Sare pare eonaṃ ayaavā honti. Jayo, bhavo, sarati kiṃ? Jeti, anubhoti.

When a vowel follows, `ay` and `av` are substituted for `e` and `o` respectively. (Examples:) jayo, bhavo. Why 'when a vowel follows' (sare)? (Examples:) jeti, anubhoti.

90. Āyāvā ṇānubandhe.

90. `Āy` and `āv` [are substituted for `e` and `o`] when a ṇ-anubandha [suffix] follows.

Eonaṃ [M 0.0195] āyāvā honti sarādo ṇānubandhe. Nāyayati, bhāvayati, ‘sayāpetvā’tiādīsu rassattaṃ.

For `e` and `o`, `āy` and `āv` are substituted when a vowel-initial ṇ-anubandha [suffix] follows. (Examples:) nāyayati, bhāvayati. In `sayāpetvā` and so on, shortening occurs.

91. Āssāṇāpimhi yuka.

91. After `ā`, the augment `yuk` [is inserted], except before `ṇāpi`.

Ākārantassa kriyatthassa yuka hoti ṇāpito-ññasmiṃ ṇānubandhe. Dāyako, ṇānubandhetveva? Dānaṃ, aṇāpimhīti kiṃ? Dāpayati.

For a verbal root ending in `ā`, the augment `yuk` is inserted when a ṇ-anubandha suffix other than `ṇāpi` follows. (Example:) dāyako. Why [the condition] 'when a ṇ-anubandha [suffix] follows'? (Example:) dānaṃ. Why [the condition] 'except before `ṇāpi`'? (Example:) dāpayati.

92. Padādīnaṃ kvaci.

92. For `pad` and other [roots], sometimes.

Padādīnaṃ yuka hoti kvaci. Nipajjitabbaṃ, nipajjituṃ nipajjanaṃ, pamajjitabbaṃ, pamajjituṃ, pamajjanaṃ, kvacīti kiṃ? Pādo.

For `pad` and other [roots], the augment `yuk` is sometimes inserted. (Examples:) nipajjitabbaṃ, nipajjituṃ, nipajjanaṃ, pamajjitabbaṃ, pamajjituṃ, pamajjanaṃ. Why 'sometimes' (kvaci)? (Example:) pādo.

93. Maṃ vā rudhādīnaṃ.

93. Optionally, a nasal infix (`ṃ`) [is inserted] in `rudh` and other [roots].

Rudhādīnaṃ kvaci maṃ vā hoti. Rundhituṃ, rujjhituṃ, kvacitveva? Nirodho.

For `rudh` and other [roots], the nasal infix `ṃ` is sometimes optionally inserted. (Examples:) rundhituṃ, rujjhituṃ. Why 'sometimes'? (Example:) nirodho.

94. Kvimhi lopo-ntabyañjanassa.

94. When the `kvi` [suffix] follows, there is elision of the final consonant.

Antabyañjanassa lopo hoti kvimhi. Bhattaṃ gasanti gaṇhanti vā etthāti bhattaggaṃ.

Elision of the final consonant occurs when the `kvi` [suffix] follows. (Example:) bhattaggaṃ, which is [derived from] 'bhattaṃ gasanti gaṇhanti vā etthā'ti' (a place where they eat or take food).

95. Pararūpamayakāre byañjane.

95. Assimilation to the following form [occurs] when a consonant other than `y` follows.

Kriyatthānamantabyañjanassa pararūpaṃ hoti yakārato-ññasmiṃ byañjane. Bhettabbaṃ, byañjaneti kiṃ? Bhinditabbaṃ, ayakāreti kiṃ? Bhijjati.

For the final consonant of a verbal root, assimilation to the following form occurs when a consonant other than `y` follows. (Example:) bhettabbaṃ. Why [the condition] 'when a consonant follows' (byañjane)? (Example:) bhinditabbaṃ. Why [the condition] 'other than `y`' (ayakāre)? (Example:) bhijjati.

96. Manānaṃ niggahītaṃ.

96. For `m` and `n`, niggahīta (`ṃ`) [is substituted].

Makāranakārantānaṃ [M 0.0196] kriyatthānaṃ niggahītaṃ hoti ayakāre byañjane. Gantabbaṃ, jaṅghā, byañjanetveva? Gamanaṃ, ayakāretveva? Gamyate.

For verbal roots ending in `m` or `n`, niggahīta (`ṃ`) is substituted when a consonant other than `y` follows. (Examples:) gantabbaṃ, jaṅghā. Why [the condition] 'when a consonant follows' (byañjane)? (Example:) gamanaṃ. Why [the condition] 'other than `y`' (ayakāre)? (Example:) gamyate.

97. Na brūsso.

97. Not for `brū`, `o`.

Brūssa o na hoti byañjane. Brūmi, byañjanetveva? Abravi.

For `brū`, `o` is not substituted when a consonant follows. (Example:) brūmi. Why [the condition] 'when a consonant follows' (byañjane)? (Example:) abravi.

98. Kagā cajānaṃ ghānubandhe.

98. `Ka` and `ga` [are substituted] for `ca` and `ja` respectively, when a gh-anubandha [suffix] follows.

Ghānubandhe cakārajakārantānaṃ kriyatthānaṃ kagā honti yathākkamaṃ. Vākyaṃ, bhāgyaṃ.

When a gh-anubandha [suffix] follows, for verbal roots ending in `ca` and `ja`, `ka` and `ga` are substituted respectively. (Examples:) vākyaṃ, bhāgyaṃ.

99. Hanassa ghāto ṇānubandhe.

99. For han, there is the substitution ghāta when ṇa is an indicatory letter.

Hanassa ghāto hoti ṇānubandhe. Āghāto.

For the root han, the substitution ghāta occurs when ṇa is an indicatory letter. For example: āghāto.

100. Kvimhi gho paripacca-samohi.

100. After pari, pacca, sam, o, and hi, gho is the substitute for han when the suffix kvi follows.

Payyādīhi parassa hanassa gho hoti kvimhi. Paligho, paṭigho, aghaṃ rassattaṃ nipātanā, saṅgho, ogho.

For the root han following pari and others, the substitution gho occurs when the suffix kvi follows. For example: paligho, paṭigho; aghaṃ is formed with shortening by special ruling; saṅgho, ogho.

101. Parassa ghaṃ se.

101. For the following root, there is the substitution ghaṃ when sa follows.

Dvitte parassa hanassa ghaṃ hoti se. Jighaṃsā.

In reduplication, for the following root han, the substitution ghaṃ occurs when sa follows. For example: jighaṃsā.

102. Jiharānaṃ gī.

102. For ji and har, there is the substitution gī.

Dvitte paresaṃ jitarānaṃ gī hoti se. Vijigīsā, jigīsā.

In reduplication, for the following roots ji and tar, the substitution gī occurs when sa follows. For example: vijigīsā, jigīsā.

103. Dhāssa ho.

103. For dhā, there is the substitution ho.

Dvitte [M 0.0197] parassa dhāssa ha hoti. Dahati.

In reduplication, for the following root dhā, the substitution ha occurs. For example: dahati.

104. Ṇimhi dīgho dusassa.

104. For dus, there is lengthening when ṇi follows.

Dusassa dīgho hoti ṇimhi. Dusito. Ṇimhīti kiṃ? Duṭṭho.

For the root dus, lengthening occurs when ṇi is present. For example: Dusito. Why is the condition 'when ṇi is present' stated? For the case of duṭṭho.

105. Guhissa sare.

105. For guh, [there is lengthening] when a vowel follows.

Guhissa dīgho hoti sare. Nigūhanaṃ sareti kiṃ? Guyhaṃ.

Lengthening occurs for guh when a vowel follows. For example: nigūhanaṃ. Why state 'when a vowel follows'? For the case of guyhaṃ.

106. Muhabahānañca te kānubandhe-tve.

106. And for muh and bah, [there is lengthening] before a suffix beginning with t or having k as an indicatory letter, except for tvā and tva.

Muhabahānaṃ guhissa ca dīgho hoti takārādo kānubandhe tvānatvāvajjite, mūḷho, bāḷho, gūḷho, teti kiṃ? Muyhati, kānubandheti-kiṃ? Muyhitabbaṃ, atveti kiṃ? Muyhitvāna, muyhitvā, ‘te kānubandhe-tve’ti ayamadhikāro yāva “sāsassa sisve”ti -117.

For muh, bah, and guh, lengthening occurs before a suffix beginning with the letter t or having k as an indicatory letter, excluding tvā and tva. For example: mūḷho, bāḷho, gūḷho. Why state 'beginning with t'? For the case of muyhati. Why state 'having k as an indicatory letter'? For the case of muyhitabbaṃ. Why state 'excluding tvā and tva'? For the cases of muyhitvāna and muyhitvā. This governing rule, 'te kānubandhe-tve', extends up to the rule 'sāsassa sisve'.

107. Vahassussa.

107. For the u of vah, [there is lengthening].

Vahassa ussa dīgho hoti te kānubandhe tvānatvāvajjite. Vuṭṭho.

For the u of vah, lengthening occurs before a suffix beginning with t or having k as an indicatory letter, excluding tvā and tva. For example: vuṭṭho.

108. Dhāssa hi.

108. For dhā, there is the substitution hi.

Dhā=dhāraṇetīmassa hi hoti te kānubandhe tvānatvāvajjite. Nihito, nihitavā.

For this root dhā in the sense of 'to hold', the substitution hi occurs before a suffix beginning with t or having k as an indicatory letter, excluding tvā and tva. For example: nihito, nihitavā.

109. Gamādirānaṃ lopo-ntassa.

109. For gam and others, there is elision of the final letter.

Gamādīnaṃ [M 0.0198] rakārantānaṃ ca antassa lopo hoti te kānubandhe tvānatvāvajjite. Gato, khato, hato, mato, tato, saññato, rato, kato, tetveva? Gamyate, kānubandhetveva? Gantabbaṃ, atvetveva? Gantvāna, gantvā.

For the roots gam and others, and for roots ending in ra, elision of the final letter occurs before a suffix beginning with t or having k as an indicatory letter, excluding tvā and tva. For example: gato, khato, hato, mato, tato, saññato, rato, kato. Why the condition 'beginning with t'? For the case of gamyate. Why 'having k as an indicatory letter'? For the case of gantabbaṃ. Why 'excluding tvā and tva'? For the cases of gantvāna and gantvā.

110. Vacādīnaṃ vassuṭa vā.

110. For vac and others, there is optionally the substitution uṭa for va.

Vacādīnaṃ vassa vā uṭa hoti kānubandhe-tve. Uttaṃ, vuttaṃ, uṭṭhaṃ, vuṭṭhaṃ, ‘atvetveva? Vatvāna, vatvā.

For the va of vac and others, the substitution uṭa optionally occurs before a suffix beginning with t or having k as an indicatory letter, excluding tvā and tva. For example: uttaṃ (or vuttaṃ), uṭṭhaṃ (or vuṭṭhaṃ). Why the condition 'excluding tvā and tva'? For the cases of vatvāna and vatvā.

111. Assu.

111. For a, there is the substitution u.

Vacādīnamassa u hoti kānubandhe-sve. Vuttaṃ, vuṭṭhaṃ.

For the a of vac and others, the substitution u occurs before a suffix with k as an indicatory letter, excluding sva. For example: vuttaṃ, vuṭṭhaṃ.

112. Vaddhassa vā.

112. For vaddh, it is optional.

Vaddhassa assa vā u hoti kānubandhe tve. Vuddho. Vaddho. Atvetveva? Vaddhitvāna, vaddhitvā, kathaṃ ‘vuttī’ti? “Vuttīmatte”ti 3-69. nipātanā, ‘vattī’ti hoteva yathālakkhaṇaṃ.

For the a of vaddh, the substitution u optionally occurs before a suffix beginning with t or having k as an indicatory letter, excluding tvā and tva. For example: vuddho or vaddho. Why the condition 'excluding tvā and tva'? For the cases of vaddhitvāna and vaddhitvā. How then is the form vuttī derived? It is by the special ruling in 'vuttīmatte'; the regular form would be vattī.

113. Yajassa yassa ṭiyī.

113. For the ya of yaj, there are the substitutions ṭi and ī.

Yajassa [M 0.0199] yassa ṭiyī honti kānubandhe-tve. Iṭṭhaṃ, yiṭṭhaṃ, atvetveva? Yajitvāna, yajitvā.

For the ya of yaj, the substitutions ṭi and ī occur before a suffix beginning with t or having k as an indicatory letter, excluding tvā and tva. For example: iṭṭhaṃ, yiṭṭhaṃ. Why the condition 'excluding tvā and tva'? For the cases of yajitvāna and yajitvā.

114. Ṭhāssi.

114. You will stand.

Ṭhāssi hoti kānubandhe-tve. Ṭhito, atvetveva? Ṭhatvāna, ṭhatvā.

Of [the root] ṭhā, ī occurs before a suffix with anubandha ka, but not before tva. [For example,] ṭhito. But what about before tva? [The forms are] ṭhatvāna, ṭhatvā.

115. Gāpānamī.

115. Of [the roots] gā and pā, ī [is substituted].

Gāpānamī hoti kānabandhe-tve. Gītaṃ, pītaṃ, atvetveva? Gāyitvā niccaṃ yāgamo, pāssa tu pītvāti bahulādhikārā.

Of [the roots] gā and pā, ī occurs before a suffix with anubandha ka and before tve. [For example,] gītaṃ, pītaṃ. But what about before tva? For [the root gā, the form is] gāyitvā; the augment yā is constant. But for [the root] pā, [the form is] pītvā, by the authority of the 'bahula' (variously) rule.

116. Janissā.

116. Of [the root] jan, ā [is substituted].

Janissa ā hoti kānubandhe-tve. Jāto. Atvetveva? Janitvā.

Of [the root] jan, ā occurs before a suffix with anubandha ka and before tve. [For example,] jāto. But what about before tva? [The form is] janitvā.

117. Sāsassa sisa vā.

117. Of [the root] sās, sisa [is substituted] optionally.

Sāsassa sisa vā hoti kānubandhe-tve. Siṭṭhaṃ, satthaṃ, sisso, sāsiyo atvetveva? Anusāsitvāna.

Of [the root] sās, sisa is optionally substituted before a suffix with anubandha ka and before tve. [For example,] siṭṭhaṃ, satthaṃ; sisso, sāsiyo. But what about before tva? [The form is] anusāsitvāna.

118. Karassā tave.

118. Of [the root] kar, ā [is substituted] before tave.

Karassa ā hoti tave. Kātave.

Of [the root] kar, ā occurs before tave. [For example,] kātave.

119. Tuṃtunatabbesu vā.

119. And optionally before [the suffixes] tuṃ, tuna, and tabba.

Tumādīsu vā karassā hoti. Kātuṃ kattuṃ, kātuna kattuna, kātabbaṃ kattabbaṃ.

Optionally, of [the root] kar, ā occurs before tuṃ and the other [such suffixes]. [For example,] kātuṃ, kattuṃ; kātuna, kattuna; kātabbaṃ, kattabbaṃ.

120. Ñāssa ne jā.

120. Of [the root] ñā, jā [is substituted] before na.

Ñādhātussa [M 0.0200] jā hoti nakāre. Jānituṃ, jānanto, neti kiṃ? Ñāto.

Of the root ñā, jā occurs when the letter na follows. [For example,] jānituṃ, jānanto. Why [the condition] 'before na'? [So that the form is] ñāto.

121. Sakāpānaṃ kukakū ṇe.

121. Of [the roots] sak and āp, [the augments] kukakū [are inserted] before ṇa.

Sakaāpānaṃ kukakuiccete āgamā honti ṇakāre. Sakkuṇanto, pāpuṇanto, sakkuṇoti, pāpuṇoti, ṇeti kiṃ? Sakkoti, pāpeti.

Of [the roots] sak and āp, these augments, kukaku, occur when the letter ṇa follows. [For example,] sakkuṇanto, pāpuṇanto, sakkuṇoti, pāpuṇoti. Why [the condition] 'before ṇa'? [So that the forms are] sakkoti, pāpeti.

122. Nito cissa cho.

122. After ni, cha [is substituted] for ci.

Nismā parassa cissa cho hoti. Nicchayo.

For ci following ni, cha is substituted. [For example,] nicchayo.

123. Jarasadānamīma vā.

123. Of [the roots] jara and sada, īma [is substituted] optionally.

Jarasadānamantasarā paro īma hoti vibhāsā. Jīraṇaṃ, jīrati, jīrāpeti, nisīditabbaṃ, nisīdanaṃ, nisīdituṃ, nisīdati, vāti kiṃ? Jarā, nisajjā, ‘īma vā’ti yogavibhāgā aññesampi, ahīratha, saṃyogādi lopotthassa.

Of [the roots] jara, sada, and [other] roots ending in a vowel, ī is optionally substituted for the vowel. [For example,] jīraṇaṃ, jīrati, jīrāpeti; nisīditabbaṃ, nisīdanaṃ, nisīdituṃ, nisīdati. Why [the word] 'optionally'? [For the forms] jarā, nisajjā. By splitting the rule 'īma vā', it applies to others also, [for example,] ahīratha; and there is elision of the first [consonant] of a following conjunct.

124. Disassa passa dassa dasa da dakkhā.

124. Of [the root] dis, [the substitutes are] passa, dassa, dasa, da, and dakkha.

Disassa passādayo honti vibhāsā. Vipassanā, vipassituṃ, vipassati, sudassī, piyadassī, dhammadassī, sudassaṃ, dassanaṃ, dasseti, daṭṭhabbaṃ. Daṭṭhā, daṭṭhuṃ, duddaso, addasa, addā, addaṃ, addakkhi, dakkhissati, vātveva? Dissanti bālā.

Of [the root] dis, passa and the other [substitutes] occur optionally. [For example,] vipassanā, vipassituṃ, vipassati; sudassī, piyadassī, dhammadassī; sudassaṃ, dassanaṃ, dasseti; daṭṭhabbaṃ, daṭṭhā, daṭṭhuṃ; duddaso, addasa, addā, addaṃ; addakkhi, dakkhissati. But why [the word] 'optionally'? [Because the original form is also seen, as in] dissanti bālā.

125. Samānā ro rīrikkhakesu.

125. After samāna, [the substitutes are] ra or rī before ikkha and ka.

Samānasaddato [M 0.0201] parassa disassa ra hoti vā rīvikkhakesu. Sarī, sadī, sarikkho, sadikkho, sariso, sadiso.

For dis following the word samāna, ra or rī is optionally substituted. [For example,] sarī, sadī; sarikkho, sadikkho; sariso, sadiso.

126. Dahassa dassa ḍo.

126. Of [the root] daha, ḍa [is substituted] for da.

Dahassa dassa ḍo hoti vā. Ḍāho, dāho, ḍahati, dahati.

Of [the root] daha, ḍa is optionally substituted for da. [For example,] ḍāho, dāho; ḍahati, dahati.

127. Anaghaṇa svāparīhi ḷo.

127. After ā and pari, ḷa [is substituted for da of daha], under the condition of anaghaṇa.

Āparīhi parassa dahassa dassa ḷo hoti anaghaṇasu. Āḷahanaṃ, pariḷāho.

For the da of the root daha following ā and pari, ḷa is substituted, under the condition of anaghaṇa. [For example,] āḷahanaṃ, pariḷāho.

128. Atyādintesvatthissa bhū.

128. Of [the root] as, bhū [is substituted], except before ti, nta, and so on.

Tyādintavajjitesu paccayesu ‘asa=bhuvi’iccassa bhū hoti. Bhavitabbaṃ. Ādesavidhānamasassāppayogatthametasmiṃ visaye, etena katthaci kassaci dhātussa appayogāpi ñāpito hoti. Atyādintesūti kiṃ? Atthi, santo, atthissāti kiṃ? Assatissa mā hotu.

Before suffixes other than ti, nta, and so on, bhū is substituted for the root as (meaning 'to be'). [For example,] bhavitabbaṃ. This substitution rule is for the purpose of ensuring the non-use of as in this domain; by this, it is also indicated that in some cases a certain root is not used at all. Why [the condition] 'except before ti, nta, and so on'? [To allow for the forms] atthi, santo. Why [the specification] 'of as'? So that it does not apply to a non-existent [root].

129. Aāssāādīsu.

129. In the cases of a, ā, ssā, and so on.

Aādo, āādo, ssādo ca atthissa bhū hoti. Babhūva, abhavā, abhavissā, bhavissati.

For the root `as` (represented by `atthi`), `bhū` is the substitute when suffixes beginning with a, ā, and ssā follow. Examples: Babhūva, abhavā, abhavissā, bhavissati.

130. Ntamānantiyiyuṃsvādilopo. Ntādisūtthissādilopo hoti. Santo, samāno, santi, santu, siyā, siyuṃ, etesvīti kiṃ? Atthi.

130. Elision of the initial vowel of the root `as` before `nta`, `māna`, `anti`, `iyuṃ`, and so on. Elision of the initial vowel of the root `as` occurs before `nta` and so on. Examples: santo, samāno, santi, santu, siyā, siyuṃ. Why state 'before these'? To account for the form `atthi`.

131. Pādito ṭhāssa vā ṭhaho kvaci.

131. After a prefix, `ṭhaha` is optionally substituted for the root `ṭhā` in some cases.

Pādīhi [M 0.0202] kiriyāvisesajotakehi saddehi parassa ṭhāssa kvaci ṭhaho vā hoti. Saṇṭhahanto santiṭṭhanto. Saṇṭhahati, santiṭṭhati. Pa parā apa saṃ anu ava o ni du vi adhi api atisu u abhi pati pari upa ā pādī. Kvacīti kiṃ? Saṇṭhiti.

After prefixes (`pādi`), which are words that indicate specific verbal actions, `ṭhaha` is optionally substituted for the root `ṭhā` in some cases. Examples: saṇṭhahanto, santiṭṭhanto; saṇṭhahati, santiṭṭhati. The prefixes are: pa, parā, apa, saṃ, anu, ava, o, ni, du, vi, adhi, api, ati, su, u, abhi, pati, pari, upa, ā. Why the phrase 'in some cases'? To account for `saṇṭhiti`.

132. Dāssiyaṅa.

132. For the root `dā`, `iyaṅa` is the substitute.

Pādito parassa dāssa iyaṅa hoti kvaci. Anādiyitvā, samādiyati, kvacitveva? Ādāya.

After a prefix, `iya` is substituted for the root `dā` in some cases. Examples: anādiyitvā, samādiyati. Why 'in some cases'? To account for `ādāya`.

133. Karotissa kho.

133. For the root `kar`, `kha` is the substitute.

Pādito parassa karassa kvaci kha hoti. Saṅkhāro, saṅkharīyati, karassāti avatvā karotissāti vacanaṃ timhi ca vikaraṇuppattiñāpetuṃ.

After a prefix, `kha` is substituted for the root `kar` in some cases. Examples: saṅkhāro, saṅkharīyati. The word `karotissa` is used in the rule instead of `karassa` to indicate that this applies when a conjugational sign (`vikaraṇa`) arises.

134. Purāsmā.

134. After `purā`.

Purā iccasmā nipātā parassa karassa kha hoti. Purakkhatvā, purekkhāro-ettaṃ tadaminādipāṭhā.

After the particle `purā`, `kha` is substituted for the root `kar`. Examples: purakkhatvā, purekkhāro. The `e` in the latter is according to the `Tadaminādi` reading.

135. Nito kamassa.

135. After `ni`, for the root `kam`.

Nismā parassa kamassa kvaci kha hoti, nikkhamati, kvacitveva? Nikkamo.

After `ni`, `kha` is substituted for the root `kam` in some cases. Example: nikkhamati. Why 'in some cases'? To account for `nikkamo`.

136. Yuvaṇṇānamiyaṅuvaṅa sare.

136. For the vowels `i` and `u`, `iyaṅ` and `uvaṅ` are the substitutes when a vowel follows.

Ivaṇṇuvaṇṇattānaṃ kriyatthānamiyaṅuvaṅa hoti sare kvaci. Vediyati, bruvanti, sareti kiṃ? Nivedeti, brūti, kvacitveva? Jayati, bhavati.

For verbal roots ending in the vowels `i` and `u`, `iyaṅ` and `uvaṅ` are substituted in some cases when a vowel follows. Examples: vediyati, bruvanti. Why 'when a vowel follows'? To account for `nivedeti`, `brūti`. Why 'in some cases'? To account for `jayati`, `bhavati`.

137. Aññādissāssī kye.

137. For the final `ā` of roots such as `ñā`, `ī` is the substitute before `kya`.

Ñādito-ññassa [M 0.0203] ākārantassa kriyatthassa ī hoti kye. Dīyati, aññādissāti kiṃ? Ñāyati, tāyatiṃ.

For a verbal root ending in `ā`, such as `ñā`, `ī` is substituted before `kya`. Example: dīyati. Why 'such as `ñā`'? To account for `ñāyati`, `tāyatiṃ`.

138. Tanassā vā.

138. For the root `tan`, `ā` is optionally the substitute.

Tanassa ā hoti vā kye. Tāyate, taññate.

For the root `tan`, `ā` is optionally substituted when `kya` follows. Examples: tāyate, taññate.

139. Dīgho sarassa.

139. Lengthening of the vowel.

Sarantassa kriyatthassa dīgho hoti kye, cīyate, sūyate.

For a verbal root ending in a vowel, lengthening occurs when `kya` follows. Examples: cīyate, sūyate.

140. Sānantarassa tassa ṭho.

140. For a `ta` immediately following an `s`, `ṭha` is the substitute.

Sakārantato kriyatthā parassā-nantarassa takārassa ṭha hoti. Tuṭṭho, tuṭṭhavā, tuṭṭhabbaṃ, tuṭṭhi, anantarassāti kiṃ? Tussitvā.

After a verbal root ending in the letter `s`, an immediately following `t` becomes `ṭha`. Examples: tuṭṭho, tuṭṭhavā, tuṭṭhabbaṃ, tuṭṭhi. Why 'immediately following'? To account for `tussitvā`.

141. Kasassima ca vā.

141. For the root `kas`, its vowel also optionally becomes `i`.

Kasasmā parassānantarassa tassa ṭha hoti kasassa vā ima ca. Kiṭṭhaṃ, kaṭṭhaṃ, anantarassātveva? Kasitabbaṃ.

After the root `kas`, an immediately following `t` becomes `ṭh`, and the vowel of `kas` optionally becomes `i`. Examples: kiṭṭhaṃ, kaṭṭhaṃ. Why 'immediately following'? To account for `kasitabbaṃ`.

142. Dhastotrastā.

142. `Dhasta` and `trasta`.

Ete saddā nipaccante.

These words are irregularly formed.

143. Pucchādito.

143. After `puccha` and so on.

Pucchādīhi [M 0.0204] kriyatthehi parassānantarassa takārassa ṭha hoti. Puṭṭho, bhaṭṭho, yiṭṭho, anantarassātveva? Pucchitvā.

After verbal roots such as `puccha`, an immediately following `t` becomes `ṭh`. Examples: puṭṭho, bhaṭṭho, yiṭṭho. Why 'immediately following'? To account for `pucchitvā`.

144. Sāsa vasa saṃsa sasā tho.

144. For the roots `sās`, `vas`, `saṃs`, and `sas`, `tha` is substituted for a following `t`.

Etehi parassānantarassa tassa tha hoti, satthaṃ, vatthaṃ, pasatthaṃ, satthaṃ. Kathamanusiṭṭho (vuṭṭho) ti? ‘Tathanarānaṃ ṭaṭṭhaṇalā’ 1-52 ti ṭṭho, anantarassātveva? Sāsituṃ.

From these, the immediately following 'ta' becomes 'tha'. For example: satthaṃ, vatthaṃ, pasatthaṃ, satthaṃ. How is anusiṭṭho (or vuṭṭho) formed? By the rule 'tathanarānaṃ ṭaṭṭhaṇalā' (1-52), it becomes ṭṭho. Why specify 'immediately following'? Consider: sāsituṃ.

145. Dho dhahabhehi.

145. After 'dha', 'ha', and 'bha', ['ta' becomes] 'dha'.

Dhakārahakārabhakārantehi kriyatthehi parassānantarassa tassa dha hoti. Vuddho, duddhaṃ, laddhaṃ.

After verbal roots ending in 'dha', 'ha', or 'bha', the immediately following 'ta' becomes 'dha'. For example: vuddho, duddhaṃ, laddhaṃ.

146. Dahā ḍho.

146. After 'dah', ['ta' becomes] 'ḍha'.

Dahā parassānantarassa tassa ḍha hoti. Daḍḍho.

After 'dah', the immediately following 'ta' becomes 'ḍha'. For example: daḍḍho.

147. Bahassuma ca.

147. And for 'bah', 'uma'.

Bahā parassānantarassa tassa ḍho hoti, bahassuma ca ḍhasanniyogena. Buḍḍho.

After 'bah', the immediately following 'ta' becomes 'ḍha', and for 'bah' there is 'uma' in conjunction with 'ḍha'. For example: buḍḍho.

148. Ruhādīhi ho ḷa ca.

148. After 'ruh' and so on, ['ta' becomes] 'ha', and ['the final consonant' becomes] 'ḷa'.

Rahādīhi parassānantarassa tassa ha hoti ḷo cāntassa. Āruḷho, gūḷho, vūḷho, bāḷho, (ogāḷho), anantarassātveva? Ārohituṃ.

After 'ruh' and so on, the immediately following 'ta' becomes 'ha', and the final consonant becomes 'ḷa'. For example: āruḷho, gūḷho, vūḷho, bāḷho, (ogāḷho). Why specify 'immediately following'? Consider: ārohituṃ.

149. Muhā vā.

149. After 'muh', optionally.

Muhā [M 0.0205] parassānantarassa tassa ha hoti vā ḷo cāntassa hasanniyogena. Mūḷho, muddho.

After 'muh', the immediately following 'ta' optionally becomes 'ha', and the final consonant becomes 'ḷa' in conjunction with 'ha'. For example: mūḷho, muddho.

150. Bhidādito no ktaktavantūnaṃ.

150. After 'bhid' and so on, the 'ta' of 'kta' and 'ktavantu' becomes 'na'.

Bhidādito paresaṃ ktaktavantūnaṃ tassa no hoti. Bhinno bhinnavā, chinno chinnavā, channo channavā, chinno khinnavā, uppanno uppannavā, sinno, sinnavā, sanno sannavā, pīno pīnavā, sūno sūnavā, dīno dīnavā, ḍīno ḍīnavā, līno līnavā, lūno lūnavā, ktaktavantūnanti kiṃ? Bhitti, chitti, bhettuṃ, chettuṃ.

After 'bhid' and so on, the 'ta' of the following 'kta' and 'ktavantu' suffixes becomes 'na'. For example: bhinno, bhinnavā; chinno, chinnavā; channo, channavā; khinno, khinnavā; uppanno, uppannavā; sinno, sinnavā; sanno, sannavā; pīno, pīnavā; sūno, sūnavā; dīno, dīnavā; ḍīno, ḍīnavā; līno, līnavā; lūno, lūnavā. Why specify 'kta' and 'ktavantu'? Consider: bhitti, chitti, bhettuṃ, chettuṃ.

151. Dātvinno.

151. After 'dā', ['ta' becomes] 'inna'.

Dāto paresaṃ ktaktavantūnaṃ tassa inno hoti. Dinno, dinnavā.

After the root 'dā', the 'ta' of the following 'kta' and 'ktavantu' suffixes becomes 'inna'. For example: dinno, dinnavā.

152. Kirādīhi ṇo.

152. After 'kir' and so on, ['ta' becomes] 'ṇa'.

Kirādīhi paresaṃ ktaktavantūnaṃ tassānantarassa ṇa hoti, kiṇṇo kiṇṇavā, puṇṇo puṇṇavā, khīṇo khīṇavā.

After roots of the 'kir'-group, the immediately following 'ta' of the 'kta' and 'ktavantu' suffixes becomes 'ṇa'. For example: kiṇṇo, kiṇṇavā; puṇṇo, puṇṇavā; khīṇo, khīṇavā.

153. Tarādīhi riṇṇo.

153. After the 'tar'-group, ['ta' becomes] 'riṇṇa'.

Tarādīhi paresaṃ ktaktavantūnaṃ tassa riṇṇo hoti. Tiṇṇo tiṇṇavā, jiṇṇo jiṇṇavā, ciṇṇo ciṇṇavā.

After roots of the 'tar'-group, the 'ta' of the following 'kta' and 'ktavantu' suffixes becomes 'riṇṇa'. For example: tiṇṇo, tiṇṇavā; jiṇṇo, jiṇṇavā; ciṇṇo, ciṇṇavā.

154. Go sanjādīhi.

154. After the 'bhañj'-group, ['ta' becomes] 'ga'.

Bhanjādīhi paresaṃ ktaktavantūnaṃ tassānantarassa ga hoti. Bhaggo bhaggavā, laggo laggavā, nimuggo nimuggavā, saṃviggo saṃviggavā.

After roots of the 'bhañj'-group, the immediately following 'ta' of the 'kta' and 'ktavantu' suffixes becomes 'ga'. For example: bhaggo, bhaggavā; laggo, laggavā; nimuggo, nimuggavā; saṃviggo, saṃviggavā.

155. Susā kho.

155. After 'sus', ['ta' becomes] 'kha'.

Susā [M 0.0206] paresaṃ ktaktavantūnaṃ tassa kho hoti. Sukkho sukkhavā.

After the root 'sus', the 'ta' of the following 'kta' and 'ktavantu' suffixes becomes 'kha'. For example: sukkho, sukkhavā.

156. Pacā ko.

156. After 'pac', ['ta' becomes] 'ka'.

Pacā paresaṃ ktaktavantūnaṃ tassa ko hoti. Pakko pakkavā.

After the root 'pac', the 'ta' of the following 'kta' and 'ktavantu' suffixes becomes 'ka'. For example: pakko, pakkavā.

157. Mucā vā.

157. After 'muc', optionally.

Mucā paresaṃ ktaktavantūnaṃ tassa ko vā hoti. Mukko mutto, mukkavā muttavā. ‘Sakko’ti ṇvādīsu siddhaṃ, ktaktavantūsu satto, sattāvātveva hoti.

After the root 'muc', the 'ta' of the following 'kta' and 'ktavantu' suffixes optionally becomes 'ka'. For example: mukko or mutto; mukkavā or muttavā. The form 'sakko' is derived with suffixes such as 'ṇva'; with 'kta' and 'ktavantu', the forms are simply 'satto' and 'sattavā'.

158. Lopo vaḍḍhā ktissa.

158. After 'vaḍḍh', the 'ta' of 'kti' is elided.

Vaḍḍhā parassa ktissa tassa lopo hoti. Vaḍḍhi.

After the root 'vaḍḍh', the 'ta' of the following 'kti' suffix is elided. For example: vaḍḍhi.

159. Kvissa.

159. [There is elision] of 'kvi'.

Kriyatthā parassa kvissa lopo hoti, abhibhū.

The suffix kvi following a verb root is elided. For example: abhibhū.

160. Ṇiṇāpīnaṃ tesu.

160. Of ṇi, ṇā, and pi, when these follow.

Ṇiṇāpīnaṃ lopo hoti tesu ṇiṇāpīsu. Kārentaṃ payojayati kāreti kārāpayati.

The causative suffixes ṇi, ṇā, and pi are elided when followed by these same suffixes. For example, from 'one causes one who is causing to do': kāreti, kārāpayati.

161. Kvaci vikaraṇānaṃ.

161. Sometimes of the conjugational signs.

Vikaraṇānaṃ kvaci lopo hoti. Udapādi, hanti.

Sometimes there is elision of the conjugational signs. For example: udapādi, hanti.

162. Mānassa massa.

162. Of the ma of māna.

Kriyatthā [M 0.0207] parassa mānassa makārassa lopo hoti kvaci. Karāṇo, kvacīti kiṃ? Kurumāno.

Sometimes the letter ma of the suffix māna following a verb root is elided. For example: karāṇo. Why 'sometimes'? To allow for kurumāno.

163. Ūlasse.

163. Elision of the augment.

Ñilāname hoti kvaci. Gahetvā, adenti, kvacitveva? Vapitvā.

Sometimes there is elision. For example: gahetvā. Why 'sometimes'? To allow for vapitvā.

164. Pyo vā tvāssa samāse.

164. The suffix tvā is optionally replaced by ya in a compound.

Tvāssa vā pyo hoti samāse. Pakāro “pye sissā” ti 5-88 visesanattho. Abhibhūya, abhibhavitvā, samāseti kiṃ? Patvā, kvacāsamāsepi bahulādhikārā ‘lataṃ dantehi chindiya’.

The suffix tvā is optionally replaced by ya in a compound. The letter p is for the purpose of specification in rule 5-88. For example: abhibhūya or abhibhavitvā. Why 'in a compound'? To exclude cases like patvā. However, sometimes it occurs even when not in a compound due to the governing principle of 'variously,' as in lataṃ dantehi chindiya.

165. Tuṃyānā.

165. Of tuṃ and yāna.

Ktvāssa vā tuṃyānā honti samāse kvacci. Abhihaṭṭhuṃ abhiharitvā, anumodiyāna anumoditvā, asamāsepi bahulādhi kārā, daṭṭhuṃ disvā, esamappavisayatāñāpanattho yogavibhāgo.

Sometimes in a compound, the suffix tvā is optionally replaced by tuṃ and yāna. For example: abhihaṭṭhuṃ for abhiharitvā; anumodiyāna for anumoditvā. Due to the governing principle of 'variously,' this also occurs when not in a compound, as in daṭṭhuṃ for disvā. The splitting of the rule serves to indicate that these substitutions have a limited scope.

166. Hanā racco.

166. After han, racca.

Hanasmā parassa ktvāssa racco vā hoti samāse. Āhacca, āhanitvā.

In a compound, the suffix tvā following the root han is optionally replaced by racca. For example: āhacca or āhanitvā.

167. Sāsādhikarā cacariccā.

167. After sa-kar and adhi-kar, caca and ricca.

Sāsādhīhi parā karā parassa ktvassa cacariccā honti yathākkamaṃ. Sakkacca sakkaritvā, asakkacca asakkaritvā, adhikicca adhikaritvā.

After the root kar preceded by the prefixes sa and adhi respectively, the suffix tvā is replaced by caca and ricca. For example: sakkacca for sakkaritvā; asakkacca for asakkaritvā; adhikicca for adhikaritvā.

168. Ito cco.

168. After i, cca.

Iiccasmā [M 0.0208] parassa ktvāssa cco vā hoti. Adhicca adhīyitvā, samecca sametvā.

After the root i ('to go'), the suffix tvā is optionally replaced by cca. For example: adhicca for adhīyitvā; samecca for sametvā.

169. Disā vānavā sa ca.

169. After dis, vāna and vā; and sa for the root.

Disato ktvāssa vānavā honti vā disassa ca sa kāro taṃsanniyogena. Sassa savidhānaṃ pararūpabādhanatthaṃ. Disvāna, disvā passitvā, kathaṃ ‘nādaṭṭhā parato dosa’nti? Ñāpakā tvāssa valopo, evaṃ ‘laddhā dhana’nti ādīsu.

After the root dis, the suffix tvā is optionally replaced by vāna or vā, with the concurrent substitution of sa for the root dis. The explicit prescription of sa is to prevent a subsequent phonetic rule. For example: disvāna, disvā (alternative: passitvā). How is the form in nādaṭṭhā parato dosaṃ explained? From this as an indicator, the va of the suffix tvā is elided. This is also the case in examples such as laddhā dhanaṃ.

170. Ñi byañjanassa.

170. The augment i before a consonant.

Kriyatthā parassa byañjanādippaccayassa ñi vā hoti. Bhuñjituṃ bhottuṃ, byañjanassāti kiṃ? Pācako.

The augment i (ñi) is optionally prefixed to a suffix beginning with a consonant that follows a verb root. For example: bhuñjituṃ or bhottuṃ. Why 'beginning with a consonant'? To exclude cases like pācako.

171. Rā nassa ṇo.

171. After r, ṇa for na.

Rantato kriyatthā parassa paccayanakārassa ṇo hoti. Araṇaṃ, saraṇaṃ.

The letter na of a suffix that follows a verb root ending in r is replaced by ṇa. For example: araṇaṃ, saraṇaṃ.

172. Na ntamānatyādīnaṃ.

172. Not of nta, māna, ti, etc.

Rantato paresaṃ ntamānatyādīnaṃ nassa ṇo na hoti, karonto, kurumāno, karonti.

Following a root ending in r, the n of suffixes such as nta, māna, and ti does not become ṇ. For example: karonto, kurumāno, karonti.

173. Gamayamisāsadisānaṃ vā cchaṅa.

173. For the roots gam, yam, is, ās, and dis, ccha is the optional substitute.

Etesaṃ vā cchaṅa hoti ntamānatyādīsu. Gacchanto gacchamāno gacchati, yacchanno yacchamāno yacchati, icchanto icchamāno icchati [M 0.0209] acchanto acchamāno acchati, dicchanto dicchamāno dicchati, vāti kiṃ? Gamissati, vavatthitavibhāsā-yaṃ, tenāññesu ca kvaci-icchitabbaṃ icchā icchituṃ, acchitabbaṃ acchatuṃ, aññesañca yogavibhāgā-pavecchati.

For these roots, the substitute ccha optionally occurs before suffixes such as nta, māna, and ti. For example: gacchanto (going), gacchamāno (going), gacchati (he goes); yacchanto (giving), yacchamāno (giving), yacchati (he gives); icchanto (wishing), icchamāno (wishing), icchati (he wishes); acchanto (being), acchamāno (being), acchati (he is); dicchanto (seeing), dicchamāno (seeing), dicchati (he sees). Why 'optionally'? To allow for forms like gamissati (he will go). This is a 'fixed option' (vavatthitavibhāsā). Therefore, in other cases too, it is sometimes to be applied, as in icchitabbaṃ (what should be wished), icchā (a wish), icchituṃ (to wish); acchitabbaṃ (what should be sat), acchituṃ (to sit). And for other roots, by 'splitting the rule' (yogavibhāga), one gets forms like pavecchati (he enters).

174. Jaramarānamīyaṅa.

174. For the roots jar and mar, īya is the substitute.

Etesamīyaṅa vā hoti ntamānatyādīsu. Jīyanto jīranto, jīyamāno jīramāno, jīyati jīrati, mīyanto maranto, mīyamāno maramāno, mīyati marati.

For these roots, the substitute 'īya' optionally occurs before suffixes such as '-nta', '-māna', and '-ti'. For example: jīyanto or jīranto (decaying), jīyamāno or jīramāno (decaying), jīyati or jīrati (he decays); mīyanto or maranto (dying), mīyamāno or maramāno (dying), mīyati or marati (he dies).

175. Ṭhāpānaṃ tiṭṭha pivā.

175. For the roots ṭhā and pā, the substitutes are 'tiṭṭha' and 'piva' respectively.

Ṭhāpānaṃ tiṭṭhapivā honti ntamānatyādīsu. Tiṭṭhanto, tiṭṭhamāno, tiṭṭhati, pivanto, pivamāno, pivati, vātvevi? Ṭhāti, pāti.

For the roots ṭhā and pā, 'tiṭṭha' and 'piva' are the respective substitutes before suffixes such as '-nta', '-māna', and '-ti'. For example: tiṭṭhanto (standing), tiṭṭhamāno (standing), tiṭṭhati (he stands); pivanto (drinking), pivamāno (drinking), pivati (he drinks). Why is this optional? To allow for forms like ṭhāti (he stands) and pāti (he drinks).

176. Gamavadadānaṃ ghammavajjadajjā.

176. For the roots gam, vad, and dā, the respective substitutes are 'ghamma', 'vajja', and 'dajja'.

Gamādīnaṃ ghammādayo vā honti ntamānatyādīsu. Ghammanto, gacchanto, vajjanto vadanto, dajjanto dadanto.

For roots such as gam, the substitutes 'ghamma', etc., optionally occur before suffixes such as '-nta', '-māna', and '-ti'. For example: ghammanto or gacchanto (going); vajjanto or vadanto (speaking); dajjanto or dadanto (giving).

177. Karassa sossa kubbakurukayirā.

177. For the root kar with the vowel 'o', the substitutes are 'kubba', 'kuru', and 'kayirā'.

Karassa saokārassa kubbādayo vā honti ntamānatyādīsu. Kubbanto kayiranto karonto, kubbamāno kurumāno kayiramāno, karāṇo, kubbati kayirati karoti, kubbate kurute, kayirate, vavatthitavibhāsattā vādhikārassa bhiyyo mānaparacchakkesu kuru, kvacideva pubbachakke ‘agghaṃ kurutu, no bhavaṃ, sossāti vuttattā kattariyevime.

For the root kar with the vowel 'o', the substitutes 'kubba', etc., optionally occur before suffixes such as '-nta', '-māna', and '-ti'. For example: kubbanto, kayiranto, karonto; kubbamāno, kurumāno, kayiramāno, karāṇo; kubbati, kayirati, karoti; kubbate, kurute, kayirate. Because this is a 'fixed option' (vavatthitavibhāsā) under the governing rule of 'optionally', the substitute 'kuru' occurs more often with the '-māna' suffix and in the middle voice endings, and only sometimes in the active voice endings. Because it is said, 'Let his honor set the price, not I,' and 'he will hear,' these substitutes are used only in the agentive sense (kattari).

178. Gahassa gheppo.

178. For the root gah, the substitute is 'gheppa'.

Gahassa [M 0.0210] vā gheppo hoti ntamānatyādīsu. Gheppanto, gheppamāno, gheppati, vātveva? Gaṇhati.

For the root gah, 'gheppa' is the optional substitute before suffixes such as '-nta', '-māna', and '-ti'. For example: gheppanto (taking), gheppamāno (taking), gheppati (he takes). Why 'optionally'? To allow for the form gaṇhati (he takes).

179. Ṇo niggahītassa.

179. The affix 'ṇo' for the one that is restrained.

Gahassa niggahītassa ṇo hoti. Gaṇhitabbaṃ, gaṇhituṃ, gaṇhanto.

For the root gah that is restrained, the affix 'ṇo' occurs. For example: gaṇhitabbaṃ (to be taken), gaṇhituṃ (to take), gaṇhanto (taking).

Itimoggallāne byākaraṇe vuttiyaṃ

Thus in the commentary on the Moggallāna Grammar.

Khādikaṇḍo pañcamo.

The Fifth Chapter: The Khādikaṇḍa.

6. Chaṭṭho kaṇḍo (tyādi)

6. The Sixth Chapter (The Ti-Endings, etc.)

1. Vattamāne ti anti si tha mi ma te ante se vhe e mhe.

1. In the present tense: ti, anti, si, tha, mi, ma; te, ante, se, vhe, e, mhe.

Vattamāne āraddhāparisamatte atthe vattamānato kriyatthā tyādayo honti. Gacchati, gacchanti, gacchasi gacchatha, gacchāmi gacchāma, gacchate gacchante, gacchase gacchavhe, gacche gacchāmhe. Kathaṃ ‘pure adhammo dippati, purā marāmī’ti?
