From the root `is` in the sense of desiring, the suffix `ṭhakana` is employed. It is desired, thus `iṭṭhakā` = a brick.

30. Samā kho.

30. From `sama`, the suffix `kho`.

Sama-upasamakhedesu[M 0.0239], etasmā kho hoti. Sameti upasametīti saṅkho=kambu.

From the root `sama` in the senses of calming and weariness, the suffix `kho` is employed. It calms, it pacifies, thus `saṅkho` = a conch.

31. Mukhā dayo.

31. `Mukha` and others.

Mukha ādayo khantā nipaccante. Mu-bandhane, ottābhāvo nipātanā, munanti bandhanti etenāti mukhaṃ=lapanaṃ. Si-sevāyaṃ, ettā bhāvo nipātanā, sayanti ettha ūkā kusuma-dayo cāti sikhā=cūḷā. Vipubbassa sissa, visatissa vā, visesena sayanti ettha, pavisantīti visikhā=racchā. Kana-dītti gati kantīsu, nipubbo, anabhāgalopo, kanati dibbatīti nikkho=suvaṇṇavikāro. Mayaiti gamanattho daṇḍako dhātu, khassa ūña, mayati yātīti mayūkho-kiraṇo. Lū-chedane, otthābhāvo, lunāti chindati sobhanti lūkho=asiniddho. Ara-gamane, aranti yanti etenāti akkho=sakaṭāvayavā, pāsako ca. Yasa-payatane, yassati payatati balimāharaṇatthāyāti yakkho=amanusso, ruha-janane, ruhati jāyatīti rukkho=pādapo, usa-dāhe, usati dahati kāmaggināti ukkho=balībaddo. Saha-marisane ‘halopo, sahati attani katāparādhaṃ khamatīti sakhā=sahāyo, evamaññepi.

Words such as `mukha` are irregularly formed with the suffix `kha`. From the root `mu` in the sense of binding; 'they bind with this,' thus `mukhaṃ` = the mouth. From the root `si` in the sense of resting on; 'lice, flowers, and so forth rest here,' thus `sikhā` = a crest. From the root `si` with the prefix `vi`, or from `visati`; 'they rest here in a special way,' or 'they enter,' thus `visikhā` = a street. From the root `kana` in the senses of shining, going, and desiring, with the prefix `ni` and elision of the `ana` part; 'it shines, it glitters,' thus `nikkho` = a gold ornament. From the root `maya` in the sense of going; 'it goes,' thus `mayūkho` = a ray. From the root `lū` in the sense of cutting; 'it cuts, it severs beauty,' thus `lūkho` = rough. From the root `ara` in the sense of going; 'one goes by means of it,' thus `akkho` = an axle of a cart, and also a die. From the root `yasa` in the sense of striving; 'he strives to bring offerings,' thus `yakkho` = a non-human being. From the root `ruha` in the sense of being born; 'it grows,' thus `rukkho` = a tree. From the root `usa` in the sense of burning; 'it burns with the fire of passion,' thus `ukkho` = a bull. From the root `saha` in the sense of enduring, with elision of `ha`; 'he endures, he forgives an offense done to himself,' thus `sakhā` = a friend. And so for others.

32. Aja vaja muda gada gamā gaka.

32. From `aja`, `vaja`, `muda`, `gada`, and `gama`, the suffix `gaka`.

Aja vaja-gamane, muda-tose, gada-vacane, ama gama-gamane, etehi gaka hoti. Ajati gacchati seṭṭhabhāvanti aggo-seṭṭho[M 0.0240]. Vajati samūhattaṃ gacchatīti vaggo=samūho. Mudanti etenāti muggo=dhaññaviseso. Gadatīti gaggo=isi. “Manānaṃ niggahīta”nti (5.96) massa niggahītaṃ, gacchatīti gaṅgā=surāpagā.

From the roots `aja` and `vaja` in the sense of going; `muda` in the sense of rejoicing; `gada` in the sense of speaking; and `ama` and `gama` in the sense of going, the suffix `gaka` is employed. It goes to a state of excellence, thus `aggo` = the chief. It goes to a state of being a group, thus `vaggo` = a group. They rejoice by means of this, thus `muggo` = a type of grain. He speaks, thus `gaggo` = a sage. By the rule `Manānaṃ niggahīta` (5.96), the `m` of `gama` becomes a `niggahīta`; it goes, thus `gaṅgā` = the celestial river.

33. Siṅgādayo.

33. `Siṅga` and others.

Siṅgaādayo saddā gakaantā nipaccante. Sī-saye, niggahītāgamo, rassattañca, sayati pavattati matthaketi siṅgaṃ=visāṇaṃ. Phura-calane, limuṅa, phurati calatīti puliṅgo=jalitaṅgā rāvayavo. Cala-kampane, upubbo, calassa cāliṃ, uccalati kampatīti uccāliṅgo=sukkakīṭo, kala-sadde, imuka, kalati abhinādaṃ karoti bahurajjatāyā ti kaliṅgo=dakkhiṇāpatho. Bhama-anavaṭṭhāne, assa ittaṃ, bhamatīti bhiṅgo=bhamaro. Paṭa aṭa-gamane, paṭissa amuka, aka ca. Paṭati patanto gacchatīti paṭaṅgo, paṭago=salabho, evamaññepi.

Words such as `siṅga` are irregularly formed with the suffix `gaka`. From the root `sī` in the sense of resting, with insertion of a `niggahīta` and shortening; 'it rests on the head,' thus `siṅgaṃ` = a horn. From the root `phura` in the sense of moving; 'it moves, it trembles,' thus `puliṅgo` = a spark. From the root `cala` in the sense of trembling, with the prefix `u` and `cala` changed to `cāli`; 'it trembles upwards,' thus `uccāliṅgo` = a white ant. From the root `kala` in the sense of making a sound; 'it makes a loud sound because of having many kingdoms,' thus `kaliṅgo` = the southern country. From the root `bhama` in the sense of wandering, with `a` changed to `i`; 'it wanders,' thus `bhiṅgo` = a bee. From the roots `paṭa` and `aṭa` in the sense of going; 'it goes by flying,' thus `paṭaṅgo` or `paṭago` = a grasshopper. And so for others.

34. Agā gi.

34. From `aga`, the suffix `gi`.

Aga-kuṭilagamanetīmasmā gi hoti. Agati kuṭilo hutvā gacchatīti aggi=pāvako.

From the root `aga` in the sense of crooked going, the suffix `gi` is employed. It goes crookedly, thus `aggi` = fire.

35. Yāvalā gu.

35. From `yā` and `vala`, the suffix `gu`.

Yā-pāpuṇane, vala valla-saṃvaraṇe, etehi gu hoti. Yātīti yāgu=peyyā. Valīyati saṃvarīyatīti vaggu=manuñño.

From the root `yā` in the sense of reaching, and `vala` or `valla` in the sense of covering, the suffix `gu` is employed. It is reached, thus `yāgu` = rice-gruel. It is chosen, thus `vaggu` = lovely.

36. Pheggādayo.

36. `Pheggu` and others.

Pheggu [M 0.0241] ādayo guantā nipaccante. Phala-nipphattiyaṃ, assa ettaṃ, phalati niṭṭhānaṃ gacchatīti pheggu=asāro. Bhara-bharaṇe, ralopo. Bharatīti bhagu=isi. Hi-gatīyaṃ, niggahītāgamo, hino ti pavattatīti hiṅgu=rāmaṭhajaṃ. Kama-icchāyaṃ, kāmīyatīti kaṅgu=dhaññaviseso, evamaññepi.

Words such as `pheggu` are irregularly formed with the suffix `gu`. From the root `phala` in the sense of bearing fruit, with `a` changed to `e`; 'it comes to fruition,' thus `pheggu` = pithless wood. From the root `bhara` in the sense of bearing, with elision of `ra`; 'he bears,' thus `bhagu` = a sage. From the root `hi` in the sense of going, with insertion of a `niggahīta`; 'it goes down,' thus `hiṅgu` = asafoetida. From the root `kama` in the sense of desiring; 'it is desired,' thus `kaṅgu` = a type of grain. And so for others.

37. Janā gho.

37. From `jana`, the suffix `gho`.

Jana-jananetīmasmā gho hoti. “Manānaṃ niggahīta”nti (5.96) nassa niggahītaṃ, jāyati gamanametāyāti jaṅghā=pāṇyaṅgaviseso.

From the root `jana` in the sense of producing, the suffix `gho` is employed. By the rule `Manānaṃ niggahīta` (5.96), the `n` becomes a `niggahīta`. Going is produced by it, thus `jaṅghā` = the lower leg.

38. Meghādayo.

38. `Megha` and others.

Meghaādayo ghantā nipaccante. Miha-secane, halopo, mehati siñcatīti megho=ambudo. Muha-mucchāyaṃ, halopo, muyhanti sattā etthāti mogho=tuccho. Sī-saye, ettābhāvo, seti lahu hutvā pavattatīti sīghaṃ=āsu. Aha-bhasmīkaraṇe, nipubbo, halopadīghā, nidahatīti nidāgho=gimho. Mahīssa halopo, mahīyati pūjīyatīti maghā=nakkhattaṃ, evamaññepi.

Words such as `megha` are irregularly formed with the suffix `gha`. From the root `miha` in the sense of sprinkling, with elision of `h`; 'it sprinkles,' thus `megho` = a cloud. From the root `muha` in the sense of bewilderment, with elision of `h`; 'beings are bewildered by it,' thus `mogho` = vain. From the root `sī` in the sense of lying down, with the absence of `e`; 'it proceeds lightly,' thus `sīghaṃ` = swiftly. From the root `aha` in the sense of reducing to ashes, with the prefix `ni`, elision of `h`, and lengthening; 'it burns up,' thus `nidāgho` = summer. From the root `mah`, with elision of `h`; 'it is honored,' thus `maghā` = a constellation. And so for others.

(Iti kavaggapaccayavidhānaṃ).

(Here ends the explanation of the suffixes of the ka-group.)

39. Cusaravarā co.

39. From `cu`, `sar`, and `var`, the suffix `ca`.

Cu-cavane, sara-gati hiṃsā cintāsu, vara-varaṇa sambhattīsu, eyehi co hoti. Cavati rukkhāti cocaṃ=upabhuttaphala- viseso[M 0.0242]. Sarati āyatiṃ dukkhaṃ hiṃsatīti saccaṃ=avitathaṃ. Vāreti sukhanti vaccaṃ=gūtho.

From the root `cu` in the sense of moving; from `sar` in the senses of going, harming, and thinking; and from `var` in the senses of choosing and devotion, the suffix `ca` is employed. 'It moves from the tree,' thus `cocaṃ` = a particular kind of enjoyed fruit. 'It goes to or harms future suffering,' thus `saccaṃ` = truth. 'It prevents pleasure,' thus `vaccaṃ` = excrement.

40. Marā cuīcī ca.

40. From `mar`, the suffixes `cu`, `īci`, and `ca`.

Mara-pāṇacāge tīmasmā cuīcī honti co ca. Maraṇaṃ maccu=maraṇaṃ. Māreti andhakāraṃ vināsetīti marīci=raṃsi, migataṇhikā ca. Maratīti macco=satto.

From the root mar in the sense of 'giving up life,' the suffixes cu, īci, co, and ca are used. Death (maraṇaṃ) is maccu (death). Because 'it destroys darkness' (māreti andhakāraṃ vināseti), it is marīci (a ray = raṃsi, and a mirage = migataṇhikā). Because 'one dies' (marati), one is a macco (a mortal = a being).

41. Kusa pasā chika.

41. From the roots kus and pas, the suffix is chika.

Kusa-akkose, pasa-bādhane, etehi chika hoti. Kusīyati akkosīyatīti kucchi=udaraṃ. Pasīyati bādhīyati etthāti pacchi=bhājanaviseso.

From the root kus in the sense of 'reviling,' and from pas in the sense of 'oppressing,' from these the suffix chika is used. Because 'it is reviled' (kusīyati akkosīyati), it is kucchi (the belly = udaraṃ). Because 'one is oppressed in it' (pasīyati bādhīyati etthā), it is pacchi (a particular kind of vessel).

42. Kasa usā chuka.

42. From the roots kas and us, the suffix is chuka.

Kasa-vilekhane, usa-dāhe, etehi chuka hoti. Kasanti vilekhanti etthāti kacchu=pāmaṃ. Usati dahati santāpanti ucchu=rasālo.

From the root kas in the sense of 'scratching,' and from us in the sense of 'burning,' from these the suffix chuka is used. Because 'they scratch in it' (kasanti vilekhanti etthā), it is kacchu (scabies = pāmaṃ). Because 'it burns, scorches, inflames' (usati dahati santāpeti), it is ucchu (sugarcane = rasālo).

43. Asa masa vada kuca kacā cho.

43. From the roots as, mas, vad, kuc, and kac, the suffix is cha.

Asa-khipane, masa-āmasane, vada-vacane, kuca-saṃkocane, kaca-bandhane, etehi cho hoti. Asati chipatīti accho=bhallūko. Masati jalanti maccho=mīno. Vadatīti vaccho=nelako. Kucīyati saṃkocīyatīti koccho=bhaddapīṭṭhaṃ. Kacīyati bandhīyatīti kaccho=tanupadeso, anūpo ca.

From the root as in the sense of 'throwing'; from mas in the sense of 'touching'; from vad in the sense of 'speaking'; from kuc in the sense of 'contracting'; and from kac in the sense of 'binding'—from these the suffix cha is used. Because 'it throws' (asati khipati), it is accho (a bear = bhallūko). Because 'it touches the water' (masati jalaṃ), it is maccho (a fish = mīno). Because 'it speaks' (vadati), it is vaccho (a calf = nelako). Because 'it is contracted' (kucīyati saṃkocīyati), it is koccho (a chair of state = bhaddapīṭhaṃ). Because 'it is bound' (kacīyati bandhīyati), it is kaccho (a region of the body, and a marshy place).

44. Gucchādayo.

44. The words beginning with guccha.

Gucchaādayo [M 0.0243] chantā nipaccante. Gupa-gopane, ottābhāvo, gopīyatīti guccho=thavako. Tusa-tuṭṭhimhī, tusanti etenāti tucchaṃ=musā. Pusa-posane, posanti tanumanenāti puccho=vāladhi, evamaññepi.

The words beginning with guccha are formed irregularly with the suffix cha. From the root gup in the sense of 'protecting,' with the absence of o; because 'it is protected' (gopīyati), it is guccho (a cluster = thavako). From the root tus in the sense of 'satisfaction'; because 'they are satisfied by it' (tusanti etena), it is tucchaṃ (empty = musā). From the root pus in the sense of 'nourishing'; because 'they nourish it a little' (posanti tanumanena), it is puccho (a tail = vāladhi). And so for others.

45. Arā ju ñaṭa ca.

45. From the root ar, the suffix is ju, and ar is replaced by uṭa.

Ara-gamanetīmasmā ju hoti, arissa uṭa ca. Ṭakāro sabbādesattho, arati akuṭilabhāvena pavattatīti uju=avaṅko.

From the root ar in the sense of 'going,' the suffix ju is used, and ar is replaced by uṭa. The letter ṭ indicates a complete substitution. Because 'it proceeds without crookedness' (arati akuṭilabhāvena pavattati), it is uju (straight = avaṅko).

46. Rajjādayo.

46. The words beginning with rajju.

Rajjuādayo juantā nipaccante. Rudha-āvaraṇe, ussa attaṃ, rundhanti etenāti rujju-yottaṃ. Mana-ñāṇe, amaññitthāti mañju=mañjulaṃ, evamaññepi.

The words beginning with rajju are formed irregularly with the suffix ju. From the root rudh in the sense of 'obstructing,' with u becoming a; because 'they obstruct with it' (rundhanti etena), it is rujju (a rope = yottaṃ). From the root man in the sense of 'knowing'; because 'one knew it' (amaññittha), it is mañju (charming = mañjulaṃ). And so for others.

47. Gidhā jhaka.

47. From the root gidh, the suffix is jhaka.

Gidha-abhikaṅkhāyamiccasmā jhaka hoti. Gedhatīti gijjho=pakkhiviseso.

From the root gidh in the sense of 'longing for,' the suffix jhaka is used. Because 'one is greedy' (gedhati), one is a gijjho (a vulture = a particular kind of bird).

48. Vañjhādayo.

48. The words beginning with vañjha.

Vañcyādayo jhaka antā nipaccante. Vana-yācane, vanoti attānaṃ anubhavituṃ yācatīti vañjho=aphalarukkho, vañjhā=apasavā itthī, assa ittaṃ viñjho=pabbato, saṃja-saṅge, niggahītalopo, sañjiyatīti sajjhaṃ=rajataṃ, evamaññepi.

The words beginning with vañjha are formed irregularly with the suffix jhaka. From the root van in the sense of 'requesting'; because 'it requests to experience itself' (vanoti attānaṃ anubhavituṃ yācati), it is vañjho (a fruitless tree) and vañjhā (a barren woman). With a becoming i, it is viñjho (a mountain). From the root sañj in the sense of 'attachment,' with elision of the niggahīta; because 'it is attached to' (sañjīyati), it is sajjhaṃ (silver = rajataṃ). And so for others.

49. Kamayajā ño.

49. From the roots kam and yaj, the suffix is ña.

Kama-icchāyaṃ[M 0.0244], yaja-devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadānesu, etehi ño hoti, massa niggahītavaggantā, kāmīyatīti kaññā=kumārī. Jassa pararūpattaṃ, yajantyanenāti yañño=yāgo.

From the root kam in the sense of 'desiring,' and from yaj in the senses of 'worship of the gods,' 'association,' 'making,' and 'giving'—from these the suffix ña is used, and the m becomes the nasal of its class. Because 'she is desired' (kāmīyati), she is a kaññā (a maiden = kumārī). The j assimilates to the following consonant; because 'they sacrifice with it' (yajanti anena), it is yañño (a sacrifice = yāgo).

50. Puññaṃ.

50. The word puñña.

Punāti puṇatismā vā ñoottābhāvo ca nipaccante. Punāti, puṇati sundarattaṃ karotīti vā puññaṃ=kusalaṃ.

The word puññaṃ is formed irregularly from the root pū or puṇ with the suffix ña and the absence of o. Because 'it purifies' (punāti) or 'makes beautiful' (puṇati sundarattaṃ karoti), it is puññaṃ (merit = kusalaṃ).

51. Ara hāñño hāssa hira ca.

51. From the roots ar and hā, the suffix is añña, and hā is replaced by hira.

Ara-gamane, vā-cāge, etehi añño hoti, hāssa hirañcādeso. Arīyate gamyateti araññaṃ=vanaṃ. Jahāti sattānaṃ hīnattanti hiraññaṃ=dhanaṃ, suvaṇṇañca.

From the root ar in the sense of 'going,' and from hā in the sense of 'abandoning,' from these the suffix añña is used, and hā is replaced by hirañ. Because 'it is gone to' (arīyate gamyate), it is araññaṃ (a forest = vanaṃ). Because 'it abandons the lowliness of beings' (jahāti sattānaṃ hīnattanti), it is hiraññaṃ (wealth, and gold).

(Iti cavaggapaccayavidhānaṃ).

(Here ends the explanation of the suffixes of the ca-group.)

52. Kira tarā kīṭo.

52. From the roots kir and tar, the suffix is kīṭa.

Kira-vikiraṇe, tara-taraṇe, etehi, kīṭo hoti. Sobhetumettha ratanāni vikirīyantīti kirīṭaṃ=makuṭaṃ. Taraiti niddesā assa ittaṃ, taranti yanti surūpatta manenāti tirīṭaṃ=veṭṭhanaṃ.

From the root kir in the sense of 'scattering,' and from tar in the sense of 'crossing,' from these the suffix kīṭa is used. Because 'jewels are scattered on it for adornment' (sobhetum ettha ratanāni vikirīyanti), it is kirīṭaṃ (a crown = makuṭaṃ). From tar, with a becoming i as indicated; because 'they cross over and go with it, having a beautiful form' (taranti yanti surūpattaṃ anena), it is tirīṭaṃ (a diadem = veṭṭhanaṃ).

53. Sakādīhyaṭo.

53. From the roots beginning with sak, the suffix is aṭa.

Saka-sattiyaṃ, kasa-gamane, kara-karaṇe, makka iti suttiyo dhātu, deva-devane, kama-icchāyaṃ, evamādihi aṭo hoti. Saṇṇoti bhāraṃ vahitunti sakaṭo=yānaṃ. Akasi nirojattaṃ agamīti kasaṭaṃ=nirojaṃ. Karoti amanāpanti karaṭo=kāko[M 0.0245]. Makkati calatīti makkaṭo=vānaro. Devīyati pūjīyatīti devaṭo=isi. Kamati icchati ārohatthanti kamaṭo=vāmano.

From the root sak in the sense of 'being able'; from kas in the sense of 'going'; from kar in the sense of 'doing'; from the root makka according to the suttas; from dev in the sense of 'praising'; from kam in the sense of 'desiring'—from these and others the suffix aṭa is used. Because 'it is able to carry a load' (saṇṇoti bhāraṃ vahituṃ), it is sakaṭo (a cart = yānaṃ). Because 'it went to worthlessness' (akasi nirojattaṃ agami), it is kasaṭaṃ (dregs = nirojaṃ). Because 'it makes an unpleasant sound' (karoti amanāpaṃ), it is karaṭo (a crow = kāko). Because 'it moves' (makkati calati), it is makkaṭo (a monkey = vānaro). Because 'he is praised' (devīyati pūjīyati), he is a devaṭo (a sage = isi). Because 'it desires to climb' (kamati icchati ārohatthaṃ), it is kamaṭo (a tortoise = vāmano).

54. Makuṭāvāṭa kavāṭa kukkuṭā.

54. The words makuṭa, āvāṭa, kavāṭa, and kukkuṭa.

Ete saddā nipaccante. Maṃkismā uṭo, niggahītalopo ca, maṃketi sobhetīti makuṭaṃ=kirīṭaṃ. Avatismā āṭaṇa, avyate khaññateti āvāṭo=kāsu. Ku-saddetīmasmā āṭo, oavādesā yathāyogaṃ, kavati ravatīti kavāṭaṃ=dvārapidhānaṃ. Kuka vaka-ādānetīmasmā kuṭaka, kukati gocaramādadātīti kukkuṭo=tambacūḷo.

These words are formed irregularly. From the root maṅk, the suffix is uṭa, with elision of the niggahīta; because 'it adorns' (maṅketi sobheti), it is makuṭaṃ (a crown = kirīṭaṃ). From the root av, the suffix is āṭa; because 'it is dug' (avyate khaññate), it is āvāṭo (a pit = kāsu). From the root ku in the sense of 'making a sound,' the suffix is āṭa, with the substitution of av for o as appropriate; because 'it makes a sound' (kavati ravati), it is kavāṭaṃ (a door panel = dvārapidhānaṃ). From the root kuk or vak in the sense of 'taking,' the suffix is kuṭaka; because 'it takes its food' (kukati gocaram ādadāti), it is kukkuṭo (a rooster = tambacūḷo).

55. Kamusa kusa kasā ṭho.

55. From the roots kam, us, kus, and kas, the suffix is ṭha.

Kama-icchāyaṃ, usa-dāhe, kusa-akkose, kasa-gamane, etehiṭho hoti, niggahītavaggantā, odanādīni kāmetīti kaṇṭho=galo. Okkapararūpādīni, odanādīsu uṇhena usīyatī ti oṭṭho=dantacchado, karabho ca. Kusīyati akkosīyatīti koṭṭho=dhaññanilayo. Kasati yāti vināsanti kaṭṭhaṃ=dāru.

From the root kam in the sense of 'desiring'; from us in the sense of 'burning'; from kus in the sense of 'reviling'; and from kas in the sense of 'going'—from these the suffix ṭha is used, and the niggahīta becomes the nasal of its class. Because 'it desires food, etc.' (odanādīni kāmeti), it is kaṇṭho (the throat = galo). With vowel gradation, assimilation, and other such processes; because 'it is burned by hot food, etc.' (odanādīsu uṇhena usīyati), it is oṭṭho (a lip = dantacchado, and a camel = karabho). Because 'it is reviled' (kusīyati akkosīyati), it is koṭṭho (a storeroom = dhaññanilayo). Because 'it goes to destruction' (kasati yāti vināsaṃ), it is kaṭṭhaṃ (wood = dāru).

56. Kuṭṭhādayo.

56. The words beginning with kuṭṭha.

Kuṭṭhaādayo saddā ṭhantā nipaccante. Kusismā ṭho, ottābhāvo ca, kusīyati akkosīyatīti kuṭṭhaṃ=chavirogo. Kuṇa-sadde, pararūpābhāvo ottābhāvo ca, kuṇati nadatīti kuṇṭho=atikhiṇo, kuṇīyati akkosīyatīti kuṇṭho= chinnahatthapādādiko[M 0.0246]. Daṃsissa dā, daṃsati etāyāti dāṭhā=dantaviseso. Kamissa aka ca. Kāmīyāti dīnetīti kamaṭho=bhikkhābhājanaṃ, vāmano, kummo ca. Phassissa phuṭo, phassīyatīti phuṭṭho=phasso, evamaññepi.

The words beginning with kuṭṭha are formed irregularly with the suffix ṭha. From the root kus, the suffix is ṭha, with no change to the o-vowel; because 'it is reviled' (kusīyati akkosīyati), it is kuṭṭhaṃ (leprosy = a skin disease). From the root kuṇ in the sense of 'making a sound,' with no assimilation and no change to the o-vowel; because 'it makes a sound' (kuṇati nadati), it is kuṇṭho (very blunt); because 'one is reviled' (kuṇīyati akkosīyati), one is kuṇṭho (one with severed hands, feet, etc.). From the root daṃs, the suffix is dā; because 'one bites with it' (daṃsati etāya), it is dāṭhā (a fang = a special kind of tooth). From the root kam, the suffix is also aṭha; because 'it is desired' or 'is miserable' (kāmīyati dīneti), it is kamaṭho (an alms bowl, a dwarf, and a tortoise). The root phass is changed to phuṭ; because 'it is touched' (phassīyati), it is phuṭṭho (contact = phasso). And so for others.

57. Vara karā aṇḍo.

57. From the roots var and kar, the suffix is aṇḍa.

Vara-varaṇe, kara-karaṇe, etehi aṇḍo hoti. Attani pephaṃ vārayatīti varaṇḍo=mukharogo. Karīyatīti karaṇḍo=bhaṇḍaviseso.

From the root var in the sense of 'warding off', and from the root kar in the sense of 'doing', the suffix aṇḍa is applied. It wards off froth in oneself, thus varaṇḍa, a mouth disease. It is made, thus karaṇḍa, a particular kind of receptacle.

58. Manantā ḍo.

58. From roots ending in ma and na, the suffix ḍa is applied.

Makāra nakārantehi kriyatthehi bahulaṃ ḍappaccayo hoti. Sama-upasame, samanaṃ saṇḍaṃ=samūho. Kama-padavikkhepe, kamati yātīti kaṇḍo=saro, paricchedo ca, dama-damane, damantvyanenāti daṇḍo=niggaho. Ama gama-gamane, amanti uppajjanti etthāti aṇḍo=pakkhipasavo, koso ca. Gacchati sūnabhāvanti gaṇḍo=byādhi, vadanekadeso ca. Ramu-kīḷāyaṃ, ramanti etthāti ruṇḍā=vidhavā. Mana-ñāṇe, maññanti etenāti maṇḍo=odanādinissāvo. Khana khaṇa=avadāraṇe, khaññatīti khaṇḍo=ucchuvikāra viseso. Lama-hiṃsāyaṃ, lamati hiṃsati sucibhāvanti laṇḍo=vaccaṃ, evamaññepi.

The suffix ḍa is frequently applied to roots ending in the letters m and n that denote an action. From sam in the sense of calming: calming is saṇḍa = a group, a collection. From kam in the sense of stepping: it moves or goes, thus kaṇḍo = an arrow, and a section. From dam in the sense of taming: one tames with this, thus daṇḍo = punishment, restraint. From am and gam in the sense of going: they arise in this, thus aṇḍo = a bird's egg, and a sheath. It goes to a state of swelling, thus gaṇḍo = a boil, and a part of the face. From ram in the sense of delighting: they delight in this, thus ruṇḍā = a widow. From man in the sense of knowing: one knows with this, thus maṇḍo = the scum of rice, etc. From khan in the sense of breaking: it is broken, thus khaṇḍo = a piece, a special product of sugarcane. From lam in the sense of harming: it harms purity, thus laṇḍo = excrement. And so for others as well.

59. Kuṇḍā dayo.

59. The words kuṇḍa, etc.

Kuṇḍaādayo ḍantā nipaccante. Kama mana tanānaṃ assa uttaṃ, kāmīyatīti kuṇḍaṃ=bhājanaṃ. Maññati hitāhitanti muṇḍo= chinnakeso[M 0.0247]. Tanoti etenāti tuṇḍaṃ=lapanaṃ. Īra-khepe, eraṃādeso. Īrati kampatīti eraṇḍo=byagghapuccho, si-sevāyaṃ, sissa khamuka, sugandhaṃ sevatīti sikhaṇḍo=cūḷā, evamaññepi.

The words kuṇḍa, etc., are irregularly formed with the suffix ḍa. For the roots kam, man, and tan, the vowel a is changed to u. It is desired, thus kuṇḍaṃ = a pot. He considers what is beneficial and harmful, thus muṇḍo = one with a shaven head. One stretches with this, thus tuṇḍaṃ = a beak, a snout. From īr in the sense of shaking, there is the substitution of eraṃ. It shakes or trembles, thus eraṇḍo = the castor-oil plant. From si in the sense of frequenting, with the augments kha and mu; it frequents fragrance, thus sikhaṇḍo = a crest, a top-knot. And so for others as well.

60. Tija kasa tasa dakkhā kiṇo jassa kho ca.

60. From the roots tij, kas, tas, and dakkh, the suffix kiṇa is applied, and kh is substituted for j.

Tija-nisāne, kasa-gamane, tasa-pipāsāyaṃ, dakkha-vuddhiyaṃ, etehi kiṇo hoti, jassa kho ca, tejayitthāti tikhiṇaṃ=nisitaṃ. Kasati pavattatīti kasiṇaṃ=asesaṃ. Tasanaṃ tasiṇā=taṇhā. Dakkhati vuddhiṃ gacchati etāyāti dakkhīṇā=kusalaṃ.

From the root tij in the sense of sharpening, kas in the sense of going, tas in the sense of thirsting, and dakkh in the sense of growing, the suffix kiṇa is applied, and kh is substituted for j. It sharpens, thus tikhiṇaṃ = sharp, pointed. It goes on, thus kasiṇaṃ = whole, entire. Thirsting is tasiṇā = craving. One grows or increases by this, thus dakkhiṇā = a donation, what is skillful.

61. Vīādito ṇi.

61. From the roots vī, etc., the suffix ṇi is applied.

Vī-tantasantāne, si-sevāsaṃ, sū-passavane, du-gamane, kī-dabbavinīmaye, sā-tanukaraṇāvasānesu, evamādīhi ṇi hoti. Vīyatīti veṇi=kesakalāpo. Sevanaṃ seṇi=sajātīnaṃ kārūnaṃ samūho. Nipubbo, nisevīyatīti niseṇi=sopānaṃ. Savati passavatīti soṇi=kaṭi. Davati vahatīti doṇi=kaṭṭhambuvāhanī, nāvā ca. Nadādipāṭhā vimhi soṇī doṇī tipi hoti. Kayanaṃ, kīyate etāyāti vā keṇi=kayo sāti dukkhaṃ tanuṃ karotīti sāṇi=tirokaraṇī, evamaññepi.

From roots such as vī in the sense of weaving, si in the sense of serving, sū in the sense of issuing forth, du in the sense of going, kī in the sense of exchanging goods, sā in the sense of making thin and finishing, and so on, the suffix ṇi is applied. It is woven, thus veṇi = a braid of hair. Serving is seṇi = a guild, a group of artisans of the same kind. With the prefix ni, it is ascended, thus niseṇi = a ladder. It flows or issues forth, thus soṇi = the hip. It runs or carries, thus doṇi = a wooden water-trough, and a boat. By the rule for the nadī-group, they also become soṇī and doṇī. Buying, or it is bought with this, thus keṇi = purchase. It makes suffering thin, thus sāṇi = a curtain. And so for others as well.

62. Gahādīhyaṇi.

62. From the roots gah, etc., the suffix aṇi is applied.

Gaha-upādāne, ara-gamane, dhara-dhāraṇe, sara-gatiyiṃsā cintāsu, tara-taraṇe, evamādīhi aṇippaccayo hoti. Gaṇhātīti gahaṇi=asitādipācako aggi. Arīyati gamīyatīti araṇi=aggimanthanakaṭṭhaṃ[M 0.0248]. Dhāretīti dharaṇi=mahī. Sarīyati gamīyatīti bharaṇi=maggo. Tarantyanenāti taraṇi=nāvā, sūriyo ca.

From roots such as gah in the sense of grasping, ar in the sense of going, dhar in the sense of holding, sar in the senses of going, harming, and thinking, tar in the sense of crossing, and so on, the suffix aṇi is applied. It takes (food), thus gahaṇi = the digestive fire. One goes to it, thus araṇi = the fire-drilling stick. It supports, thus dharaṇi = the earth. One moves on it, thus saraṇi = a road. One crosses with this, thus taraṇi = a boat, and the sun.

63. Rīvībhāhi ṇu.

63. From the roots rī, vī, and bhā, the suffix ṇu is applied.

Rī-passavane, vī vā-gamane, bhā-dittiyaṃ, etehiṇu hoti. Rīyati passavatīti reṇu=rajo. Veti pavattatīti veṇu=veḷu. Bhāti dibbatīti bhāṇu=raṃsi.

From the root rī in the sense of issuing forth, vī or vā in the sense of going, and bhā in the sense of shining, the suffix ṇu is applied. It issues forth, thus reṇu = dust. It grows, thus veṇu = bamboo. It shines, thus bhāṇu = a ray of light.

64. Khāṇvā dayo.

64. The words khāṇu, etc.

Khāṇuādayo ṇuantā nipaccante. Khaṇa khana-avadāraṇe, ṇassa ā, khaññati avadārīyatīti khāṇu=chinnasākho rukkho. Jana-janane, nassa vā āttaṃ, jāyati gamana manenāti jāṇu, jaṇṇu=jaṅghorūnaṃ sandhi. Hara-haraṇe, eka, harīyatīti hareṇu=gandhadabba, evamaññepi.

The words khāṇu, etc., are irregularly formed with the suffix ṇu. From the root khan in the sense of breaking, the vowel of the root is lengthened: it is broken, thus khāṇu = a tree stump. From the root jan in the sense of being born, the vowel of the root is optionally lengthened: one is born or goes with this, thus jāṇu or jaṇṇu = the knee, the joint of the lower and upper leg. From the root har in the sense of carrying, the vowel is changed to e: it is carried, thus hareṇu = a fragrant powder. And so for others as well.

65. Kvādito ṇo.

65. From the roots ku, etc., the suffix ṇa is applied.

Ku-sadde, su-savane, du-gamane, vara-varaṇe, kara-karaṇe, paṇa-byavahārathutisu, tā-pālane, lī-nilīyane, evamādīhi ṇo hoti. Kavati nadati etthāti koṇo=assi, vīṇādivādanadaṇḍo ca. Suṇotīti soṇo=sunakho, naro ca. Davati pavattatīti doṇo=parimāṇaviseso. Virūpatta vāretīti vaṇṇo=nīlādi. Savanaṃ karotīti kaṇṇo=savanaṃ. Paṇīyati voharīyatīti paṇṇo=palāso. Lāyatīti tāṇaṃ=rakkhā. Nilīyanti etthāti leṇaṃ=nilīyanaṭṭhānaṃ.

From roots such as ku in the sense of making a sound, su in the sense of hearing, du in the sense of going, var in the sense of choosing, kar in the sense of doing, paṇ in the senses of transacting and praising, tā in the sense of protecting, lī in the sense of hiding, and so on, the suffix ṇa is applied. It sounds or makes a noise, thus koṇo = a corner, and a plectrum for a lute. It hears, thus soṇo = a dog, and a person. It runs or proceeds, thus doṇo = a particular measure. It wards off ugliness, thus vaṇṇo = appearance, color (blue, etc.). It performs hearing, thus kaṇṇo = the ear. It is transacted or used, thus paṇṇo = a leaf. It protects, thus tāṇaṃ = protection. They conceal themselves in it, thus leṇaṃ = a hiding place.

66. Suvīhi ṇaka.

66. From the roots su and vī, the suffix ṇaka is applied.

Su-savane[M 0.0249], vī-tantasantāne, etehi ṇaka hoti. Suṇotīti suṇo=sunakho. Vīyatīti vīṇā=vallakī.

From the root su in the sense of hearing, and vī in the sense of weaving, the suffix ṇaka is applied. It hears, thus suṇo = a dog (sunakho). It is woven, thus vīṇā = a lute (vallakī).

67. Tiṇādayo.

67. The words tiṇa, etc.

Tiṇaādayo ṇakantā nipaccante. Tija-tejane, jalopo, tejeti etenāti tiṇaṃ=bīraṇādi. Lī liha sāda kledānaṃ lo lavā, līyati rasato sabbattha allīyatīti loṇaṃ lavaṇaṃ, lehīyatīti loṇaṃ lavaṇaṃ, sādīyatīti loṇaṃ lavaṇaṃ, kledayatīti loṇaṃ lavaṇaṃ, gamissa o, gacchatīti goṇo=go. Hara-haraṇe, ṇassañji, harīyatīti hariṇo=migo. Īra-kampane, rassattaṃ, ṇassa ñica, attano lūkhabhāve sampatte īrati kampatīti iriṇaṃ=ūsaraṃ. Thu-abhitthave, dīgho, abhitthavīyatīti thūṇaṃ=nagaraṃ, thūṇo=gharatthambho, evamaññepi.

The words tiṇa, etc., are irregularly formed with the suffix ṇaka. From the root tij in the sense of sharpening, with elision of ja: one sharpens with it, thus tiṇaṃ = grass, such as bīraṇa grass. From the roots lī, lih, sād, and kled, the forms loṇa and lavaṇa are derived: it dissolves and pervades everywhere with its taste, or it is licked, or it is tasted, or it moistens, thus loṇaṃ or lavaṇaṃ = salt. From the root gam, with o substituted for the root: it goes, thus goṇo = an ox. From the root har in the sense of carrying, with the augment i before the suffix: it is carried, thus hariṇo = a deer. From the root īr in the sense of trembling, with shortening of the vowel and the augment i before the suffix: having reached a state of roughness, it trembles, thus iriṇaṃ = barren soil. From the root thu in the sense of praising, with lengthening of the vowel: it is praised, thus thūṇaṃ = a town, and thūṇo = a house-pillar. And so for others as well.

68. Ravaṇa varaṇa pūraṇā dayo.

68. The words ravaṇa, varaṇa, pūraṇa, etc.

Ravaṇa varaṇa pūraṇā dayo aṇappaccayena siddhā. Ravatīti ravaṇo=kokilo. Vāretīti varaṇo=pākāro. Pūrīyate anenāti pūraṇo=paripūrī.

The words ravaṇa, varaṇa, pūraṇa, etc., are formed with the suffix aṇa. It makes a sound, thus ravaṇo = the cuckoo. It wards off, thus varaṇo = an enclosure wall. It is filled by this, thus pūraṇo = completion.

(Iti ṭavaggapaccayavidhānaṃ).

(Thus ends the section on the suffixes of the ṭ-class.)

69. Pāvasā ati.

69. From the roots pā and vas, the suffix ati is applied.

Pā-rakkhaṇe, vasa-nivāse, eteti ati hoti. Pubbasaralopo, pāti rakkhatīti pati=sāmī, vasanti etthāti vasati=gehaṃ.

From the root pā in the sense of protecting, and vas in the sense of dwelling, the suffix ati is applied. There is elision of the preceding vowel. He protects, thus pati = a master. They dwell in it, thus vasati = a dwelling.

70. Dhā hi si tana jana jara gama sacā tu.

70. From the roots dhā, hi, si, tan, jan, jar, gam, and sac, the suffix tu is applied.

Dhā-dhāraṇe[M 0.0250], hi-gatiyaṃ, tana-vitthāre, jana-janane, jara-vayo-hāniyaṃ, ama gama-gamane, saca-samavāye, etehi tu hoti. Dhāretīti dhātu=gerukādi. Hinoti pavattāti phalaṃ etenāti hetu=kāraṇaṃ, sevīyati janehīti setu=bandhati (paddhati). Taññateti tantu=suttaṃ. Janīyate kammakilesehīti jantu, jāyati kammakilehīti vā jantu=satto. Jīratīti jattu=aṃsasandhi. Gacchatīti gantu=gamiko, sacati sametīti sattu=yavādicuṇṇaṃ.

From the root dhā in the sense of holding, hi in the sense of moving, si in the sense of serving, tan in the sense of stretching, jan in the sense of being born, jar in the sense of aging, gam in the sense of going, and sac in the sense of being associated, the suffix tu is applied. It holds, thus dhātu = an element, such as red ochre. It impels, or a fruit proceeds from this, thus hetu = a cause. It is resorted to by people, thus setu = a causeway. It is stretched, thus tantu = a thread. It is born from kamma and defilements, or it is born from kamma and defilements, thus jantu = a living being. It decays, thus jattu = the collarbone. He goes, thus gantu = a traveler. It adheres or combines, thus sattu = flour, such as barley meal.

71. Arissuṭa ca.

71. From the root ar, the suffix tu is also applied, with substitution of uṭa.

Ara-gamanetīmasmā tu hoti, arissa uṭa ādesoca. Arati pavattatīti utu=hemantādi,

From this root ar in the sense of going, the suffix tu is applied, and uṭa is substituted for the root ar. It goes on or proceeds, thus utu = a season, such as winter.

72. Pitvādayo.

72. The words pitu, etc.

Pituādayo saddā tuantā nipaccante. Pā-rakkhaṇe, āssa ittaṃ, pāti rakkhatīti pitā=janako. Pātissevādissa mo, pāyetīti mātā=jananī. Bhā-dittiyaṃ, bhātīti bhātā=sodariyo. Dhā-dhāraṇe, āssa īttaṃ, dhārīyatīti dhītā=puttī. Duha-papūraṇe, ottābhāvo, tussa ñchica. Duhati pasave papūretīti duhitā=puttī. Jana-janane, assa āttaṃ, mā cāntādeso. Paputte janetīti jāmātā=duhitupati. Naha-bandhane, nahīyati bandhīyati pemenāti nattā-paputto. Hu-havane, havati pūjetīti hotā=yaññako. Pū-pavane, punāti [M 0.0251] āyatiṃ bhavaṃ pavittaṃ karotīti potā=soyeva.

The words pitu, etc., are irregularly formed with the suffix tu. From the root pā in the sense of protecting, with i substituted for ā: he protects, thus pitā = father. She gives drink, thus mātā = mother. From the root bhā in the sense of shining: he shines, thus bhātā = brother. From the root dhā in the sense of supporting, with ī substituted for ā: she is supported, thus dhītā = daughter. From the root duh in the sense of milking: she milks or fills the vessel, thus duhitā = daughter. From the root jan in the sense of begetting, with lengthening of the vowel and substitution of mā at the end: he begets grandsons, thus jāmātā = son-in-law. From the root nah in the sense of binding: he is bound by love, thus nattā = a grandson. From the root hu in the sense of sacrificing: he sacrifices or worships, thus hotā = a sacrificial priest. From the root pū in the sense of purifying: he purifies the future existence, thus potā = the same.

73. Jana karā ratu.

73. From the roots jan and kar, the suffix ratu is applied.

Jana-janane, kara-karaṇe, etehi ratu hoti, rakāro antasarādilopattho. Jāyatīti jatu=lākhā. Karīyatīti katu=sayūpo yañño.

From the root jan in the sense of being born, and kar in the sense of doing, the suffix ratu is applied; the letter r in the suffix indicates the elision of the final vowel of the root. It is produced, thus jatu = lac. It is performed, thus katu = a sacrifice with a post.

74. Sakā unto.

74. From the root sak, the suffix unta is applied.

Saka-sattiyamiccasmā unto hoti. Sakkotīti sakunto=pakkhī.

From this root sak in the sense of being able, the suffix unta is applied. It is able, thus sakunto = a bird.

75. Kapā oto.

75. From the root kap, the suffix ota is applied.

Kapa-acchādane iccasmā oto hoti. Kapatīti kapoto=pārevato. Ṭo tassa vā hoti kapoṭo=soyeva.

From this root kap in the sense of covering, the suffix ota is applied. It covers, thus kapoto = a pigeon. Alternatively, its t becomes ṭ, giving kapoṭo, the same.

76. Vasādīhyanto.

76. From the roots vas, etc., the suffix anta is applied.

Vasa-nivāse, ruha-janane, bhadda-kalyāṇe, nanda-samiddhiyaṃ, jīva-pāṇadhāraṇe, evamādīti anto hohi. Vasanti etasmiṃ kāle kīḷāpasutāti vasanto=utu. Ruhati jāyatīti ruhanto=rukkho, evaṃnāmako migarājā ca. Bhaddissa saṃyogādilopo, bhajati kalyāṇadhammanti bhadanto=pabbajito. Nandati etāyāti nandantī=sakhī, nadādipāṭhā vī, evamupari ca. Jīvanti etā- yāti [M 0.0252] jīvantī=osadhi. Savatīti savantī=nadī. Rodāpetīti rodantī=osadhi. Avati rakkhatīti avantī=janapado.

From roots such as vas in the sense of dwelling, ruh in the sense of growing, nand in the sense of prospering, jīv in the sense of sustaining life, and from the noun bhadda in the sense of auspiciousness, and so on, the suffix anta is applied. They dwell devoted to play in this time, thus vasanto = the spring season. It grows or is born, thus ruhanto = a tree, and a lion of that name. From the word bhadda, with elision of the first member of the consonant cluster; he cultivates good qualities, thus bhadanto = a venerable one, a monk. She delights in this, thus nandantī = a female friend; the long ī is by the rule for the nadī-group, and similarly for the following. They live by this, thus jīvantī = a medicinal plant. It flows, thus savantī = a river. It makes one cry, thus rodantī = a medicinal plant. It protects, thus avantī = a country.

77. Hisīnaṃ muka ca.

77. From the roots hi and sī, the suffix anta is applied, with the augment muka.

Hi-gatiya, sī-saye, etehi anto hoti muka ca. Kakāro antāvayavattho, himaṃ hinoti pavattati etasminti hemanto=utu, sayanti ettha ūkā kusumādayo cāti sīmanto=kesamaggo.

From the roots hi (in the sense of going) and sī (in the sense of lying), the suffix anta is applied, with the augment muka. The letter ka indicates it is a final augment. hemanto, the cold season, is so called because it makes the snow (hima) go (hinoti) or proceed from it. sīmanto, the parting of the hair, is so called because lice, flowers, and so on lie (sayanti) there.

78. Hara ruha kulā ito.

78. From the roots hara, ruha, and kula, the suffix ita is applied.

Hara-haraṇe, ruha-janane, kula-patthāre, eteti ito hoti. Attano sinehaṃ haratīti harito=vaṇṇaviseso. Ruhatīti rohito=macchaviseso. Ruhati sarīre byāpanavasenāti rohitaṃ, rassa latte lohitaṃ=rudhiraṃ. Attano guṇaṃ kulati pattharatīti kolito=dutiyaggasāvako, evaṃ nāmako maru ca.

From the roots hara (in the sense of taking), ruha (in the sense of growing), and kula (in the sense of spreading), the suffix ita is applied. Because it takes away one's affection, it is harita, a particular color. Because it grows, it is rohita, a particular kind of fish. Because it grows by pervading the body, it is rohitaṃ; when r becomes l, it is lohitaṃ, blood. Because he spreads his own virtues, he is Kolita, the second chief disciple, and also a maru of that name.

79. Bharādīhyato.

79. From the root bhara and others, the suffix ata is applied.

Bhara raṃja yaja paca evamādīhi ato hoti. Bharatīti bharato=naṭo. Niggahītalopo, rañjanti etthāhi rajataṃ=sajjhaṃ. Yajitabboti yajato=aggi. Pacatīti pacato=sūpakāro.

From roots such as bhara (to bear), rañj (to be colored/delighted), yaj (to sacrifice), and pac (to cook), the suffix ata is applied. Because he bears, he is bharato, an actor. With elision of the nasal, rajataṃ, silver, is so called because they delight in it. Because it is to be sacrificed to, it is yajato, fire. Because he cooks, he is pacato, a cook.

80. Kirā dīhyātaka.

80. From the root kira and others, the suffix ātaka is applied.

Kira-vikiraṇe, ala-bandhane, cila-vasane, evamādīhi ātaka hoti, kiratīti kirāto=savaro, rassa lakke ki- lāto=sova[M 0.0253]. Alatīti alātaṃ=ummukaṃ. Cilatīti cilāto=malacchajāti.

From roots such as kira (to scatter), ala (to adorn/prevent), and cila (to wear), the suffix ātaka is applied. Because he scatters, he is kirāto, a savage. When r becomes l, it is kilāto, the same. Because it adorns, it is alātaṃ, a firebrand. Because he wears rags, he is cilāto, a person of a barbarian tribe.

81. Amādīhyatto.

81. From the root am and others, the suffix atta is applied.

Ama mā vara kalādīhi atto hoti. Amati kālantaraṃ pavattatīti amattaṃ=bhājanaṃ. Pubbasaralopo, mānaṃ mattaṃ=pamāṇaṃ paricchedo ca. Varantunenāti varattā=yottaṃ. Kalati paricchindatīti kalattaṃ=bhariyā.

From roots such as am (to go), mā (to measure), vara (to choose), and kal (to count), the suffix atta is applied. Because it continues for another time, amattaṃ is an earthenware vessel. With elision of the preceding vowel, mānaṃ becomes mattaṃ, meaning measure or limitation. Because one encloses with it, varattā is a tether. Because she delimits, kalattaṃ is a wife.

82. Vādīhi to.

82. From the root vā and others, the suffix ta is applied.

Vā-gamane, tā-pālane, tana-vitthāre, dama-upasame, a-magamane, si-sevāyaṃ, su-savane, pū pavane, gupa-govane, yuja-saṃyame, gaha-upādāne, ata-sātaccagamāna, khipa-peraṇe, evamādīhi to hoti. Vāyatīti vāto=vāyu. Tāyatīti tāto=pitā. Tanuteti tantaṃ=tantavo. Damatīti anto=dasano. Amati yātīti anto=osānaṃ, koṭṭhāsasamīpāvayavā ca. Sevīyatīti seto=dhavalo. Suṇantunenāti sotaṃ=savanaṃ. Savatīti soto=jalappavāho. Punīyatīti poto=bālo. Gopīyatīti gotthaṃ=kalādi. Yojantyanenāti yottaṃ=rajju. Mamāyantehi gayhatīti gattaṃ=sarīraṃ. Abādhaṃ nirantaraṃ atati pavattatīti attā=manādi. Khipīyati etthāti khettaṃ=kedāraṃ.

From roots such as vā (to go), tā (to protect), tan (to stretch), dam (to tame), am (to go), si (to serve), su (to hear), pū (to purify), gup (to guard), yuj (to yoke), gah (to grasp), at (to go continuously), and khip (to throw), the suffix ta is applied. Because it blows, it is vāto, wind. Because he protects, he is tāto, father. Because it stretches, it is tantaṃ, thread. Because it tames, it is danto, a tooth. Because it goes, it is anto, an end, a part, vicinity, or member. Because it is resorted to, it is seto, white. Because one hears with it, it is sotaṃ, the ear. Because it flows, it is soto, a stream. Because he is purified, he is poto, a child or the young of an animal. Because it is guarded, it is gotthaṃ, a cattle-pen. Because one yokes with it, it is yottaṃ, a rope. Because it is grasped by those who have a sense of 'mine,' it is gattaṃ, the body. Because it proceeds unhindered and continuously, it is attā, the self, mind, etc. Because something is thrown into it, it is khettaṃ, a field.

83. Gharādīhi taka.

83. From the root ghar and others, the suffix taka is applied.

Gara ghara-secane, si-sevāyaṃ, dū-paritāpane, mida-sinehe, cita-sañcetane, pusa-posane, vida-lābhe, evamādīhi taka [M 0.0254]4 hoti, gharati siñcatīti ghataṃ=sappi. Sevīyatīti sito=seto. Dubbacattā dūyati paritāpetīti dūto=pesarakāro. Mijjati sinehatīti mitto=suhadayo. Cintetīti cittaṃ=viññāṇaṃ cittakammādi ca. Posīyatīti putto=attajo. Vindanti pīti manenāti vittaṃ=dhanaṃ. Vara-varaṇasambhattīsu, varaṇaṃ vattaṃ=brahmacariyādi.

From roots such as gar/ghar (to sprinkle), si (to serve), dū (to be in pain), mid (to be affectionate), cit (to think), pus (to nourish), and vid (to find), the suffix taka is applied. Because it is sprinkled, it is ghataṃ, ghee. Because it is resorted to, it is sito, white. Because he is tormented due to being difficult to speak to, he is dūto, a messenger. Because he is affectionate, he is mitto, a friend. Because it thinks, it is cittaṃ, consciousness, artwork, etc. Because he is nourished, he is putto, a son. Because they find it with a joyful mind, it is vittaṃ, wealth. From the root var (in the sense of choosing or devotion), varaṇaṃ is vattaṃ, conduct, such as the holy life.

84. Nettādayo.

84. Netta and others.

Nettaādayo taka parā nipaccante. Nī-pāpane, ettaṃ, tuka ca nipātanā. Nayati pāpetīti nettaṃ=nayanaṃ, netā ca. Kara-kara-ṇe, assu, karaṇaṃ kuttaṃ=kiriyā. Kamissa assu, kamati yātīti kunto=āvudhaviseso. Rama-kīḷāyaṃ, supubbo, sussaniccaṃ dīgho. Suṭṭhu ramaṇaṃ, suṭṭhu ramatīti vā sūrato=sukhasaṃvāso. Mihissaissu, mihati siñcatīti muttaṃ=passāvo. Pāla=rakkhaṇe āssa rassattaṃ, ñica. Pālīyatīti palitaṃ=kesalomānaṃ jarāya kataṃ setattaṃ, saddhādittā akāre taṃ yassa atthi so palito=pumā, palitā=itthī. Mhissa si, mihi ca, mhayanaṃ sitaṃ=mandahasitaṃ, mhayanaṃ mihitaṃ=tadeva, kusa-akkose tassa īña, kusīyati akkosīyatīti kusīto=alaso, si=bandhane, dīgho, senti bandhanti gharāvāsaṃ etāyāti sītā=naṅgalalekhā, evamaññepi.

`Netta` and others are irregularly formed with the suffix `ta` and others. From the root `nī` (to lead), `etta` and `tuka` are irregular suffixes; because it leads, it is `nettaṃ` (the eye) and `netā` (a leader). From the root `kar` (to do), `kuttaṃ` (action) is an irregular formation. From the root `kam` (to go), `kunto` (a spear) is so called because it goes. From the root `ram` (to play), with the prefix `su-`, the vowel of `su` is always long; `sūrata` (a pleasant companion) is one who plays well. From the root `mih` (to sprinkle), `muttaṃ` (urine) is so called because it sprinkles. From the root `pāl` (to protect), its `ā` is shortened; `palitaṃ` (grey hair) is the whiteness of hair caused by old age. A person having this is `palito` (m.) or `palitā` (f.). From the root `smi` (to smile), `sitaṃ` and `mihitaṃ` mean a gentle smile. From the root `kus` (to revile), `kusīto` (lazy) is so called because one is reviled. From the root `si` (to bind), with lengthening, `sītā` (a furrow) is so called because they bind the household life with it. And so for others.

85. Samādīhyatho.

85. From `sam` and others, the suffix `atha`.

Sama-upasame[M 0.0255], dara-daraṇe, dama-upasame, kilama klama-gelaññe, sapa-akkose, vasa-nivāse, āpubbo, evamādīhi atho hoti. Sametīti samatho=samādhi. Daraṇaṃ daratho=pīḷā. Damanaṃ damatho=damo. Kilamanaṃ kilamatho=parissamo. Sapanaṃ sapatho=saccakaraṇaṃ. Āvasanti etthāti āvasatho=gharaṃ.

From roots such as `sam` (to be calm), `dar` (to split), `dam` (to tame), `kilam`/`klam` (to be weary), `sap` (to curse), and `vas` (to dwell) with the prefix `ā-`, the suffix `atha` is added. Because it calms, it is `samatho`, concentration. Splitting is `daratho`, oppression. Taming is `damatho`, self-control. Weariness is `kilamatho`, exertion. Cursing is `sapatho`, an oath. Because they dwell there, it is `āvasatho`, a house.

86. Upavasā vassoṭa ca.

86. From `vas` with `upa-`, `vassa` becomes `oṭa`.

Upapubbā vasatismā atho hoti, vassa oṭa cādeso. Upavasanti etthāti uposatho=tithiviseso, navamahatthi kulañca.

From the root `vas` preceded by `upa-`, the suffix `atha` is added, and `vassa` is substituted by `oṭa`. Because they observe a fast (`upavasanti`) on it, it is `uposatho`, a particular day of the lunar month, and also the name of an elephant family.

87. Ramā thaka.

87. From `ram`, the suffix `thaka`.

Ramatismā thaka hoti, kānubandhakaraṇasāmatthiyā ata kārādopi malopo. Ramanti kīḷanti etenāti ratho=sandano.

From the root `ram`, the suffix `thaka` is added. By the force of `k` being an indicatory letter, the `m` of the root is elided. Because they delight and play with it, it is `ratho`, a chariot.

88. Titthādayo.

88. `Tittha` and others.

Titthaādayo thakaparā nipaccante. Tara-taraṇe, assa ittaṃ, pararūpādi, tarantyanenāti titthaṃ=najjādiṃ yenāvataranti taṃ. Sica-rakkhaṇe, secatīti sittaṃ=madhucchiṭṭhaṃ. Hasa-hasane, hasantyanenāti hattho=karo, nakkhattāñca. Gāyatīti gāthā=pajjaviseso. Aranti pavattantyanenāti attho=dhanaṃ. Rogaṃ tudati pīḷetīti tutthaṃ=osadhaṃ. Yu-missane, dīgho, yavatīti yū- tho=sajātikānaṃ [M 0.0256] tiracchānānaṃsamūho. Gupa-gopane, dīgho, palopo, paṭikūlattā gopīyatīti gūtho=vaccaṃ, evamaññepi.

`Tittha` and others are irregularly formed with the suffix `tha` and others. From the root `tar` (to cross), its vowel becomes `i`; because they cross with it, it is `titthaṃ`, a ford. From the root `sic` (to protect), because it sprinkles, it is `sittaṃ`, beeswax. From the root `has` (to laugh), because they laugh with it, it is `hattho`, the hand, and also a constellation. Because it is sung, it is `gāthā`, a verse. Because one proceeds with it, it is `attho`, wealth or meaning. Because it strikes disease, it is `tutthaṃ`, medicine. From the root `yu` (to mix), with lengthening, because it mixes, it is `yūtho`, a herd. From the root `gup` (to guard), with lengthening and elision of `p`, because it is hidden due to its repulsiveness, it is `gūtho`, excrement. And so for others.

89. Vasa masa kusā thu.

89. From `vas`, `mas`, and `kus`, the suffix `thu`.

Vasa-nivāse, masa-āmasane, kusa-akkose, etehi thu hoti. Vasanti etthāti vatthu=padattho. Dadhiṃ āmasatīti matthu=dadhimaṇḍo. Kusīyati akkosīyati bhera vanādattāti kotthu=sigālo.

From the roots `vas` (to dwell), `mas` (to touch), and `kus` (to revile), the suffix `thu` is added. Because they dwell in it, it is `vatthu`, an object or basis. Because it touches the curd, it is `matthu`, whey. Because it is reviled for its terrifying sound, it is `kotthu`, a jackal.

90. Saka vasā thi.

90. From `sak` and `vas`, the suffix `thi`.

Saka-sattiyaṃ, vasa-nivāse, etehi thi hoti. Sakkoti gantumanenāti satthi=ūru. Vasīyati acchādīyatīti vatthi=nābhiyā adho.

From the roots `sak` (to be able) and `vas` (to dwell), the suffix `thi` is added. Because one is able to go with it, it is `satthi`, the thigh. Because it is covered, it is `vatthi`, the bladder, which is below the navel.

91. Vīto thika.

91. From `vī`, the suffix `thika`.

Vī vā-gamanetīmasmā thika hoti. Vīyanti gacchanti etāyāti vīthi=āvali.

From the root `vī` or `vā` (in the sense of going), the suffix `thika` is added. Because they go along it, it is `vīthi`, a street or row.

92. Sārismā rati.

92. From the causative of `sar`, the suffix `rathi`.

Sārismā ṇyantā rathi hoti. Sāretīti sārathi=ratha-vāho.

From the causative form of the root `sar`, the suffix `rathi` is added. Because he makes the horses go, he is `sārathi`, a chariot-driver.

93. Tā-tā ithi.

93. From `tā` and `at`, the suffix `ithi`.

Tā-pālane, ata-sātaccagamane, etehi ithi hoti. Tāyati pāletīti tithi=paṭipadādi, atati gacchatīti atithi=abbhāgato.

From the roots `tā` (to protect) and `at` (to go continuously), the suffix `ithi` is added. Because it protects, it is `tithi`, a lunar day. Because he goes continuously, he is `atithi`, a guest.

94. Isā thī.

94. From `is`, the suffix `thī`.

Isatismā [M 0.0257] thī hoti. Icchati icchīyatīti vā itthī=nārī.

From the root `is` (to desire), the suffix `thī` is added. Because she desires or is desired, she is `itthī`, a woman.

95. Ruda khuda muda mada chida sūda sapa kamā daka.

95. From `rud`, `khud`, `mud`, `mad`, `chid`, `sūd`, `sap`, and `kam`, the suffix `daka`.

Etehi daka hoti. Rudatīti ruddo=umāpati. Rassa latte luddo=nesādo. Khudati asahatīti khuddo=nīco. Modanti etāyāti muddā=sakkharamaṅguliyaṃ. Majjanti asminti maddo=janapado. Chijjatīti chiddaṃ=randhaṃ. Ūssa rassattaṃ, sūdati sāmikehi bhatiṃ pakkharatīti suddo=vasalo. Sapantunenāti saddo=sotavisayo. Kāmīyatīti kando=mūlaviseso.

From these roots, the suffix `daka` is added. Because he weeps, he is `ruddo`, the husband of Umā. When `r` becomes `l`, it is `luddo`, a hunter. Because he is intolerant, he is `khuddo`, a lowly person. Because they rejoice with it, it is `muddā`, a seal ring. Because they are intoxicated in it, it is `maddo`, the Madda country. Because it is cut, it is `chiddaṃ`, a hole. With shortening of `ū`, because he prepares food for wages from his masters, he is `suddo`, a commoner. Because one curses with it, it is `saddo`, sound. Because it is desired, it is `kando`, a bulbous root.

96. Kundādayo.

96. `Kunda` and others.

Kundaādayo dakaantā nipaccante. Kamissa assu, kāmīyatīti kundo=pupphavidhasaso, maṇissa mana, maññateti mando=jaḷo. Vuṇātissa buna, vuṇīyati saṃvarīyatīti bundo=mūlappadeso. Ninda-garahāyaṃ, nalopo, nindīyatīti niddā=soppaṃ. Unda-kiledane, nalopo, undati kiledatīti uddo=jalabiḷālo. Saṃpubbassa undissa ca, sammā undati kiledatīti samuddo=sāgaro. Pula-mahattahiṃ sāñāṇesu, imuña, pulati hiṃsatīti pulindo=savaro. Evaṃ-maññepi.

`Kunda` and others are irregularly formed with the suffix `daka`. From `kam` (to desire), `kundo` (jasmine) is so called because it is desired. From `man` (to think), `mando` (a fool) is so called because he imagines. From `vuṇā` (to cover), `bundo` (a root-stalk) is so called because it is covered. From `nind` (to blame), with elision of `n`, `niddā` (sleep) is so called because it is blamed. From `und` (to be wet), with elision of `n`, `uddo` (an otter) is so called because it gets wet. From `und` with the prefix `saṃ-`, `samuddo` (the ocean) is so called because it is thoroughly wet. From `pul` (to hurt), `pulindo` (a savage) is so called because he hurts. And so for others.

97. Dadā du.

97. From `dadā`, the suffix `du`.

Dada-dānetīmasmā du hoti. Dukkhaṃ dadātīhi daddu=kuṭṭhaviseso.

From the root `dad` in the sense of giving, the suffix `du` is added. Because it gives suffering, it is `daddu`, a type of skin disease, which is a particular kind of leprosy.

98. Khanāna dama ramā dho.

98. From `khan`, `an`, `dam`, and `ram`, the suffix `dho`.

Khana [M 0.0258] khaṇa-avadāraṇe, ana-pāṇane, dama-upasame, rama-kīḷāyaṃ, etehi dho hoti. Ñāṇena dhaññateti khandho=rāsi. Anati jīvati etenāti andho=acakkhuko. Dametabboti dandho=jaḷo, ramanti ettha sappādayoti randhaṃ=chiddaṃ.

From the roots `khan`/`khaṇa` (to dig/break open), `ana` (to breathe), `dam` (to tame), and `ram` (to play), the suffix `dho` is added. Because it is made known by knowledge, it is `khandho`, an aggregate or heap. Because one lives by it, one is `andho`, blind or sightless. Because one is to be tamed, one is `dandho`, slow or dull. Because snakes and so forth delight therein, it is `randhaṃ`, a hole or perforation.

99. Muddhā dayo.

99. `Muddha` and others.

Muddhaādayo dhantā nipaccante. Muda-tose, ottābhāvo, modanti ettha ūkāti muddhā=matthako. Ara-gamane, aranti yanti etthāti addhā=maggo, kālo ca, addhaṃ=upaddhaṃ. Gidha-abhi kaṅkhāyaṃ, issa attaṃ, gedhatīti gaddho=gijjho. Vidha-vedhane, ettābhāvo, parivajjhatīti viddhaṃ=vimalaṃ, evamaññepi.

Words such as muddhā are irregularly formed with the suffix 'dha'. From the root 'mud' in the sense of 'to rejoice', with 'o' becoming 'u'; because lice rejoice therein, it is 'muddhā', meaning 'head' (matthako). From the root 'ar' in the sense of 'to go'; because they go therein, it is 'addhā', meaning 'path' (maggo) and also 'time' (kālo); and 'addhaṃ', meaning 'a half' (upaddhaṃ). From the root 'gidh' in the sense of 'to desire greedily', with 'i' becoming 'a'; because it desires greedily, it is 'gaddho', meaning 'vulture' (gijjho). From the root 'vidh' in the sense of 'to pierce', with 'e' becoming 'i'; because it is avoided, it is 'viddhaṃ', meaning 'stainless' (vimalaṃ). And so with others.

100. Sīto dhuka.

100. From the root 'sī', the suffix 'dhuka'.

Setismā dhuka hoti. Sayanti etāyāti sīdhu=surāviseso.

From the root 'sī', the suffix 'dhuka' is used. Because they are bound by it (sayanti etāya), it is 'sīdhu', meaning 'a type of spirituous liquor' (surāviseso).

101. Varārakarataradarayamaajjamithasakā kuno.

101. From the roots 'vara', 'ara', 'kara', 'tara', 'dara', 'yama', 'ajja', 'mitha', and 'saka', the suffix 'kuno'.

Vara-varaṇasambhattīsu, ara-gamane, kara-karaṇe, tara-tara-ṇe dara-vidāraṇe, yama-uparame, ajja sajja-ajjane, mitha-saṅgame, saka-sattiyaṃ, etehi kuno hoti. “Rā nassa ṇo”ti (5-171) nassa ṇattaṃ, vāretīti varuṇo=evaṃnāmako isi, devarājā, pādapo ca. Arati gacchatīti aruṇo=sūriyo, tassa [M 0.0259] sārathi ca. Paradukkhe sati sādhūnaṃ hadayakammanaṃ karotīti karuṇā=dayā. Bālabhāvaṃ atarīti taruṇo=yuvā. “Ṇiṇāpina”nti (5.160) yogavibhāgā ṇilopo, vidāretīti dāruṇo=kakkhaḷo. Yameti pāvaṃ nāsetīti yamunā=ekā mahānadī. Ajjati dhanasañcayaṃ karotīti ajjuno=rājā, rukkhaviseso ca. Mitho saṅgamo mithunaṃ=pumitthiyugaḷaṃ. Sakkotīti sakuno=pakkhī. Nadādipāṭhā vīmhi=sakunī. “Tathanarānaṃṭaṭṭhaṇalā”ti (1-27) vā ṇatte=sakuṇo, sakuṇi.

From the roots 'vara' (in the sense of choosing and bestowing), 'ara' (to go), 'kara' (to do), 'tara' (to cross), 'dara' (to split), 'yama' (to restrain), 'ajja' and 'sajja' (to acquire), 'mitha' (to unite), and 'saka' (to be able), from these the suffix 'kuno' is used. By the rule 'Rā nassa ṇo' (5-171), 'na' becomes 'ṇa'. Because he wards off (vāreti), he is 'varuṇo', a sage of that name, a king of the gods, and also a tree. Because he goes (arati gacchati), he is 'aruṇo', the sun, and also his charioteer. Because, when there is suffering in others, it causes the hearts of the good to tremble (sādhūnaṃ hadayakammanaṃ karoti), it is 'karuṇā', meaning 'compassion' (dayā). Because he has crossed over the state of childhood (bālabhāvaṃ atari), he is 'taruṇo', meaning 'a youth' (yuvā). By the rule 'Ṇiṇāpina' (5.160), through splitting the rule, there is elision of 'ṇi'; because it splits (vidāreti), it is 'dāruṇo', meaning 'harsh' (kakkhaḷo). Because it restrains and destroys evil (yameti pāpaṃ nāseti), it is 'yamunā', a great river. Because he acquires, that is, accumulates wealth (ajjati dhanasañcayaṃ karoti), he is 'ajjuno', a king, and also a specific tree. Mutual union (mitho saṅgamo) is 'mithunaṃ', meaning 'a male and female pair' (pumitthiyugaḷaṃ). Because it is able (sakkoti), it is 'sakuno', meaning 'a bird' (pakkhī). From its inclusion in the 'nadādi' group, in the feminine it is 'sakunī'. Or by the rule 'Tathanarānaṃṭaṭṭhaṇalā' (1-27), with the suffix 'ṇa', it becomes 'sakuṇo' or 'sakuṇi'.

102. Ajā ino.

102. From the root 'aj', the suffix 'ino'.

Aja vaja-gamane tīmasmā ino hoti. Ajati vikkayaṃ yātīti ajinaṃ=cammaṃ.

From the roots 'aj' and 'vaj' in the sense of 'to go', the suffix 'ino' is used. Because it goes to be sold (ajati vikkayaṃ yāti), it is 'ajinaṃ', meaning 'hide' (cammaṃ).

103. Vipinādayo.

103. Words such as vipina.

Vipinaādayo inantā nipaccante. Vapa-bījanikkhepe, assa ittaṃ, vapanti etthāti vipinaṃ=vanaṃ. Supa-saye, supanti etenāti supinaṃ=niddā, supantena diṭṭhañca. Tuda-byathane, dassa ho, tudati satte pīḷetīti tuhinaṃ=himaṃ. Kappa-sāmatthiye, kappati ripavo vijetuṃ samatthetīti kappino=rājā. Kama-padavikkhepe, assa uttaṃ, kamanti ettha mīnādayo pavisantīti kuminaṃ=macchabandhanopakaraṇaviseso. Dā-dāne, denti etasminti dinaṃ=divaso, evamaññepi.

Words such as 'vipina' are irregularly formed with the suffix 'ina'. From the root 'vap' in the sense of 'to sow seeds', with 'a' becoming 'i'; because they sow therein (vapanti ettha), it is 'vipinaṃ', meaning 'forest' (vanaṃ). From the root 'sup' in the sense of 'to sleep'; because one sleeps by means of it (supanti etena), it is 'supinaṃ', meaning 'sleep' (niddā), and also that which is seen by one who is sleeping. From the root 'tud' in the sense of 'to hurt', with 'd' becoming 'h'; because it hurts and afflicts beings (tudati satte pīḷeti), it is 'tuhinaṃ', meaning 'frost' (himaṃ). From the root 'kapp' in the sense of 'to be able'; because he is able, that is, competent to conquer his enemies (kappati ripavo vijetuṃ samattho), he is 'kappino', meaning 'a king' (rājā). From the root 'kam' in the sense of 'to step', with 'a' becoming 'u'; because fish and so on step into, that is, enter it (kamanti ettha mīnādayo pavisanti), it is 'kuminaṃ', meaning 'a special kind of fishing implement' (macchabandhanopakaraṇaviseso). From the root 'dā' in the sense of 'to give'; because they give in this (denti etasmiṃ), it is 'dinaṃ', meaning 'day' (divaso). And so with others.

104. Kirā kano.

104. From the root 'kir', the suffix 'kano'.

Kiratismā [M 0.0260] kano hoti. Nassa ṇo, kiranti vikirantīti kiraṇā=raṃsiyo.

From the root 'kir', the suffix 'kano' is used. 'Na' becomes 'ṇa'. Because they scatter and spread out (kiranti vikiranti), they are 'kiraṇā', meaning 'rays' (raṃsiyo).

105. Dī jiimīhi naka.

105. From the roots 'dī', 'ji', 'i', and 'mī', the suffix 'na'.

Dī-khaye, ji-jaye, i-ajjhenagatīsu, mī-hiṃsāyaṃ, etehi naka hoti. Adesi khayamagamāsīti dīno=niddhano. Pañcamāre ajinīti jino=buddho. Esi issarattamagamāsīti ino=sāmī. Mīyate hiṃsīyateti mīno=maccho.

From the roots 'dī' in the sense of 'to decay', 'ji' in the sense of 'to conquer', 'i' in the senses of 'studying' and 'going', and 'mī' in the sense of 'to harm', from these the suffix 'na' is used. Because he has decayed, has gone to destruction (adīyi khayamagamāsi), he is 'dīno', meaning 'impoverished' (niddhano). Because he conquered the five Māras (pañcamāre ajini), he is 'jino', meaning 'the Buddha'. Because he went to, that is, attained lordship (esi issarattamagamāsi), he is 'ino', meaning 'lord' (sāmī). Because it is harmed, that is, killed (mīyate hiṃsīyate), it is 'mīno', meaning 'fish' (maccho).

106. Sidhāvīvāhi no.

106. From the roots 'si', 'dhā', 'vī', and 'vā', the suffix 'no'.

Si-bandhane, dhā-dhāraṇe, vī vā-gamane, etehi no hoti. Seti bandhatīti seno=sasādano senā=camū. Dhāretīti dhānā=bhajjitayavo. Veti pavattatīti veno=hīnajāti. Sattesu vāti pavattatīti vānaṃ=taṇhā.

From the root 'si' in the sense of 'to bind', 'dhā' in the sense of 'to hold', and 'vī' or 'vā' in the sense of 'to go', from these the suffix 'no' is used. Because it binds (seti bandhati), it is 'seno', meaning 'one possessing an army' (sasādano); and 'senā', meaning 'army' (camū). Because it sustains (dhāreti), it is 'dhānā', meaning 'parched barley' (bhajjitayavo). Because he goes about (veti pavattati), he is 'veno', meaning 'one of low birth' (hīnajāti). Because it proceeds among beings (sattesu vāti pavattati), it is 'vānaṃ', meaning 'craving' (taṇhā).

107. Ūnādayo.

107. Words such as ūna.

Ūnaādayo nantā nīpaccante. Ūha-vitakke, halopo, ūhanaṃ ūno=apuṇṇo. Hi-gatiyaṃ, dīghattaṃ, hesi hīnattamagamīti hīno=nihīno. Ci-caye, dīghattaṃ, cayanti ettha ratanānīti cīno=janapado. Hanissa jagho, haññatīti jaghanaṃ=kaṭi. Ṭhāssa the ṭhāti pavattatīti theno=coro. Undissa odo, undīyatīti odano=annaṃ. Annaṃ. Raṃjissa niggahītalopo, aka ca, raṃjate anenāti rajanaṃ=rāgo. Rañjanti etthāti rajanī=ratti. Padissa junuka[M 0.0261], pajjati gacchatīti pajjunno=indo, megho ca. Gamissa gaṅa, gacchanti ettha vihaṅgādayoti gaganaṃ=antalikkhaṃ, evamaññepi.

Words such as 'ūna' are irregularly formed with the suffix 'na'. From the root 'ūh' in the sense of 'to reason', with elision of 'h'; from 'ūhanaṃ' (reasoning) comes 'ūno', meaning 'deficient' (apuṇṇo). From the root 'hi' in the sense of 'to go', with lengthening; because he went to a low state (hesi hīnattamagamī), he is 'hīno', meaning 'inferior' (nihīno). From the root 'ci' in the sense of 'to collect', with lengthening; because jewels are collected here (cayanti ettha ratanāni), it is 'cīno', meaning 'a country' (janapado). Of the root 'han', 'jagh' is the substitute; because it is struck (haññati), it is 'jaghanaṃ', meaning 'the hip' (kaṭi). Of the root 'ṭhā', 'the' is the substitute; because he stands about (ṭhāti pavattati), he is 'theno', meaning 'a thief' (coro). Of the root 'und', 'od' is the substitute; because it is moistened (undīyati), it is 'odano', meaning 'cooked rice' (annaṃ). Of the root 'raṃj', there is elision of the nasal, and the suffix is 'ana'; because one is colored by this (rañjate anena), it is 'rajanaṃ', meaning 'passion' (rāgo). Because they delight therein (rañjanti ettha), it is 'rajanī', meaning 'night' (ratti). Of the root 'pad', 'junna' is the substitute; because he goes (pajjati gacchati), he is 'pajjunno', meaning 'Indra' and also 'a cloud' (megho). Of the root 'gam', 'gaṅa' is the substitute; because birds and so on go here (gacchanti ettha vihaṅgādayo), it is 'gaganaṃ', meaning 'the sky' (antalikkhaṃ). And so with others.

108. Vī patā tano.

108. From the roots 'vī' and 'pata', the suffix 'tano'.

Vī vā-gamane, pata patha-gamane, etehi tano hoti. Veti pavattati etenāti vetanaṃ=bhati. Patanti etthāti pattanaṃ=nagaraṃ.

From the roots 'vī' or 'vā' in the sense of 'to go', and 'pat' or 'path' in the sense of 'to go', from these the suffix 'tano' is used. Because one proceeds by means of this (veti pavattati etena), it is 'vetanaṃ', meaning 'wages' (bhati). Because they alight here (patanti ettha), it is 'pattanaṃ', meaning 'a city' (nagaraṃ).

109. Ramā tanaka.

109. From the root 'ram', the suffix 'tana'.

Rama kīḷāyamicasmā tanaka hoti. “Gamādirānaṃ lopontassā”ti (5.109) malopo, ramanti etthāti ratanaṃ=maṇi ādī, hatthamattañca.

From the root 'ram' in the sense of 'to delight', the suffix 'tana' is used. By the rule 'Gamādirānaṃ lopontassā' (5.109), there is elision of 'm'; because they delight therein (ramanti ettha), it is 'ratanaṃ', meaning 'a jewel, etc.' (maṇi ādi), and also 'a measure of a hand' (hatthamattaṃ).

110., Sū bhāhi nuka,

110. From the roots 'sū' and 'bhā', the suffix 'nu'.

Sū-pasave, bhā-dittiyaṃ, etehi nuka hoti. Pasavīyatīti sūnu=putto. Bhāti dibbatīti bhānu=sūriyo.

From the root 'sū' in the sense of 'to generate' and 'bhā' in the sense of 'to shine', from these the suffix 'nu' is used. Because he is generated (pasavīyati), he is 'sūnu', meaning 'son' (putto). Because it shines and is brilliant (bhāti dibbati), it is 'bhānu', meaning 'the sun' (sūriyo).

111. Dhāsse ca.

111. And of 'dhā', 'e' is the substitute.

Dhā-dhāraṇetīmasmā nuka hoti, dhāssa e ca. Dhāretīti dhenu=gāvī.

From the root 'dhā' in the sense of 'to give suck', the suffix 'nu' is used, and 'e' is the substitute for 'dhā'. Because she gives suck (dhāreti), she is 'dhenu', meaning 'a cow' (gāvī).

112. Vattā ṭāva dhamāsehyani.

112. From the roots 'vatt', 'aṭ', 'av', 'dham', and 'as', the suffix 'ani'.

Vatta-vattane, aṭa-gamanattho, ava-rakkhaṇe, dhama-sadde, asa-khepane, etehi ani hoti. Vattanti etenāti vattani=tasaradaṇḍaṃ. Vīmhi vattanī=pantho. Aṭate gammateti aṭani= mañcaṅgo[M 0.0262]. Satte avati rakkhatīti avani=mahī. Dhamanti etena vīṇādayoti dhamani=sīrā. Daṇḍatthāya asīyate khipīyateti asani=kulisaṃ.

From the root 'vatt' in the sense of 'to turn', 'aṭ' in the sense of 'to go', 'av' in the sense of 'to protect', 'dham' in the sense of 'to sound', and 'as' in the sense of 'to throw', from these the suffix 'ani' is used. Because one turns by means of it (vattanti etena), it is 'vattani', meaning 'a spindle-stick' (tasaradaṇḍaṃ). In the feminine, 'vattanī' means 'a path' (pantho). Because one goes on it (aṭate gammate), it is 'aṭani', meaning 'a part of a bed' (mañcaṅgo). Because it protects beings (satte avati rakkhati), it is 'avani', meaning 'the earth' (mahī). Because lutes and so on are sounded by means of it (dhamanti etena vīṇādayo), it is 'dhamani', meaning 'a vein' (sīrā). Because it is thrown for the purpose of punishment (daṇḍatthāya asīyate khipīyate), it is 'asani', meaning 'a thunderbolt' (kulisaṃ).

113. Yuto ni.

113. From the root 'yu', the suffix 'ni'.

Yu-missanetīmasmā ni hoti. Yavanti sattā anena etībhāvaṃ gacchantīti yoni=bhagaṃ, aṇḍajādiyoni ca.

From the root 'yu' in the sense of 'to mix', the suffix 'ni' is used. Because beings, by means of this, go to existence (yavanti sattā anena etībhāvaṃ gacchanti), it is 'yoni', meaning 'vulva' (bhagaṃ), and also the origin of the egg-born and so on.

(Iti tavaggapaccayavidhānaṃ).

(Thus ends the section on suffixes of the 'ta' group).

114. Camāpa pā vapā po.

114. From cam, ap, pā, and vap, the suffix po is derived.

Cama-adane, apa-pāpuṇane, pā-rakkhaṇe, vapa-bījanikkhepe, etehi po hoti. Camanti adanti etthāti campā=nagaraṃ, apesi īsakamattamagamāsīti appaṃ=abahu. Apāyaṃ pāti rakkhatīti pāpaṃ-kibbisaṃ. Vapanti etthāti vappo=kedāraṃ.

From the root cam in the sense of eating, ap in reaching, pā in protecting, and vap in sowing seeds, the suffix po is derived. 'They eat in it,' thus campā means a city. 'It went a small distance,' thus appaṃ means little, not much. 'It protects from a state of loss,' thus pāpaṃ means evil, a sin. 'They sow in it,' thus vappo means a field, cultivated land.

115. Yu thu kūnaṃ dīgho ca.

115. From yu, thu, and kū, and their vowels are lengthened.

Yu-missane, thu-abhitthave, ku-sadde, etehi po hoti, etesaṃ dīgho ca. Dīghavidhānasāmatthiyā ottābhāvo. Yavanti saha vattanti etthāti yūpo=yaññayaṭṭhi, pāsādo ca. Thavīyatīti thūpo=cetiyaṃ. Kavanti nadanti etthāti kūpo=udapāno.

From the root yu in the sense of mixing, thu in praising, and ku in sounding, the suffix po is derived, and the vowels of these roots are lengthened. Due to the provision for lengthening, the vowel o is not substituted. 'They are mixed together in it,' thus yūpo means a sacrificial post, and also a palace. 'It is praised,' thus thūpo means a stupa, a shrine. 'They make a sound in it,' thus kūpo means a well.

116. Khipa supa nīsū pūhi paka.

116. From khip, sup, nī, sū, and pū, the suffix paka is derived.

Khipa-peraṇe, supa-saye, nī-naye, sū-pasave, pū-pavane, etehi paka hoti. Khapati khayaṃ gacchatīti khippaṃ=sīghaṃ. Supanti [M 0.0263] ettha sunakhādayoti suppaṃ=papphoṭanaṃ. Nayanti etasmā phalanti nipo=rakkho. Savati ruciṃ janetīti sūpo=byañjanaviseso. Pavīyati maricajīrakādīhi pavittaṃ karīyatīti pūpaṃ=khajjakaṃ.

From the root khipa in the sense of sending, supa in sleeping, nī in leading, sū in producing, and pū in purifying, the suffix paka is derived. 'It perishes, it goes to destruction,' thus khippaṃ means swift. 'Dogs and so on sleep in it,' thus suppaṃ means a winnowing basket. 'Fruits are led from it,' thus nīpo means a tree. 'It produces relish,' thus sūpo means a particular kind of curry. 'It is purified, made clean with pepper, cumin, and so on,' thus pūpaṃ means a cake.

117. Sippādayo.

117. Words such as sippa.

Sippaādayo pakaantā nipaccante. Sapissa assaittaṃ, sapati anenāti sippaṃ=kalā. Vapissa assi, vijjaṃ vapatīti vippo=brāhmaṇo. Vassa bo, vapati bahi nikkhamati hadayaṅgatasokenāti bappaṃ=assu. Chupa-samphasse, usse, chupati anenāti cheppaṃ=naṅguṭṭhaṃ. Rupa=ruppane, palopa dīghā, ruppati vikāramāpajjatīti rūpaṃ-bhūtabhūtikaṃ, evamaññepi.

Words such as sippa, ending in paka, are irregularly formed. For the root sap, its a becomes i: 'one is connected by it,' thus sippaṃ is art. For the root vap, its a becomes i: 'he sows knowledge,' thus vippo is a brahmin. For vap, va becomes ba: 'it is shed, it comes out due to sorrow in the heart,' thus bappaṃ is a tear. From the root chup in the sense of touching, its u becomes e: 'it touches with this,' thus cheppaṃ is a tail. From the root rup in the sense of being afflicted, with elision of p and lengthening of the vowel: 'it is afflicted, it undergoes alteration,' thus rūpaṃ is material form and its derivatives. Similarly for others.

118. Sāsā apo.

118. From the root sās, the suffix apa is derived.

Sāsa anusiṭṭhiyamiccasmā apo hoti. Sāsīyanti etenāti sāsapo=vīhiviseso.

From the root sās in the sense of 'instructing,' the suffix apa is derived. 'One is instructed by it,' thus sāsapo means a particular kind of grain, i.e., a mustard seed.

119. Viṭapādayo.

119. Words such as viṭapa.

Viṭapaādayo apantā nipaccante. Vaṭa-veṭṭhane, assa ittaṃ, vaṭati veṭṭhati etenātiviṭapo=gumbaviseso, kutha-pūtibhāve, thassa ṇo, akuthi pūtibhāvamagamīti kuṇapo=matako. Maṇḍa=bhūsane, maṇḍeti janaṃ, maṇḍīyati janehīti vā maṇḍapo=janālayo, evamaññepi.

Words such as viṭapa, ending in the suffix apa, are irregularly formed. From the root vaṭa in the sense of surrounding, its a becomes i: 'it surrounds with this,' thus viṭapo means a particular kind of thicket. From the root kutha in the sense of putrefying, its th becomes ṇ: 'it putrefied, it went to a state of foulness,' thus kuṇapo means a corpse. From the root maṇḍa in the sense of adorning: 'it adorns people,' or 'it is adorned by people,' thus maṇḍapo means a hall for people. Similarly for others.

120. Gupā pho.

120. From the root gup, the suffix pha is derived.

Gupismā pho hoti. Gopīyatīti goppho=caraṇagaṇṭhi.

From the root gup, the suffix pha is derived. 'It is protected,' thus goppho means the ankle.

121. Garasarādīhi bo.

121. From the roots gar, sar, and so on, the suffix ba is derived.

Garasarādīhi [M 0.0264] bo hoti. Garati aññe anena pīḷetīti gabbo=abhimāno. Sarati pavattatīti sabbo=sakalo. Phalakāmehi janehi amīyati gamīyatīti ambo=cūto. Puttena amīyati gamīyatīti ambā=mātā.

From the roots gar, sar, and so on, the suffix ba is derived. 'He despises, he oppresses others with this,' thus gabbo means arrogance. 'It proceeds, it occurs,' thus sabbo means all. 'It is approached, gone to by people desiring fruit,' thus ambo means a mango tree. 'She is approached, gone to by her son,' thus ambā means mother.

122. Nimbādayo.

122. Words such as nimba.

Nimbaādayo bantā nipaccante. Namissa assi, namati phalabhārenāti nimbo=ariṭṭho. Vamissa vassa bittaṃ. Pittādayo vamati uggiratīti bimbaṃ=sarīraṃ. Kusissa amuka, tittena kusīyati akkosīyatīti kosambo=rukkho. Kadatissa amuka, kadanti etena dvārādīnīti kadambo=rukkho. Kuṭissa umuka, janehi koṭīyati pavattīyatīti kuṭumbaṃ=catuppado, khettaṃ, gharaṃ, kalattaṃ, dāsā ca. Kaṇḍissa kuḍu. Taṇḍulādayo anena kaṇḍanti paricchindantīti kuḍubo=mānaṃ, evamaññepi.

Words such as nimba, ending in the suffix ba, are irregularly formed. For the root nam, its a becomes i: 'it bends with the weight of its fruit,' thus nimbo is the Nimba tree. For the root vam, va becomes bi: 'it emits bile and so on,' thus bimbaṃ is the body. For the root kus, with the suffix amba: 'it is reviled because of its bitterness,' thus kosambo is the Kosamba tree. For the root kad, with the suffix amba: 'they mark boundaries, doors, and so on with it,' thus kadambo is the Kadamba tree. For the root kuṭ, with the suffix umba: 'it is managed by people,' thus kuṭumbaṃ is a quadruped, a field, a house, a wife, and slaves. For the root kaṇḍ, the substitution is kuḍu: 'rice grains and so on are pounded or divided by this,' thus kuḍubo is a measure. Similarly for others.

123. Darā bi.

123. From the root dar, the suffix bi is derived.

Dara vidāraṇetīmasmā bi hoti. Odanādīni dārenti jatāyāti dabbi=kaṭacchu, vīmhi dabbī.

From the root dar in the sense of 'splitting,' the suffix bi is derived. 'It splits rice and so on,' thus dabbi means a ladle; in the feminine, dabbī.

124. Kara sara sala kala valla vasā abho.

124. From the roots kar, sar, sal, kal, val/vall, and vas, the suffix abha is derived.

Kara-karaṇe, sara-gati hiṃsācintāsu, sala-gamanattho, kala-saṅkhyāne, vala valla-saṃvaraṇe, vasa-nivāse, etehi abho hoti. Karotīti karabho=oṭṭhā, pāṇippadeso ca. Sarati gacchatīti sarabho=migaviseso. Salati gacchatīti salabho=paṭaṅgo[M 0.0265]. Kalīyati parimīyati vayasāti kalabho=hatthipotako. Tadaminādipāṭhā ḷatte kaḷabho=sova. Valleti saṃvaraṇaṃ karotīti vallabho=piyo. Vasantyanenāti vasabho=puṅgavo.

From the roots kar in the sense of doing; sar in going, harming, and thinking; sal in the sense of going; kal in counting; val and vall in covering; and vas in dwelling, the suffix abha is derived. 'It does,' thus karabho means a lip and also a part of the hand. 'It moves, it goes,' thus sarabho means a particular kind of deer. 'It moves, it goes,' thus salabho means a moth. 'It is counted or measured by age,' thus kalabho means a young elephant. In another reading, with ḷ, kaḷabho means a parrot. 'It covers, makes a covering,' thus vallabho means a favorite. 'They dwell by means of it,' thus vasabho means a bull.

125. Gadā rabho.

125. From the root gad, the suffix rabha is derived.

Gadatismā rabho hoti. Gadatīti gadrabho=kharo.

From the root gad, the suffix rabha is derived. 'It brays,' thus gadrabho means a donkey.

126. Usarāsā kabho.

126. From the roots us and rās, the suffix kabha is derived.

Usa-dāhe, rāsa-sadde, etehi kabho hoti. Usati paṭipakkhe dahatīti usabho=seṭṭho. Rāsati nadatīti rāsabho=gadrabho.

From the root us in the sense of burning and rās in the sense of sounding, the suffix kabha is derived. 'It burns, it burns up opponents,' thus usabho means a bull, the best. 'It sounds, it brays,' thus rāsabho means a donkey.

127. Ito bhaka.

127. From the root i, the suffix bhaka is derived.

I itismā bhaka hoti. Eti gacchatīti ibho=hatthī.

From the root i, the suffix bhaka is derived. 'It goes,' thus ibho means an elephant.

128. Garāvā bho.

128. From the roots gar and av, the suffix bha is derived.

Gara ghara-secane, ava-rakkhane, etehi bho hoti. Garati bahi nikkhamanavasena siñcatīti gabbho=pasavo, ovarako ca. Avati satte rakkhatīti abbhaṃ=megho.

From the roots gar or ghar in the sense of sprinkling, and av in the sense of protecting, the suffix bha is derived. 'It emits, it sprinkles by way of coming out,' thus gabbho means a womb and also an inner chamber. 'It protects beings,' thus abbhaṃ means a cloud.

129. Sobbhādayo.

129. Words such as sobbha.

Sobbhaādayo bhantā nipaccante. Sadatissa assa ottaṃ, sīdanti etthāti sobbhaṃ=vivaraṃ, sobbho=jalāsayaviseso. Kamissa assu, kāmīyatīti kumbho=dasambaṇamatto, ghaṭo [M 0.0266] ca. (Kena jalena umbhīyati pūrīyatīti vā kumbho=ghaṭo.) Kusissa umuka, kusati avhāyatīti kusumbhaṃ=mahārajanaṃ. Kusumbho=kanakaṃ, evamaññepi.

Words such as sobbha, ending in bha, are irregularly formed. For the root sad, its a becomes o: 'they sink in it,' thus sobbhaṃ means a chasm, and sobbho means a particular kind of reservoir. For the root kam, its a becomes u: 'it is desired,' thus kumbho means a measure of ten ambaṇas, and also a pot. (Or, 'it is filled with water,' thus kumbho means a pot.) For the root kus, with the suffix umbha: 'it shines,' thus kusumbhaṃ means safflower dye. Kusumbho also means gold. Similarly for others.

130. Usa kusa pada sukhā kumo.

130. From the roots us, kus, pad, and sukh, the suffix kuma is derived.

Usādīhi kumo hoti. Usati dahatīti usumaṃ=uṇhaṃ. Kusati avhāyatīti sukumaṃ=pupphaṃ. Pajjati devapūjādiṃ yātīti padumaṃ=paṅkajaṃ. Sukhayatīti sukhuma=aṇu.

From the roots us and so on, the suffix kuma is derived. 'It burns,' thus usumaṃ means heat. 'It is attractive,' thus sukumaṃ means a flower. 'It goes to the worship of gods and so on,' thus padumaṃ means a lotus. 'It gives pleasure,' thus sukhuma means subtle.

131. Vaṭumādayo.

131. Words such as vaṭuma.

Vaṭumaādayo kumantā nipaccanthe. Vajissa-ntassa ṭo, vajanti etthāti vaṭumaṃ=patho. Silisassa lisse, silissatīti silesupaṃ=semhaṃ. Kamissa kuṅkādeso, kāmīyatīti kuṅkamaṃ=kasmīrajaṃ, evamaññepi.

Words such as vaṭuma, ending in the suffix kuma, are irregularly formed. For the root vaj, its final consonant becomes ṭ: 'they go on it,' thus vaṭumaṃ means a path. For the root silis, the substitution is lesu: 'it adheres,' thus silesumaṃ means phlegm. For the root kam, the substitution is kuṅka: 'it is desired,' thus kuṅkamaṃ means saffron. Similarly for others.

132. Gudhā umo.

132. From the root gudh, the suffix uma is derived.

Gudha pariveṭṭhanetīmasmā umo hoti. Gudhati pariveṭṭhatīti godhumo=dhaññaviseso.

From the root gudh in the sense of 'enveloping,' the suffix uma is derived. 'It envelops, it covers,' thus godhumo means a particular kind of grain (wheat).

133. Paṭha carā amimā.

133. From the roots paṭh and car, the suffixes ama and ima are derived respectively.

Paṭhaticaratismā ama imā honti yathākkamaṃ. Paṭṭhīyati uccārīyati uttamabhāvenāti paṭhamaṃ=seṭṭhaṃ. Carati hīnattaṃ yātīti carimaṃ=pacchimaṃ.

From the roots paṭh and car, the suffixes ama and ima are derived respectively. 'It is read, uttered as the highest,' thus paṭhamaṃ means first, best. 'It moves, it goes to an inferior state,' thus carimaṃ means last.

134. Hidhūhi maka.

134. From the roots hi and dhū, the suffix ma is derived.

Hi-gatiyaṃ[M 0.0267], dhū-kampane, etehi maka hoti. Hinoti pavattahīti himaṃ=tuhinaṃ. Dhunāti kampatīti dhūmo=aggipasavo.
